title: Statkraft, SSE complete first swap tied to battery storage revenue index - Energy Storage
content: Norwegian energy company Statkraft and UK power group SSE have completed what the companies describe as the first financial swap of its kind, based on Modo Energy’s ME BESS GB (2H) Index, a benchmark that tracks average revenue earned by operational two-hour battery energy storage systems (BESS) in Great Britain. In practical terms, the deal lets SSE trade uncertain revenue from part of its battery storage portfolio for a fixed, predictable amount, while Statkraft takes on the risk and potential upside of how the benchmark battery-revenue index performs relative to the agreed strike level. Under the swap, Statkraft will pay SSE if the index value falls below an agreed strike level, and SSE will pay Statkraft if the index value rises above it. The swap is settled against the index itself, not the specific performance of either company’s own battery assets. For example, if the agreed strike level were GBP 70,000 ($94,290)/MW/year and the index came in at GBP 50,000, Statkraft would pay SSE the GBP 20,000 difference; if the index came in at GBP 90,000 instead, SSE would pay Statkraft the difference. The Modo Energy index measures the average revenue earned per megawatt by a pool of qualifying, operational two-hour batteries in Great Britain – batteries whose energy storage capacity is roughly double their power rating, such as a 50 MW/100 MWh system. Unlike simpler hedging tools that model only the gap between high and low wholesale electricity prices, the index captures the main publicly observable battery revenue streams, including wholesale trading, Great Britain’s balancing mechanism, frequency-response and reserve services, and the capacity market. Modo Energy said the broader revenue coverage can reduce basis risk: in one comparison provided by the company, a battery’s actual revenue diverged from the index by an average of about GBP 5,700/MW annually, versus roughly GBP 29,500/MW annually when measured against a simpler wholesale-price-spread benchmark. The index is FCA-regulated, meaning its administrator and methodology meet UK financial regulatory standards for benchmarks used in financial contracts, giving banks, insurers and trading counterparties a more standardized reference point for pricing battery-linked derivatives. Statkraft and SSE did not disclose the swap’s size, strike level, duration or other commercial terms. Duncan Dale, Statkraft’s head of origination for the United Kingdom and Ireland, said the deal reflects growing use of financial tools that let battery owners manage risk by locking in revenue when prices are considered high, and that Statkraft expects to pursue more such transactions across its 9,000 MW portfolio. Gordon Bell, managing director of SSE Energy Markets, said the transaction shows the growing maturity of battery storage as an asset class and provides a new way for market participants to manage exposure to battery revenue. Quentin Scrimshire, CEO and co-founder of Modo Energy, said the swap signals that battery storage has matured to the point where it can be hedged and valued using tools common in established financial markets, adding that he expects more such deals to follow. Statkraft’s European battery portfolio , which underpins deals like this swap, spanned eight operational or under-construction assets across the United Kingdom, Ireland and Germany as of May 2025, according to the company. Modo Energy, the London-based analytics platform behind the index used in the swap, raised $15 million in late 2023 to expand its subscription-based revenue and performance data platform, and has since built out benchmark indices across 13 global markets. title: Kia's new PV7 EV van shows up in the US [Image]
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 15 2026 - 8:35 am PT
Shortly after
officially unveiled the PV7, the new electric van was spotted testing in the US.
Is Kia launching the PV7 EV van in the US?
took the covers off the PV7
at IAA Transportation on Monday, the second electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) lineup.
The PV7 is considerably bigger than the PV5, measuring over 17.5 feet (5,350 mm) long, or about 2 feet longer than the PV5 (4,695 mm in length).
Like its first electric van, Kia will offer several PV7 variants, starting with the Passenger and Cargo models.
The PV7 will be available with 71.5 kWh and 96.2 kWh nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) battery packs. Kia said the Long Range Cargo variant will offer a WLTP range of over 285 miles (460 km).
Front-wheel drive (FWD) will come as standard, but Kia plans to add an all-wheel drive (AWD) variant to the lineup. Depending on the configuration, the FWD powertrain delivers up to 268 horsepower (200 kW) and 309 lb-ft (420 Nm) of torque.
Kia PV7 Cargo (left) and Passenger (right) Source: Kia)
It also uses an 800V electrical architecture, enabling it to charge from 10% to 80% in about 25 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.
The PV7 Cargo (shown below) is designed for delivery, logistics, and other business uses. It’s available in 2- and 3-seat configurations and offers up to 6.1 cubic meters of cargo space. The High Roof variant offers even more, with up to 8 cubic meters.
The Passenger version (shown below), on the other hand, is designed for families or as a shuttle with space for up to nine passengers. In Korea, it will be available as an 11-seater.
Following the Passenger and Cargo models, Kia plans to launch 23 PV7 variants in total. Will the US see any of them?
The same day Kia unveiled the PV7, the electric van was spotted testing in the US. The image from
KindelAuto
shows a disguised prototype during hot-weather testing.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by KindelAuto (@kindelauto)
Kia plans to launch the PV7 in Korea and Europe in the second half of 2027. After that, Kia said “additional markets, derivatives, and conversion models” will follow, but didn’t offer any specifics.
Electrek’s Take
While we are pulling for Kia to bring the electric van to the US, don’t get too excited. The PV5 was caught testing in the US several times, raising speculation that it would eventually go on sale. However, it still hasn’t.
The PV7 could find a market in the US as a larger alternative, but it’s still unlikely that Kia will bring it to the States.
For one, Kia builds the electric vans at a dedicated plant in South Korea, meaning they would be subject to the Trump Administration’s import tax.
Kia’s president and CEO, Ho Sung Song, also told reporters that it chose Hanover, Germany, to reveal the PV7 because it’s aimed at the heart of Europe’s light commercial vehicle segment as a bigger sibling to the PV5.

title: NYC’s newest electric school buses come with a money-saving twist
content:
EV Chargers
New York
Electric school buses
Michelle Lewis
| Sep 15 2026 - 8:00 am PT
Photo: First Student
First Student is adding 40 electric school buses in New York City after completing the first phase of a charging project that cut infrastructure costs by 20%.
The electric school buses will serve NYC Public Schools in Brooklyn and Queens, building on a demonstration project with Con Edison that tested a less disruptive way to install charging equipment in a dense urban environment.
At the center of the project is First Charge, First Student’s above-ground charging system. Instead of digging trenches to bury electrical cables, the equipment carries them overhead, cutting construction costs and making installations faster and less disruptive. Here’s how First Charge works:
“Eliminating the need to bury the service line to these chargers lowers the upfront costs for First Student and is a strategy that other fleet owners can replicate to save money and complete projects more quickly,” said Vicki Kuo, senior vice president of Customer Energy Solutions at Con Edison.
That could be especially useful in cities like New York, where digging up paved bus yards can be expensive and complicated.
Con Edison and the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) helped fund the demonstration project. The funding included six electric school bus vouchers awarded through NYSERDA’s New York School Bus Incentive Program, plus support for four buses converted from diesel to electric.
The project is also using load-management software to charge buses during off-peak hours, when electricity is generally cheaper. For a large school bus fleet, coordinating charging times can help control energy costs and reduce pressure on the grid.
“Deploying electric school buses at scale requires more than vehicles; it requires the right infrastructure, technology, and utility partnership,” said Kevin Matthews, head of electrification at First Student. “Working with Con Edison, we’ve demonstrated a more efficient approach that can help overcome some of the cost and construction challenges that have traditionally made fleet electrification difficult in dense urban environments.”
First Student is considering more clean-energy upgrades at its Brooklyn facilities, including solar and a smart energy hub.
New York State mandated that all new school buses purchased by 2027 must be zero-emission and all school buses on the road must be zero-emission by 2035.

title: Segway’s new 28 MPH MUXI Pro cargo e-bike gets automatic shifting and regen braking
content:
Micah Toll
| Sep 15 2026 - 6:00 am PT
Segway is giving its compact MUXI utility e-bike a fairly significant upgrade, adding everything from automatic electronic shifting to front suspension and a higher Class 3 top speed.
The new Segway MUXI Pro builds on the company’s existing short-tail cargo e-bike platform,
launched earlier this year
as part of Segway’s continued expansion into the electric bike industry.
The design retains the distinctive swooping step-through frame while packing in a number of features that should make it more capable as an
everyday car-replacement-style e-bike.
Perhaps the most interesting upgrade is the new 9-speed electronic drivetrain with automatic shifting.
Besides saving riders from having to think about shifting, the wider drivetrain also helps the MUXI Pro reach a pedal-assisted top speed of 28 mph (45 km/h). Riders can select between Class 1, 2, and 3 operation through the Segway app, subject of course to local regulations.
As such regulations continue to shift and fragment in cities and states around the US in absence of a single federal standard, riders are reminded to check their local laws.
Power comes from a 750W direct-drive rear motor producing 80 Nm of torque, paired with a 716Wh battery. Segway claims up to 73 miles (117 km) of range, though as usual, expect real-world range to vary considerably based on assist level, terrain, rider weight, and riding conditions.
That direct-drive motor also enables regenerative braking and Hill Descent Control (basically like engine braking on an ICE vehicle, where the bike won’t simply continue accelerating due to gravity), while Hill-Start Assist helps prevent the bike from rolling backward on inclines. There’s even traction control designed to detect rear wheelspin.
Another major improvement is the addition of a 70mm front suspension fork, addressing one of the limitations of many rigid utility bikes. Hydraulic disc brakes with 180mm rotors handle stopping duties, while the bike rolls on chunky 20×3-inch tires. Front and rear fenders are now standard equipment, as are turn signals integrated into the lighting system.
Don’t forget thought that this is still very much a utility bike. The MUXI Pro is rated for a hefty 418 lb (190 kg) total payload, and Segway offers an optional passenger kit rated for passengers up to 120 lb (54 kg). Front and center baskets are also available.
Segway has loaded the bike with its increasingly expansive suite of smart features, too, including Apple Find My, GPS tracking, proximity-based AirLock, Lost Mode, OTA updates, and a color TFT display with navigation. Some connected features require a subscription after the first year, as is common for GPS and data-connected services.
At 82.2 lb (37.3 kg), the MUXI Pro certainly isn’t a lightweight e-bike, but that’s not really the point here. It’s a compact cargo bike designed to carry people and stuff without growing into the footprint of a full-size long-tail.
The Segway MUXI Pro will be available in Anthracite and Reef Blue, priced at $1,999.99. US sales are scheduled to begin September 22 through Segway dealers and the c
ompany’s online store.

title: Stark turns its 80 hp electric supermoto into a titanium-loaded blacked-out beast
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Micah Toll
| Sep 15 2026 - 6:33 am PT
Stark Future has already turned its ridiculously powerful electric dirt bike into a street-going supermoto – upon which I recently got to cruise the streets and cities around Barcelona (more on that experience coming soon). But now the company is taking that concept in an even darker direction with the new Stark VARG SM Sköll, a limited-edition, nearly completely blacked-out version of the 80 hp electric supermoto.
And when I say limited, I mean it.
says it will build just 500 numbered examples worldwide, with no second production run planned. And based on
the rate that Stark is selling bikes
, those 500 units aren’t likely to stick around very long.
The name comes from Norse mythology, where Sköll is the wolf that hunts the sun across the sky, eventually destined to catch and devour it. That explains both the name and the rather extreme commitment to blacking out seemingly everything Stark could get its hands on.
Based on the existing VARG SM, the Sköll gets Stark’s full ALPHA specification with 80 hp of peak power as well as tunable Dynamic Traction Control. The underlying bike remains largely unchanged, including the structural 7.2 kWh battery pack, single-speed drivetrain, chassis architecture, and carbon-fiber-sleeved motor with integrated inverter.
But Stark didn’t simply spray a VARG SM black and call it a day. That blackout comes from manufacturing changes, not black airbrushing.
The company says essentially every eligible component received some form of black treatment through anodizing, powder coating, or other finishing processes. That includes the upper and lower triple clamps, steering stem, swingarm, motor housing, inverter casing, charging port cap, docking station, and even the handlebar map switch.
The black anodized triple clamps also receive individual limited-edition engraving.
There is one conspicuous exception to all that darkness: the 520 RK MXU chain retains its gold finish, contrasting against a black 7075 T6 rear sprocket.
Stark also put the Sköll on a bit of a diet.
New 3D-printed titanium footpegs save 140 grams compared to the standard parts, while a complete titanium bolt kit cuts another 900 grams. Together, that trims 1.1 kg (2.4 lb) from the bike, bringing the claimed weight down from 124.5 kg (274.5 lb) for the standard VARG SM to 123.4 kg (272 lb).
That makes the Sköll the lightest VARG SM Stark has produced.
Admittedly, replacing nearly a kilogram’s worth of bolts with titanium probably sits pretty high on the diminishing-returns end of the weight-saving spectrum. But after personally seeing the collection of room-sized titanium 3D printers at Stark’s production facility recently, that’s also exactly the sort of unnecessary excess I’d expect from their 500-unit special edition of an 80 hp electric supermoto.
And considering the VARG platform’s already absurd power-to-weight ratio, shaving off another couple of pounds certainly isn’t going to hurt. The crazy experience is only going to get a bit crazier.
The Stark VARG SM Sköll’ 500 units will start with their first deliveries scheduled for October 2026.
For anyone who looked at the regular VARG SM and thought, “This is great, but it needs more titanium and less color,” it looks like your motorcycle has just arrived.

title: Tesla's record month: 4 fatal Autopilot and Full Self-Driving crashes
content:
Tesla Autopilot
Tesla Full self-Driving
Fred Lambert
| Sep 15 2026 - 7:05 am PT
July 2026 was the worst month on record for Tesla driver-assist crashes. Tesla reported
of them to federal regulators, the most it has ever filed in a single month.
Four of those crashes killed someone. In every one, Tesla’s own data says Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, and in every one, the public was never told the system was involved. This is the latest from our
ongoing investigation
matching Tesla’s redacted NHTSA reports to real, named crashes.
A record month, and a rising line
Under a 2021 NHTSA Standing General Order, automakers must report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact. Tesla’s monthly count has climbed all year, from 135 in March to 207 in May to 209 in June. July’s 236 is a new high.
Seven deaths, four sealed reports
Each of these appears in Tesla’s July filings, each marked
“Verified Engaged”
— meaning Tesla confirmed through its telematics that the system was on. And on each one, Tesla redacted the three fields that would explain the crash: the narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating area.
Electrek
, we matched the non-redacted facts about each crash to public reports to better understand each one, since Tesla is trying to limit the information.
Upper Marlboro, Maryland.
Around 12:45 a.m. on July 12, a Tesla Model 3 making a left turn onto Governor’s Park Lane off Route 301 failed to yield to a Harley-Davidson going straight, Maryland State Police said. Three people died: the motorcyclist, Matthew Vowell, 48; his passenger, Krystal Vowell, 47; and a passenger inside the Tesla, Adriana Maxwell, 22. The Tesla was operating as a rideshare. Tesla’s report logs a left turn at 20 mph, driver-assist verified engaged, and says it holds the video. An unprotected left turn across oncoming traffic is a City-Streets maneuver, the kind of thing FSD does and basic Autopilot cannot, the same failure mode as the
Batavia crash we documented
San Mateo, California.
On July 15, a 2016 Tesla Model S left the road, struck a light pole, and caught fire, killing its driver. Tesla’s report: driver-assist verified engaged, 52 mph, a solo strike of a fixed object. It’s a road departure, the single most common crash type in Tesla’s entire driver-assist file.
Ione, California.
Around 7:18 a.m. on July 22, a Tesla heading north on Highway 104 crossed into the southbound lane, sideswiped a Honda, and hit a Cadillac head-on, according to the California Highway Patrol. The Tesla’s driver, Shelby Waldie, 25, was killed; a 2-year-old in the car was hospitalized. Investigators said the reason it crossed the center line is under investigation. Tesla’s report: a brand-new 2026 Model Y, verified engaged, 54 mph. The reason it crossed is the redacted narrative.
Ashby, Minnesota.
Around 3:57 p.m. on July 20, on Interstate 94 in a work zone, a westbound Ford collided with an eastbound Tesla, and a third vehicle then struck them, the Minnesota State Patrol said. Two people died: the Tesla’s driver, Harold Ennulat, 73, and the Ford’s driver, 24. Here, the police made it sound like the Ford was going the wrong way, so the engaged Tesla was likely not to blame. But Tesla’s data still shows the system on at 50 mph, and Tesla holds the EDR and the video.
None of the four was reported publicly as involving Autopilot or FSD. In each, the only reason anyone can connect the death to a driver-assist system is that Tesla had to file a report, which it then redacted.
Tesla’s own count is low
There’s a second problem buried in these filings. Tesla’s report lists a single “highest injury severity.” In Upper Marlboro, three people died, and in Ashby, two did, yet each report records one fatality. Tesla’s federal filings undercount the dead in its driver-assist crashes, which means every aggregate built from this data, including safety comparisons Tesla itself points to, starts low.
Why the redaction matters
Almost no other automaker does this. GM runs a comparable connected-fleet system in Super Cruise and redacts none of its crash narratives. Across the current file, Tesla hides the narrative on 100% of its reports; GM, 0%.
This is the heart of the
investigation
. Tesla is, more than ever, pushing owners to treat a Level 2 driver-assistance system as if it drives itself, selling the software as “Full Self-Driving” while the human stays legally responsible at all times. Then it seals the records that would show how the system behaves when things go wrong, telling regulators it would
“suffer financial harm”
if the public saw them. A motorcyclist, a rideshare passenger, a 25-year-old with her toddler in the car, a 73-year-old man: four people dead in one month, in cars Tesla’s own data says were driving themselves, and not one of those reports says what the car did.
Electrek’s Take
We’ve now matched more than a dozen of these, one by one, from
, and July made the point in a single month: as the crash count climbs to record highs, the fatal cases keep surfacing in Tesla’s data and staying out of the public record. Some of these deaths, like the Minnesota one, may not be Tesla’s fault at all. That’s exactly why the narratives should be open, because right now no one outside Tesla can tell the difference between a crash the system caused and one it didn’t.
We’re careful about the claim. A system being engaged within 30 seconds of a crash doesn’t prove it caused the crash, and the redacted software field means we can’t even separate Autopilot from FSD. But that uncertainty is Tesla’s doing. It has the data, it filed the reports, and it decided that what its cars did in four fatal crashes is a trade secret. Tesla is already
under NHTSA investigation
over how it reports these crashes. Until the narratives open up, we’ll keep matching them.
Even in the Minnesota crash, which I conceded might not sound like Tesla is at fault, the data and crash narrative might still be useful. Maybe the driver was on FSD, not paying attention, and could have avoided or mitigated the crash if they were.

title: The world's largest EV company just partnered with an African electric motorcycle company
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Micah Toll
| Sep 15 2026 - 8:15 am PT
Africa’s electric motorcycle market is about to get an interesting new combination of Chinese manufacturing scale and homegrown battery-swapping infrastructure.
Yadea, the Chinese electric two-wheeler giant that has sold more than 100 million vehicles globally, has announced a new strategic partnership with African electric mobility company Spiro. The two companies plan to work together on electric motorcycles and scooters specifically tailored to African markets while integrating those vehicles into Spiro’s rapidly growing battery-swapping network.
And this isn’t exactly a small pilot project.
says it already has more than 130,000 electric motorcycles operating across seven African countries, supported by over 2,500 battery-swapping stations. The company claims its riders have completed more than 50 million battery swaps and traveled over two billion kilometers.
Now Yadea’s considerable manufacturing muscle is being added to that ecosystem. As the
world’s largest EV company by unit sales
, Yadea knows a thing or two about manufacturing vehicles at scale.
Under the new agreement, Yadea will supply electric two-wheelers and other EV products for Spiro’s markets, while Spiro will integrate those vehicles into its existing swapping and energy infrastructure.
Perhaps more interestingly, the companies say they will jointly develop customized electric two-wheelers designed specifically for African markets. That means adapting the vehicles for local road conditions as well as the heavy commercial use common among motorcycle taxi riders, delivery workers, and other high-mileage operators.
Two-wheelers already serve as essential transportation and commercial tools across much of the African continent. High daily mileage also means the operating-cost savings of switching from gasoline to electricity can add up quickly.
Battery swapping solves another major piece of that puzzle. Instead of asking riders to stop working for hours while charging a motorcycle, depleted batteries can simply be exchanged for charged packs in minutes.
Spiro has been building
that type of infrastructure precisely
, while also expanding regional manufacturing and assembly operations in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria, and Rwanda.
Yadea brings a very different kind of scale to the partnership. Founded in China in 2001, the company says it now operates in more than 100 countries, has 10 production facilities, over 40,000 retail locations, and more than 2,000 patents related to electric vehicle technology.
Spiro, meanwhile, recently raised another $270 million as it works to expand its electric motorcycle and battery-swapping operations.
Put those two pieces together and this partnership could become much more significant than simply another electric motorcycle distribution agreement. Yadea knows how to manufacture electric two-wheelers by the millions, while Spiro has spent years figuring out the considerably harder question of how to actually keep electric motorcycles running all day in African markets.
If the two can successfully combine those strengths, we could be looking at one of the more consequential electric two-wheeler partnerships on the continent yet.

title: This Brooklyn startup will put nearly 700 EV plugs on NYC curbs
content:
EV Charging
New York
Curbside Charging
Michelle Lewis
| Sep 15 2026 - 6:10 am PT
Photo: it's electric
New York City has chosen Brooklyn-based
it’s electric
to supply the hardware for its permanent curbside EV charging network, which will bring nearly 700 Level 2 charging points to all five boroughs over the next three years.
The rollout will replace the city’s existing pilot infrastructure and add 600 new charging points to the current 88. The chargers will be manufactured in Queens.
NYC DOT announced the expansion
in early August
but didn’t reveal who would supply the chargers. The agency is working with the New York Power Authority on procurement and installation.
Each PlugNYC station will have at least two charger posts with two plugs each, for a minimum of four charging points per site. Engineering and construction will be handled by Maverick Corporation, and SWTCH Energy will provide the software platform.
The stations are deliberately headed for dense neighborhoods where residents rely on street parking – especially communities with large numbers of Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) and rideshare drivers. Initial locations include Soundview and Unionport in the Bronx; Rego Park, Forest Hills, and Far Rockaway in Queens; Red Hook, Carroll Gardens, and Bedford-Stuyvesant in Brooklyn; the Upper West Side and Washington Heights in Manhattan; and Stapleton on Staten Island.
That location strategy matters because half of New York City’s car owners park on the street. Without a driveway or garage, charging an EV at home isn’t an option.
The city’s existing curbside chargers are already occupied by an EV more than 70% of the time, with utilization approaching 99% at some locations.
Just as fire hydrants are on every street, our vision is for EV chargers to become that normal – infrastructure New York’s kids simply grow up with,” said Nathan King, cofounder and CEO of it’s electric.
The buildout will also support the city’s
Green Rides initiative
, which requires that 100% of Uber and Lyft trips be completed in zero-emission or wheelchair-accessible vehicles by 2030. New York’s rideshare drivers are already completing around 3 million EV trips per month, according to NYC DOT.
Pricing hasn’t been set yet, but NYC DOT will retain control over what drivers pay. Charging will be billed by the kilowatt-hour, and drivers will be able to pay through multiple apps or by tapping a credit card. The city says prices will be structured to remain affordable while encouraging drivers to move their cars when charging is finished.
Where possible, the sites will also include electrical connections for e-bike charging, electrified bike-share docks, secure bike parking, or cargo-bike hubs.
it’s electric launched its first New York curbside charging pilot at the Brooklyn Army Terminal in Sunset Park in 2023 and is headquartered at Newlab in the Brooklyn Navy Yard. It now operates in Los Angeles, San Francisco, Detroit, Washington, DC, and Boston.
The company has also announced a new funding round led by Halogen Ventures, bringing its total funding to $15 million. The company says every charger it supplies as it expands across North America will be built in Queens.

title: Volvo's new PHEVs beat the Toyota RAV4 with up to 78 miles of electric range
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 15 2026 - 7:05 am PT
introduced the new XC60 and XC90, its first long-range plug-in hybrids. With up to 78 miles on a single charge, the new models are now America’s longest-range electric PHEVs.
Volvo unveils first long-range XC60 and XC90 PHEVs
The new long-range hybrids are a key part of Volvo’s “bridge to a fully electric future,” the company said.
Volvo revealed the new variants of its best-selling XC60 and XC90 SUVs on Tuesday. Alongside an updated design, the new PHEVs offer more than twice the electric driving range of the current models.
Thanks to a larger 41.2 kWh battery, which is more than double the size of the current models, the new XC60 delivers a “class-leading” electric range of up to 78 miles. The XC60 offers up to 73 miles of EV range.
Both of Volvo’s new PHEVs now offer more electric range than any plug-in hybrid in the US. In comparison, the
new Toyota RAV4 PHEV
has an EPA-estimated electric driving range of just 54 miles.
The new long-range Volvo XC60 and XC90 PHEVs (Source: Volvo Cars)
Together with its new all-electric XC60, the brand has built its “strongest-ever electrified offering in the mid-size SUV segment,” according to Volvo Cars’ president and CEO Håkan Samuelsson.
The XC60, Volvo’s best-selling model of all time, received an updated interior and exterior design, including its signature Thor’s Hammer LED headlights.
Inside, the new XC60 features a new dashboard and door panel design, plus Volvo’s latest active safety tech and infotainment system. The setup includes an 11.2″ screen with Google Gemini, Google’s next-gen AI assistant.
New Volvo XC60 PHEV interior (Source: Volvo Cars)
Like all new Volvo cars, the new XC60 and XC90 will receive regular over-the-air (OTA) software updates.
Volvo will begin production of the new long-range PHEVs later this fall, with customer deliveries expected to begin in early 2027.
While the new XC60 and XC90 PHEVs are on the way, we learned last week that
Volvo is pulling the electric EX40
2027 Volvo EX60 (Source: Volvo)
According to
Automotive News
, Volvo plans to replace it with a new entry-level electric SUV by the end of 2027. The EX50, as it’s expected to be called, will start at around $50,000 as a more affordable EV under the EX60.
2027 Volvo EX60 P6 Plus
starts at $59,795 (including destination fee) and offers an EPA-estimated range of up to 307 miles.
Volvo has not yet announced prices for the new long-range XC60 and XC90 PHEVs. The current 2026 Volvo XC60 PHEV starts at $62,545, while the 2026 XC90 PHEV starts at $77,595. Volvo’s three-row electric SUV, the EX90, starts at $78,090.

title: 德赛电池为超充站配储注入新动能
content:
近年来，充电功率从120kW一路拉升至480kW、600kW乃至更高，补能时长不断被压缩。但对运营方而言，功率越高，压力也随之而来：多车同时超充时，瞬时负荷容易突破场站变压器上限，按峰值负荷扩容则一次性投资与需量电费双双抬升，不扩容又只能在高峰限功率；与此同时，充电负荷曲线与用电高峰高度重合，运营方往往在用最贵的电做最薄的毛利。容量与电价的双重约束，成为超充站走向规模化运营绕不开的现实难题。
面对这一行业共性课题，德赛电池携手湖北桓德新能源科技有限公司，从其超充站的实际运营场景出发，给出了一份标准化答案。
具体而言，德赛电池在湖北桓德新能源旗下超充站项目配置16MWh储能系统，将储能柜、充电主机与场站配电纳入统一调度，让储能充当"电力缓冲池"：低谷蓄能、高峰放电，场站既不依赖扩容，也不必吃高价电。项目以德赛智储自研的261kWh储能柜为基本单元模块化组合，柜体集成电池系统、PCS变流、能量管理与消防系统，支持灵活分布布置与分期扩容，既适配新建场站的整体规划，也便于已投运场站的改造加装。
电芯的循环寿命、一致性与安全性，直接决定储能系统全生命周期的度电成本。作为当前储能系统的主流大容量规格，自研314Ah电芯在单体能量密度、成组效率与集成度之间取得了较好平衡：单柜所需电芯数量更少、串并联结构更简洁，有利于降低簇间环流与一致性风险，同时减少结构件占用、提升整柜能量密度。对充电站这类日循环强度高的场景而言，更长循环寿命直接对应更长使用年限与更低度电成本。
项目通过变压器负载控制和峰谷套利模式，不仅能够实时监测场站变压器负荷，使变压器始终运行在安全区间内，同时对于充电站而言，售电电价不变、购电成本下降，价差直接转化为运营利润，收益模型清晰可测算。
从"充电"到"储充一体"，补能网络正从单纯的用电负荷，转向具备调节能力的柔性节点。16MWh储充一体超充站项目的落地，既为湖北桓德新能源在超充站配储领域积累了可复制的工程样板，也是德赛电池在储充场景中的一次务实验证。未来，德赛电池将持续以可靠性与安全性，携手更多合作伙伴，把储能的价值落到每一个具体场景里。

title: 晶科/天合/隆基预中标，多个光伏集采项目结果公示
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期光伏组件市场中标与交付动态频传，国内多地组件中标结果陆续公示。汉伏能源高效组件发往奥地利，晶科、天合、隆基、正泰等多家组件企业也相继入围山西、广东等地的光伏项目。
汉伏能源36MW组件批量交付奥地利
9月15日，汉伏能源宣布，近日其第二批HITOUCH 6N PRO四分片高效组件从上海陆续发往奥地利。
据悉，此次出货的HITOUCH 6N PRO 655W采用大尺寸硅片与四分片高效电池技术。这批高效组件将分别安装于施泰尔马克州维尔东与克罗滕多夫两个小镇的地面电站，两个项目合计36MW。
100MW光伏组件采购中标公示
9月14日，华能众丰沁县100MW（118.79712MWp）光伏发电项目—光伏组件设备采购中标候选人公示，晶科能源位列第一中标候选人，晶澳太阳能为第二中标候选人，通威股份为第三中标候选人。
招标公告显示，华能众丰沁县100MW（118.79712MWp）光伏发电项目交流侧装机为100MW，拟采用N型730Wp及以上单晶高效组件和300kW以上组串式逆变器，通过35kV升压箱变升压后接入拟建的110kV升压站。招标人为山西众丰生态农业有限责任公司，供货地点为山西省长治市沁县施工项目现场。
天合光能预中标光伏组件采购订单
9月11日，格盟应县新能源有限公司光伏组件采购项目中标候选人公示。其中，天合光能股份有限公司为第一中标候选人，投标报价1770万元；英利能源发展有限公司为第二中标候选人，1752万元。
此前招标公告显示，招标人为格盟应县新能源有限公司，预估采购容量为25MW。供货周期为2026年11月底前，交货地点为山西省朔州市应县跑马梁光伏电站。
隆基、正泰等6企预中标组件订单
9月11日，惠州市龙源电力技术服务有限公司2026-2027年光伏组件框架公开招标（三次招标）中标结果公示，共计6家企业中标，分别是：隆基乐叶光伏科技有限公司、正泰新能科技股份有限公司、晶科能源股份有限公司、浙江爱旭太阳能科技有限公司、广东东江新能源科技有限公司、东峻阳光(厦门)新能源有限公司。
招标公告显示，项目招标人为惠州市电力发展有限公司，本项目预估金额8000万元，招标人不对该预估金额进行承诺，具体以合同有效期实际发生的订单为准。

title: 赣锋锂电注资增至35亿，增幅约10%
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月13日，天眼查显示，赣锋锂电发生工商变更，注册资本由31.75574668亿人民币增至35.08908002亿人民币，增幅约10%。
图：赣锋锂电企业信息
赣锋锂电成立于2011年6月，法定代表人为肖海燕，经营范围包括锂离子动力电池、燃料电池、储能电池的研发、生产和销售，超级电容器、电池管理系统、风光电储能系统、相关设备仪器的研发、生产和销售等。
据此前消息，本次注册资本变更，对应赣锋锂业今年3月董事会审议通过的母公司增资事项，新增注册资本约3.33亿元，由赣锋锂业以自有资金认缴出资。在此之前，赣锋锂电在今年6月完成20亿元外部增资扩股，半年内完成两轮增资。
资本补充的同时，赣锋锂电储能产品研发与产线建设同步推进。
当前，赣锋锂电储能业务重点推进大容量储能电芯落地，自研588Ah储能大电芯产线已进入调试试产阶段，配套的6.26MWh集装箱储能产品计划于2026年四季度批量交付。此外，648Ah储能电芯研发工作也在同步开展。
产能端，现阶段赣锋锂电储能电芯产能利用率维持高位。目前，新余基地已建成40GWh动力储能电芯产能与18GWh储能PACK产能，南昌新增10GWh储能电池产线尚在建设阶段。

title: 超1GWh！天合光能等4企储能订单及项目新动态
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，多家储能企业接连披露海内外项目订单、交付及落地进展。其中，天合储能签署日本约1GWh储能系统供货协议，卫蓝新能源向新疆储能项目供应约40MWh混合固液电芯，创维储能落地越南2.09MWh工商业储能项目，德赛电池则为湖北超充站配置16MWh储能系统。
天合储能签署日本1GWh储能订单
9月14日，天合储能与日本清洁能源平台AMP-lify签署谅解备忘录，计划为AMP-lify在日本推进的储能项目供应约1GWh储能系统。
根据协议，天合储能将向AMP-lify相关项目供应Elementa 3系列储能系统，并提供系统配置、技术咨询、交付协调及售后服务等支持。
此外，天合储能还提供Elementa 3 Flex产品，单机容量为1.56MWh，占地约5平方米，可用于应对日本储能项目在土地、运输及周边环境等方面的限制。
卫蓝新能源交付40MWh半固态电芯
近日，卫蓝新能源半固态电芯参与新疆甘泉堡400MW/1600MWh混合电化学共享储能项目，相关储能单元已完成建设及并网。
该项目位于新疆乌鲁木齐甘泉堡经济技术开发区，建设单位为乌鲁木齐和芯储能有限公司，整体储能规模为400MW/1600MWh。
其中，卫蓝新能源通过旗下卫蓝海博（淄博）新能源科技有限公司，与产业链合作伙伴协同推进产品应用，为项目提供314Ah混合固液磷酸铁锂电芯，结合项目采购及验收情况折算，参与规模约40MWh。
创维储能落地越南2.09MWh工商储项目
近日，创维储能位于越南胡志明市的2.09MWh工商业储能项目完成系统投运，这是公司在越南落地的首个工商业储能项目。
该项目总容量2.09MWh，应用于热带高温高湿环境。项目实施过程中，创维储能负责方案设计、设备交付、现场施工、技术指导及并网调试等环节，并围绕充放电策略、设备接线、现场培训及系统调试提供技术支持，目前项目已完成并网运行。
据悉，创维储能同期完成越南市场品牌授权，本地渠道布局进一步推进。此次项目落地也成为公司进入越南工商业储能市场后的首个实际应用案例。
德赛电池落地16MWh储能系统订单
近日，德赛电池为湖北桓德新能源超充站项目配置16MWh储能系统，应用于超充场站储充一体化场景。
据介绍，该项目采用德赛电池自研的261kWh储能柜作为基本单元，整体配置16MWh储能系统，并将储能系统与充电主机、场站配电进行协同控制。系统通过峰谷价差进行充放电，同时结合变压器负载控制，降低充电站高峰时段的用电负荷。

title: EKPO unveils next-generation NM20 fuel cell stack
content:
The NM20 platform has been developed around scalability, optimized manufacturing and system architectures, and easier integration into heavy-duty applications. EKPO has refined the stack, module, interfaces, and manufacturing processes while redesigning and standardizing the architecture from the bipolar plate to the housing.
Assembly and joining techniques have also been optimized for automation, quality assurance, and traceability. Module volume has been reduced by approximately 20%, while the fully assembled module weighs 178 kg, a reduction of 39 kg. The Cell Row Assembly is approximately 25% lighter.
Functions including media distribution, water separation, media monitoring, sensor technology, cell voltage monitoring (CVM), and high-voltage connectivity are integrated directly into the stack architecture. Standardized, reusable components support different power levels and configurations while reducing the number of variants required.
The NM20 range includes a 323-cell single-stack module delivering more than 200 kW, a Max variant producing more than 300 kW, and a 646-cell twin-stack module delivering more than 400 kW. The twin-stack module has a maximum continuous current of 1,000 A and operating pressures of up to 3.0 bara.
EKPO specifies a service life of 25,000 operating hours and efficiency of 56%–69%, depending on the operating range. Operating temperatures reach up to 95°C.
Dr. Stefan Dwenger, Managing Director of EKPO Fuel Cell Technologies, said: “The new generation of the NM20 marks a significant milestone in the industrialization of our fuel cell technology. The NM20 stack platform combines high power density, straightforward system integration, operating temperatures of up to 95°C, and an architecture designed specifically for industrial scale-up. We are thus laying the groundwork for the widespread use of hydrogen powertrains in heavy-duty transportation.”
The platform is intended for heavy-duty road, rail, and marine transportation, as well as stationary power supply and backup power systems.

title: INERATEC and Ramboll advance e-SAF production at ERA ONE
content:
The two companies are currently in the front-end engineering design (FEED) phase for an upgrading unit at ERA ONE, following a successfully completed pre-FEED phase. The upgrading unit will convert Fischer-Tropsch crude – a synthetic hydrocarbon mixture produced at the plant – into standard-compliant sustainable aviation fuel (e-SAF) directly on site.
The process steps to be integrated into the existing production infrastructure include isomerization, hydrocracking, and distillation. INERATEC said the addition of these upgrading units extends its technological vertical integration, enabling the conversion of captured CO₂ and green hydrogen into synthetic aviation fuel within a single integrated production platform. The company said this reduces dependence on external refinery infrastructure and supports scalable, decentralized fuel production.
“With the further development of our upgrading technology, we are taking the next important step on the way to the industrial production of drop-in-capable e-SAF. The expansion of ERA ONE enables us to take technological control over further process steps in the power-to-liquid value chain and to offer our customers a reliable supply of synthetic fuels in the long term,” said Dr. Tim Böltken, Co-Founder and CEO of INERATEC.
Ramboll contributes international engineering and project management expertise in Power-to-X and sustainable fuels to the collaboration.
“The decarbonisation of aviation requires high-performance and scalable solutions for the production of sustainable aviation fuels. We are pleased to support INERATEC in the further development of ERA ONE and to jointly create the conditions for the industrial deployment of e-SAF,” said Anders Nimgaard Schultz, Director PtX & Gas Infrastructure of Ramboll.
The project is supported by Breakthrough Energy Catalyst and the European Investment Bank. INERATEC has described ERA ONE as a blueprint for future industrial power-to-liquid plants.

title: Stargate Hydrogen secures €20.6m for production scale-up
content:
The expansion will increase Stargate Hydrogen’s manufacturing capacity for large-scale industrial electrolysis and Power-to-X projects.
The new plant will be developed in phases and will have annual production capacity of 250 MW for alkaline electrolyzer electrodes, 150 MW for pressurized alkaline stacks, and 66 MW for electrolyzer systems.
Stargate Hydrogen’s technology includes a proprietary stack design and electrodes coated with a patented ceramic-based catalyst that replaces precious metals.
The €20.6 million grant was awarded under the EU Innovation Fund through an agreement with the European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA). The funding will support the expansion of the company’s existing manufacturing operations in Tallinn.
Marko Virkebau, Chief Executive Officer of Stargate Hydrogen, said: “This grant marks an important milestone for Stargate Hydrogen and demonstrates confidence in our technology and manufacturing strategy. With the help of the Innovation Fund, we truly step up our game. After the factory expansion is finalised, Stargate will become one of the largest electrolyser manufacturers in Europe. Such manufacturing capability is important in order for us to be able to deliver our products to large industrial electrolysis projects, such as projects delivering green ammonia, synthetic natural gas, as well as sustainable aviation fuel.”
The project is expected to create approximately 150 direct jobs and support additional employment across construction, logistics, maintenance, and the European supply chain.
Over its first 10 years of operation, Stargate Hydrogen expects the project to avoid approximately 3 million tons of CO₂-equivalent emissions by supporting wider deployment of green hydrogen in chemicals, steel, and other energy-intensive industries.

title: 2028 Volvo XC60 And XC90 Plug-In Hybrids Get A Massive EV Range Boost
content:
2028 Volvo XC60 And XC90 Plug-In Hybrids Get A Massive EV Range Boost
With more than double the EV range, the 2028 Volvo XC60 and XC90 PHEVs will make you forget that gas stations exist.
- Volvo's updated XC60 and XC90 will be the longest range plug-in hybrids in the U.S.
- Owners can cover most of their driving needs just using battery power.
- The XC60's EV range is more than the original Nissan Leaf.
Office commutes, everyday errands, and even weekend getaways can now be handled purely on battery power in the 2028 Volvo XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrids (PHEVs). That's because both SUVs are getting more than double the all-electric range of their current versions, thanks to larger, floor-mounted battery packs, Volvo said Tuesday.
The updated XC60 will cover 78 miles on a single charge before its gas engine kicks in, up from 35 miles today. That's more range than the first-generation Nissan Leaf, which had an EPA rating of 73 miles. And that car was all electric. The larger XC90 PHEV's all-electric range is now 73 miles, up from 32 miles on the current model. That makes the XC60 and XC90 the two longest-range PHEVs sold in the U.S.
Gallery: 2028 Volvo XC60 T8 Long Range PHEV
The range increase reflects real advances in battery technology and energy density, but it's also a reminder of Volvo's retreat from its original EV ambitions. The automaker pledged to fully ditch combustion engines by 2030 at the start of the decade, then walked that back in 2024 as EV sales growth slowed more than expected, especially in the U.S. Volvo says it's still committed to EVs, but it's clearly doubling down on plug-in hybrids too.
“The XC60 is our best-selling model of all time, while the XC90 marked the beginning of our premium journey,” Hakan Samuelsson, the CEO of Volvo Cars said in a statement. “Now, as long-range plug-in hybrids, they build on those legacies and, together with the all-electric EX60, give us our strongest-ever electrified offering in the mid-size SUV segment. This means a path to full electrification for every customer.”
Volvo says the median round-trip driving distance for its U.S. customers is just 22 miles, and the vast majority of its drivers here cover less than 30 miles a day. That means most owners could drive entirely on electric power for most of their needs, whether that's dropping the kids at school or a slightly longer weekend trip. You could also do more things with fewer charging sessions, thanks to the larger battery pack.
Gallery: 2028 Volvo XC90 T8 Long Range PHEV
With gas prices soaring due to the U.S. war in Iran, owners could lean on cheap residential electricity for most of their driving and skip the pump on most days. That could also potentially mean less wear on the gas engine and lower repair bills down the road. For longer trips, the XC60 delivers 590 miles of total range on a full tank and a full charge, while the XC90 is good for 560 miles.
Both cars will continue to be powered by their turbocharged four-cylinder engines which are now paired with larger 37.9 kilowatt hours of usable battery capacity, doubling from 18.8 kWh before. They will continue to get standard AWD and the same 455 horsepower of peak combined output. Volvo didn’t say if the PHEVs could fast charge, but added that despite doubling the capacity, they will charge in under six hours on a Level 2 charger, which is only a 14% increase in charging time. If you have a more powerful home charger with 16 amps of output, the battery can juice up in four hours.
The XC60, the automaker’s best-selling model globally and in the U.S., is also getting a minor facelift. The front end design is now sleeker with a smaller and more squared off grille and more chiseled headlamps. The Thor’s hammer daytime running lights also get updated signatures. The tailgate and taillamp now look cleaner than before whereas the overall silhouette stays identical.
The 2028 Volvo XC60 plug-in hybrid will have longest all electric range of any PHEV in the U.S.
PHEVs have made some real strides over the past few years, too. The Mercedes-Benz GLC 350e can cover up to 54 miles on a single charge from a 24.8 kWh battery. And the 2026 Toyota RAV4 PHEV also gets up to 54 miles of EPA-rated all-electric range with a larger 22.7 kWh battery. Both the Mercedes and the Toyota are among the few PHEVs which can also DC fast charge, with a 10-80% time of just about 30 minutes. The Mercedes peaks at 60 kW of maximum charging rate whereas the Toyota is rated for 50 kW.
But again, all this is based on the assumption that owners will actually charge their PEHVs and not be lazy about it. If they don’t, they’ll just be lugging a really heavy battery pack around and burn more gas. Some previous studies have shown that most PHEV owners don’t really plug in their vehicles, leading to more emissions and fewer savings at the pump than what the automakers advertise.
However, a newer peer-reviewed study from Toyota concluded that PHEV owners in North America were actually plugging-in their vehicles most of the time, taking advantage of the all-electric driving range as intended.
Both the XC60 and XC90 long range PHEVs will enter production this fall and go on sale in the U.S. early 2027.

title: BMW Is Giving Its Navigation System A Tesla-Style Makeover
content:
BMW Is Giving Its Navigation System A Tesla-Style Makeover
The new BMW iX3 is the first to get the updated system, which integrates the navigation and driver assistance info into a single view.
- BMW is updating the way its latest GPS navigation system looks.
- Starting next month, cars running the BMW Operating System X will get a unified 3D view.
- The redesign puts the route guidance, the vehicle’s surroundings, and driver assistance information into a single screen on the central display.
BMW is changing how it shows driver assistance information in the latest iteration of its in-car navigation system.
Starting next month, cars running BMW Operating System X, which debuted on the new iX3 electric SUV, will get a redesigned BMW Maps app that overlays driver assistance info onto a 3D view that shows the car’s position on the road in real time, the route, and how the safety systems work.
That’s a similar approach to Tesla’s 3D visualizations, which show the vehicle in its lane and the upcoming maneuvers, based on the trip planner info.
BMW says the updated BMW Maps experience helps with navigation on highways, at intersections, and in city traffic. It also makes assisted and semi-automated driving even easier to understand, as the dynamic 3D view overlays those inputs in real time.
The car is shown within its lane and at the correct level, with the surrounding vehicles also depicted on the central infotainment screen, which is useful when driving on multi-lane highways or busy urban areas.
The new navigation system will particularly come in handy a few months from now, as the German automaker is gearing up to deploy navigation-guided, semi-automated driving in urban areas in Germany in 2027, with more countries to follow.
Until that happens, owners of the new BMW iX3 crossover can use the Highway Assistant 2 system, which enables hands-free driving on highways at speeds of up to 80 miles per hour (130 kilometers per hour). In addition to the first Neue Klasse EV, the upcoming i3, iX5, and facelifted i7 will also get the same features.
Gallery: BMW Maps With Driver Assistance
BMW’s all-in-one 3D navigation system was developed in-house but uses navigation data and map technology from Mapbox, which provides information about lanes, landmarks, and other physical features.
The automaker said that the updated Maps feature with driver assistance is available only in combination with the latest Highway Assistant or Highway & City Assistant system in select countries, cities, and on select roads. The promotional video that showcases the new features was shot in the United States, so logic dictates that it will work here, but the company didn’t say which cities or roads are compatible.

title: BYD Takes On The Tesla Semi With Its Own 372-Mile Truck
content:
BYD Takes On The Tesla Semi With Its Own 372-Mile Truck
The new ETT 44 electric semi comes with an enormous 651 kWh battery and megawatt charging. It's coming to Europe soon.
Tesla isn't the only brand showcasing its new European electric semi trucks at the IAA Transportation 2026 show today in Hanover, Germany. BYD also showed off its own vision for the future of electric long-haul trucking, and while it looks much more traditional than Tesla's Semi, it's anything but conventional under the skin.
It's called the BYD ETT 44, which isn't the catchiest name in the world but it is a commercial work truck, not a something to impress your neighbors with. The ETT 44 4X2 uses BYD's "Ultra-safe Blade Battery" tech, which is a massive 651 kWh Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) unit. That enormous battery powers a 732-horsepower electric motor, with 1,000 peak horsepower, and it's capable of 1.5+ megawatt "Flash Charging" using MCS stations.
According to BYD, using an MCS charger, the ETT 44 can jump from 20-80% state-of-charge (SOC) in less than 20 minutes. With a full battery, it packs a claimed range of 372 miles, and the aforementioned 20-80% charge is said to add another 248 miles. That's pretty good for something that weighs 24,140 pounds unladen. There's going to be a 6X2 model as well, but there aren't range specs for that one just yet. The most impressive spec, though, is the 44-tonne (97,000-pound) gross vehicle combination weight, which bests Tesla's by four tonnes (8,818 pounds).
BYD mentioned a warranty, too. The Blade Battery gets a 10-year / 1.2-million kilometer (745,000-mile) warranty, which is longer than most European electric truck makers' 6-8 year warranties. For a workhorse, it's interesting to see such a long warranty. For whatever it's worth, Tesla did not announce the terms of the warranty for the Semi, the BYD's main competitor.
This platform won't just be for semi trucks, though. It will be available for all sorts of commercial vehicles, like rigid trucks and yard tractors. It's part of BYD's commercial ecosystem, offering commercial customers more options.
Like most semi trucks, the ETT 44 has a big tall roof with a sleeper cab in there for driver's on long-haul trips. It even has Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and a 12.8-inch screen, to keep drivers sane on longer journeys.
The BYD ETT 44 joins several electric semi trucks in Europe, including Tesla's, Volvo's, and Mercedes', so it will be interesting to see how many commercial applications it's used in. There are more established trucking brands in Europe that have their own offerings, and Swedish trucking giant Einride just ordered 500 Tesla Semis. So while BYD certainly has the specs to compete, and even beat, its competitors, it's heading into a quickly crowding market.

title: Hyundai's Tesla FSD Rival Is Delayed To 2029. But It May Be Worth The Wait
content:
Hyundai's Tesla FSD Rival Is Delayed To 2029. But It May Be Worth The Wait
Hyundai says it didn't want to rush a "middling Level 2++" system to market, so its in-house ADAS is now coming in 2029.
- Hyundai is developing two driver-assistance systems in parallel to take on Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised).
- One will use Nvidia's platform and the other is being developed in-house.
- The automaker plans to begin the rollout in 2028, with the in-house Atria AI Level 2++ system arriving in late 2029.
Hyundai is delaying the launch of its next-generation in-house advanced driver assistance system (ADAS), betting that a revised approach and a fresh Nvidia partnership will help it take on rivals like Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised).
The South Korean automaker says it's planning to advance its driver-assistance ambitions in two phases. First, Hyundai will roll out an Nvidia-based Level 2 system to vehicles, the company announced during its HMG Autonomous Driving Media Day on Saturday. In parallel, the automaker will continue developing its in-house technology and unleash that in 2029. Reuters notes this is two years later than Hyundai initially planned.
“We made a strategic decision to slow down,” Park Min-woo, the head of HMG's advanced vehicle platform division told Korea JoongAng Daily. “Rushing into mass production now risks delivering a middling Level 2++ system, far short of our real target,” he added. He said Hyundai sells 7 million vehicles annually across 190 markets, and the driving data collected from these vehicles could help speed up development and overtake rivals in the autonomy race.
It isn't alone in this race. Pretty much every major global automaker is trying to build cars that can accelerate, brake, steer, and navigate complex traffic on their own. From Korea and China to the U.S. and Europe, automakers are betting that highly automated cars will make roads safer than human drivers, while also unlocking a new revenue stream for their businesses. Toyota also recently shared its plans to release its own FSD-like system in 2028.
Hyundai released footage this past weekend showing an Ioniq 5 equipped with its latest ADAS navigating some seriously complex urban roads. With a human supervisor on board, the EV deftly makes its way through Seoul's Gangnam District, an area about as congested and chaotic as Manhattan.
That vehicle is running the automaker's latest Level 2+ ADAS, which can drive from point A to point B on its own while a human driver supervises. Hyundai said production models with this system will start rolling out in the second half of 2028. That rollout will bring software and hardware standardization not just between Hyundai and Kia vehicles, but also between Motional and 42dot, the company's robotaxi and AV software development divisions.
In the first phase, vehicles will run on the Nvidia Drive Hyperion 10 architecture. Nvidia says this platform can support Level 2 supervised ADAS up to unsupervised Level 4 autonomy. The company told reporters that the system will rely on cameras, ultrasonic sensors, and radar, but skip lidar. (Hyundai could add lidar for its Level 3 systems, though, an executive said.) Mercedes-Benz also uses the Nvidia Drive Hyperion platform for its MB.Drive Assist Pro system, skipping lidar in favor of cameras and radar.
The second phase will bring Hyundai's in-house Atria AI autonomous driving system, which the company says will start rolling out in the second half of 2029. Hyundai calls Atria AI a "Level 2++" system, which is industry jargon for a more capable ADAS that still needs human supervision. Per SAE International's levels of driving automation, Level 2 systems are supervised, while Level 3 ones can operate autonomously at times. Level 2++ would land somewhere in the middle.
Atria AI is essentially Hyundai's answer to Tesla's FSD (Supervised). It will use an end-to-end system, meaning that an AI model will take in sensor inputs and spit out driving commands.
“Autonomous driving competitiveness depends not on how much data you secure, but on how rapidly you can connect data to learning, validation and performance improvement,” Junghyun Kwon, the head of HMG’s autonomous driving development center said in a statement. “Through the data flywheel system now in full operation, we expect continuous improvement of issues identified on real roads and rapid technology advancement.”
Hyundai's autonomy ambitions extend well beyond passenger cars. The automaker is deeply invested in humanoid robots through its wholly owned Boston Dynamics subsidiary, and it plans to roll out its first Ioniq 5 robotaxis through its AV division Motional in Las Vegas by the end of this year. Separately, Hyundai is also supplying Ioniq 5 robotaxis to Waymo, with the vehicles expected to join that fleet by the end of this year.

title: Lidl Is Now Using A Truck With No Cab To Ship Goods
content:
Einride’s Level 4-capable truck got a first-of-its-kind permit to operate on Germany’s public roads.
Photo by:
4:22am ET
Supermarket giant Lidl has partnered with Einride to deploy an autonomous, cab-less truck for daily deliveries.
The driverless truck got a first-of-its-kind permit from Germany’s strict transport regulator to drive on public roads.
Einride claims Germany’s approval process is among the toughest in the world, and getting it is like a badge of honor.
Lidl, the German supermarket chain that sells everything from fresh fruit to Arnold Schwarzenegger-endorsed power tools, has deployed Germany’s first cab-less SAE Level 4 autonomous truck in daily operations on public roads.
The truck, engineered and built by Einride, got a first-of-its-kind permit from the country’s Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA), which is known for its strictness. It’s a big win for the Swedish startup, which also operates a fleet of about 200 electric trucks rented to companies like Heineken and PepsiCo.
Einride boasts that achieving a Level 4 approval in Germany “sets a new benchmark for what is already possible in autonomous logistics globally,” and that the permit confirms that the driverless truck can operate reliably and safely under real-world conditions on public roads.
“Germany's approval process is among the toughest in the world, and obtaining clearance there gives us a foundation to scale with confidence,” said Roozbeh Charli, Chief Executive Officer at Einride.
According to the truck maker, Lidl’s new autonomous pod is currently transporting goods between a logistics center and a store in Edermunde. It drives one shift a day, five days a week, and carries approximately 45 pallets per shift.
All this being said, there is an undisclosed asterisk here. After reviewing the video embedded above and comparing it to Google Street View imagery, it looks like the autonomous truck's route is less than a mile long, as the store is right next to the warehouse. The company said that the next step is to expand the route to include multiple stops in a so-called “milkrun” model.
Besides getting some bragging rights, Einride and Lidl said that the deployment also addresses the growing issue of commercial driver shortages, as well as securing the flow of goods from warehouses to stores.
With the first cab-less electric truck making deliveries in Germany, the Swedish company is already in talks with Swarz Group, Lidl’s parent company, to explore the possibility of deploying more autonomous trucks.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Einride’s pod-like electric truck doesn’t have a driver or a safety monitor, but its movements are remotely monitored by a human operator. However, the company makes it clear that the remote operator doesn’t drive the vehicle; they can, however, perform low-speed maneuvering at up to 4 miles per hour (6 kilometers per hour) to handle edge cases or facilitate docking operations.
The autonomous truck, which is built by a contract manufacturer in the Netherlands, features a comprehensive sensor suite, including nine outdoor cameras, six radars, and four Lidars.

title: New York City Is Getting 700 EV Chargers Right On The Curb
content:
New York selected Brooklyn-based It's Electric to install 700 curbside EV chargers over the next three years.
9:01am ET
New York City selected Brooklyn-based It's Electric to install 700 curbside EV chargers.
The hardware will be dispersed across the five boroughs and target neighborhoods with lots of rideshare drivers.
Curbside charging is common in Europe but rare in most large U.S. cities.
Say goodbye to dangling a 30-foot extension cord out of your window to charge your Tesla. New York City has selected Brooklyn-based startup It’s Electric to blanket the five boroughs with hundreds of new curbside chargers, the company announced on Tuesday. The idea is to make going electric an easier decision in a city where off-street parking is hard to come by and where EV charging has always been a challenge.
It’s Electric will install 700 level 2 chargers across the city over the next three years, creating the kind of EV infrastructure for street-parkers that’s popular in Europe but barely exists in most U.S. cities.
“Once you leave L.A. and you go to Boston, you go to New York, you go to San Francisco, you go to D.C., you go to Philadelphia, you go to New York, it's a desert,” Tiya Gordon, the startup’s cofounder and COO, told me.
It's Electric's EV chargers don't have a built-in cord and were designed from the start for New York City streets.
The U.S. has an unusually high proportion of people who live in detached homes, which is a boon to the country’s EV transition, since those folks can charge cheaply in their garage or driveway. But making the switch is much harder for people who live in apartments in America’s densest cities and don’t have that luxury. Although DC fast chargers tend to get more attention and public funding, EV researchers and advocates see curbside Level 2 infrastructure as an important piece of the puzzle for expanding EV adoption too.
Today, New York has 88 curbside Flo chargers that were installed through a pilot program and that will be replaced over time by It’s Electric. Those have been “immensely popular with EV owners,” the city said in August, when it
announced plans
to dramatically expand its curbside charging network. According to the city’s Department of Transportation, the sites were occupied by an EV 70% of the time (or up to 99% for some stations) and were supplying energy 85% of the time they were occupied.
It's Electric will install 700 EV chargers across New York City's five boroughs, creating the kind of street-side infrastructure that's rare in the U.S.
Now the DOT is expanding the program in a bid to cut CO2 emissions and support its goal of making all rideshare vehicles electric by 2030. For the new It’s Electric sites, the city selected areas heavily populated by Uber, Lyft, and taxi drivers. Gordon hopes that will be a game changer for the city’s 80,000 rideshare drivers.
“Without curbside charging in neighborhoods like Jackson Heights or Flushing or the Bronx, they are being forced to drive to a limited amount of fast charging stations, wait in long lines, … pay 50 cents per kilowatt hour, and then drive two hours back into Manhattan,” she said. “By putting chargers in the neighborhoods where these rideshare drivers just park overnight and go to sleep, they're waking up and they have that full battery.”
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
It’s Electric’s hardware differs from other
level 2 chargers
you might find in a parking garage or by the curb. The sleek, stainless steel posts lack included cords; drivers bring their own instead that the company provides. Further reducing the clutter, they don’t have screens or credit card readers. Gordon told me the company designed the hardware from the start to get through New York’s Public Design Commission review, which “ensures that we just don't have terribly ugly street furniture everywhere.”
“New York has been like the apex city for us in a lot of ways, and so we knew that we had to do things in a very specific way to win a city like New York,” she said.
The new EV charging posts will be installed in neighborhoods with high concentrations of rideshare drivers.
It’s Electric’s chargers get their power from nearby apartment buildings, which the company says makes the infrastructure cheaper and quicker to build. Gordon said they will be dispersed throughout the city, and that a given block will have no more than two units. They will be manufactured in Queens.
On Tuesday, It’s electric also announced that it had closed a new funding round, bringing its total funding to $15 million. Today, the company operates 50 chargers and has 700 customers, Gordon said, with all of those coming online since April of last year. It should have many more in the ground soon; the startup has also won contracts in Boston, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Philadelphia.

title: President Trump Says He's Open To Chinese EVs. But Only If They're Made Here
content:
President Trump Says He's Open To Chinese EVs. But Only If They're Made Here
During a segment on Fox News, Trump said he'd be okay with them if they were made domestically. But current laws make that tough.
- On Fox News, Trump said he'd be OK with Chinese car brands making vehicles here for sale.
- However, there is still a 100% tariff on Chinese-made cars, and a ban on cars that use Chinese-developed software and hardware.
- The news has attracted the ire of some politicians, including Michigan senator Elissa Slotkin.
If you’re a Chinese automaker with eyes on the U.S. market, it hasn’t been such a great time for you. What once felt like an inevitable step in the late 2010s has quickly turned into a country protecting its home manufacturing base. Tariffs make importing uncompetitive, while software and hardware bans for anything developed in China make sales infeasible. It's safe to say that U.S.-China relations are pretty frosty, and it wasn't looking like they were going to get better anytime soon.
But last Friday, while on Fox News’ Ingraham Angle, Trump said he would be open to Chinese automakers coming to the U.S., so long as they build the cars here.
“If China wanted to come in and open a plant to build their cars here, I'd be okay with that," Trump said. "Japan does it, but they hire our people. The big thing is they hire our people.” However, he wasn’t OK with these brands using Mexico to build cars and ship them here, and circumvent any sort of trade rules, he said.
On one hand, this feels very incongruent considering the U.S. has been somewhat bipartisan in its opposition to Chinese cars ever coming to the U.S., even if they’re built here. Last week, Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy explicitly went after Ford, which has a licensing deal with Chinese battery manufacturer CATL for its Michigan facility. Ford has a battery plant here in the U.S., which used hires American workers to produce batteries using designs and expertise licensed from CATL. Yet, the scathing letter went out of its way to deride Ford’s involvement with China. This is hot on the heels of Michigan Senator Elissa Slotkin sounding the alarm that there could be a package to accept Chinese cars in the U.S. as part of a deal with China. Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit the U.S. and meet with Trump later this month.
That rumored package isn’t great news for Slotkin, who in part sponsored the bill that wants to flat-out ban Chinese cars from ever being sold in the U.S. Still, even without her bill, there’s a slightly softer effective ban put in place by the Department of Commerce. If a car has hardware or software developed by Chinese firms, then it can’t be sold in the U.S., starting in 2027 for software and 2030 for hardware. That rule isn’t just for show, either. It’s the reason why Polestar was banned in the U.S., and why Mercedes-Benz may be embroiled in a battle with the U.S. government. So, despite what Trump says, the infrastructure in place doesn’t allow for Chinese cars to come here.
On the other hand, Trump has openly talked about wanting a better relationship with China. Sure, he may talk a lot about trade deficits, or spying, or China’s role in the Iran war, but in the same breath he’s extolled President Xi in the past. Also, Trump’s comments aren’t new. In 2024 during his campaign, Trump was open to the idea that Chinese cars could be sold here, so long as they’re made here in the U.S. Perhaps things will cool off between the two countries.
Whether or not Chinese cars will come to the U.S. will be seen in a few weeks. For better or worse, some of Trump's more left-field promises end up coming true. There may be political resistance to Chinese cars, but if Trump gives the go-ahead, I wouldn’t be surprised if the U.S. suddenly lets them come.

title: This Tiny EV Camper Is Smaller Than A Chevy Bolt. It Sleeps Four
content:
It’s also extremely affordable, costing less than $15,000 with all the kit included.
Photo by:
Everything Electric APAC
1:55am ET
A startup is making a kei car-like electric camper that costs less than $15,000.
With a pop-up roof tent and some clever packaging, Vala’s tiny electric camper can sleep four–in a pinch.
The tiny house on wheels is based on a Wuling EV that’s shorter and narrower than a Chevy Bolt.
America’s idea of a house on wheels typically involves a truck chassis and a $100,000+ price tag. As always, there are exceptions, but none can quite match what China is cooking right now.
This tiny camper is almost as small as a Japanese kei car, and yet its makers claim it can sleep up to four people. Measuring just 141.7 inches (3.6 meters) long, 59 in (1.5 m) wide, and 74.8 in (1.9 m) tall, the pint-sized motorhome is shorter and narrower than a
Chevrolet Bolt
, but quite tall.
The fact that it has a built-in pop-up roof tent also helps, as two people can cuddle up there and leave the second twin bed downstairs open for another couple of the kids. As is the case with most RVs, the bed on the main floor only converts from a table and a couple of seats.
According to
Everything Electric APAC
, there’s a large TV at the rear, which swivels in and out, so occupants can watch it from the inside when the weather is bad or turn it into an outdoor small-scale cinema. The rear of the van also has a slide-out table that can accommodate all sorts of appliances, but they can only be used when the rear door is open. That’s not ideal, but it’s to be expected for a car so small.
Speaking of appliances, they draw power directly from the van’s high-voltage battery, thanks to
vehicle-to-load (V2L)
functionality, so nobody is inhaling nasty fumes from a noisy gas generator.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The van itself is made by
, a brand that’s known for its partnership with General Motors. It’s powered by a 30.6-kilowatt-hour battery that’s good for a CLTC-rated driving range of up to 190 miles (305 kilometers) on a full charge. A 40-horsepower electric motor powers the rear wheels, so there’s not a lot to write home about in terms of specs.
However, the whole thing costs the equivalent of less than $15,000, which makes it fantastic value for money. The base vehicle is roughly $8,000, with Vala adding another $7,000 worth of stuff. Sure, its driving range may not be a great fit for the great American highway, but for short camping trips with the kids, it could work.

title: Waymo Is Bringing Driverless Rides To Las Vegas
content:
Waymo Is Bringing Driverless Rides To Las Vegas
The company has been rapidly expanding through the U.S. this year. Now, it's coming to Vegas, where rival Zoox already operates.
Waymo is collecting major U.S. cities like Infinity Stones for its driverless ride hailing service. Nashville, Tennessee was just added a few days ago, joining Denver, Colorado, and San Diego California. Now there's another new city on the list: Las Vegas.
Soon, you'll be able to hail a ride in a Waymo Ojai, the company's Zeekr-built, four-passenger driverless van all throughout Vegas. You can get rides to casinos, major venues like the Sphere or Allegiant Stadium, or your local neighborhood. There are likely geographic restrictions, and Waymos don't always start out going on highways, but we don't know full details yet. And it seems like the city will be helping Waymo expand its capabilities as much as possible.
“The public rollout of Waymo's all-electric autonomous ride-hailing brings technology directly to our municipal streets, helping residents and patrons travel seamlessly between the cultural districts and neighborhood centers," said Las Vegas Mayor Shelley Berkley. "By investing in cleaner, safer urban mobility, we ensure the City of Las Vegas remains an accessible, vibrant, and forward-looking community."
Waymo Lyft Nashville
However, Vegas seems like the perfect place for a driverless Waymo. It's a city designed to wow you with big lights and impressive technical achievements. A driverless cab dropping you off at your casino will probably feel very at home in the same city that has what is essential a giant ball stadium made out of customizable screens and a replica Eiffel Tower.
Waymo is wasting no time expanding its operation, and likely won't stop anytime soon. There are plenty more cities on its expansion list, so don't be surprised if you see a Waymo near you soon.

title: “三巨头”联手，OpenAI、Anthropic、谷歌 Deepmind 开始合作研究 AI 安全措施
content:
IT之家 9 月 15 日消息，随着美国各界对 AI 可能威胁经济和国家安全的担忧不断升温，OpenAI 开始与主要竞争对手 Anthropic 和谷歌 DeepMind 合作研究 AI 安全措施，进一步推动行业共同应对潜在风险。
据彭博社今天（15 日）晚间报道，OpenAI 全球政策主管克里斯 · 莱恩透露，公司与 Anthropic 和谷歌围绕 AI 安全问题的接触持续了数周。OpenAI 认为，三家公司开展这类协调并不需要专门获得反垄断豁免。“尝试合作、优先保障安全，对大家都更好。”
当地时间上周六，Anthropic CEO 达里奥 · 阿莫迪发表了一篇 3800 词的长文，呼吁放缓最先进 AI 系统的研发，让研究人员有更多时间了解潜在威胁，也让 AI 生存风险迅速进入公众讨论。OpenAI CEO 萨姆 · 奥尔特曼和 SpaceXAI 负责人埃隆 · 马斯克很快对阿莫迪的主张表达支持。
Anthropic、谷歌 DeepMind 的发言人没有立即回应置评请求。
莱恩认为，企业为了安全开展合作并不罕见，航空业就是一个例子。“长期以来，企业为了提高安全性而相互帮助的情况很多。”
IT之家从报道中获悉，此次前往华盛顿期间，莱恩还计划与美国议员会面。他补充说，OpenAI 愿意支持两党提出、旨在防范 AI 潜在灾难性风险的方案。“只要能推动通过，我们都支持。”

title: 中文互联网基础语料 4.0 发布：数据量 120GB，为大模型训练和 AI 发展提供可信数据支撑
content:
IT之家 9 月 15 日消息，据中国网络空间安全协会官方公众号，9 月 15 日（今天）下午，在济南召开的 2026 年国家网络安全宣传周人工智能安全治理分论坛上，中文互联网基础语料 4.0 正式向社会发布，数据量 120GB，并在“中文互联网语料资源平台”上线。
据IT之家了解，用户登录中国网络空间安全协会官网（点此前往），点击“中文互联网语料资源平台”链接，通过注册、认证等程序，即可下载或联系获取相关数据。
在中央网信办指导下，中国网络空间安全协会联合国家互联网应急中心，会同百度、中科闻歌、开普云、拓尔思、科大讯飞、知乎等单位，在前期发布中文互联网基础语料 1.0、2.0 和 3.0 的基础上，依托网安协会人工智能安全治理专委会建立的语料共建共享机制，汇聚一批新的高质量可信数据，经过一系列严格细致的数据加工处理措施，形成并对社会发布中文互联网基础语料 4.0，数据量 120GB，为大模型训练和人工智能发展提供可信数据支撑。
网安协会负责人表示，中文互联网基础语料 4.0 是社会各界协同共建高质量中文语料的重要阶段性成果，进一步丰富了国内高质量中文语料供给体系。下一步，协会将继续联合国家互联网应急中心等单位，联动各行业领域深化中文互联网基础语料建设，持续为人工智能产业高质量发展筑牢数据底座。
广告声明：文内含有的对外跳转链接（包括不限于超链接、二维码、口令等形式），用于传递更多信息，节省甄选时间，结果仅供参考，IT之家包含外链的文章均包含本声明。
