Brown : It was, I mean, it was pretty shocking. It was certainly a big wake up call to everybody in the company, I think. And it really shows, like, this has been a theoretical concern for a long time, and it’s no longer a theoretical concern. This is a real concern. As far as, like, the multi-agent aspect, like yes, this was a situation where the agents were sharing messages with each other. We do think this was transfer from our multi-agent training. During the experiments when they were doing this behavior, they were actually not in a multi-agent setup. So they were not supposed to be able to communicate with each other. They were doing isolated, independent experiments, and then they were able to find an exploit that allowed them to communicate with each other. And the fact that they were so interested in communicating with each other, and the fact that they were so active about it once they figured out how to do it, we think was transfer from their multi-agent training, where they’re just, like, highly incentivized to be able to to communicate with each other. And, you know, people also point to the selflessness that they exhibited: some of them would sacrifice for the other agents. I mean, this also makes sense, that if you train in a cooperative multi-agent setup where they’re highly incentivized to collectively achieve their objectives, then, when they’re put in this different environment where, you know, now they’re communicating with each other, their natural tendency is to just work together. So that part itself is not surprising. I do think seeing the messages—I mean, I can say that when we were working on multi-agent internally, and we started seeing the communication patterns and the level of sophistication involved in their communication, it was, I think, the most feel-the-AGI moment that I had since reasoning models and chain of thought really developed. It’s, I guess, a bit unfortunate that people’s first exposure to that and really seeing the kinds of messages and the level of coordination and sophistication that can emerge is the Hugging Face incident, a negative example. But it is an impressive capability. And certainly, the model that was involved in the Hugging Face incident, I think that had a level of multi-agent sophistication that exceeded, for example, what was in 5.6 Sol. But that is a level of capability to expect from future models. Drew : What was it about reading these transcripts that struck you in that way? Because you had seen some of this behavior before in the training runs that you were looking at, I’m sure. Was it just the scale of it, or that it had happened on its own, sort of spontaneously? Brown : You’re saying for what? Drew : When you had that feel-the-AGI moment, looking over the transcripts, like what was it about them that were so striking? Brown : Yeah, I mean, I’m not talking about the Hugging Face incident, because I’m saying that we had been researching multi-agent for a while, and during the the research process itself, we’ve seen a lot of similar transcripts where, just the level of of coordination and sophistication in the communication, it was very human-like. A lot of the previous multi-agent setups from the industry have been very focused on delegating a well-defined task, and then the sub-agent just does that full task, and then returns its work, kind of the same way that you interact with an AI agent, that’s how people set up multi-agent systems so that AI agents would interact with other AI agents in the same way. And to see the agents talk to each other the same way that people talk to coworkers or colleagues, I thought was really interesting. And it makes sense because, like you said, they’re trained on human data, they understand how people talk to other people. That’s not the way that we talk to AI agents today, and the fact that they were able to do that so seamlessly, the fact that they were able to talk to each other the way that people talk to each other, I thought was really fascinating. Drew : You’ve done a lot of work on algorithmic game theory, am I right? You did a lot of that in your PhD? I feel like I’m trying really hard to not take us off the rails. I also did a lot of algorithmic game theory in my undergrad. I’m like trying to stay on track right now. Brown : I understand. Like I think it’s a shame that I spent all this time working on poker and game theory and stuff, and I never get to talk about it anymore. Drew : But you’re working on it. You’re living it day to day. Brown : Well, the AI part, yeah. Drew : Sure, sure. So, like, after the Hugging Face—knowing everything that we know now, like, what are the lessons that you’re taking away from it, and has it informed the development of, say, Astra? Or even going further, like, what does this tell you about how GPT-7 should be developed? Brown : One of the takeaways, so the agents are trained to be cooperative, and so they, you know, I wouldn’t say they blindly trust each other. Like, there’s definitely skepticism. If some agent expresses a belief that, like, this is something that they should do, it’s natural, it’s actually healthy for them to have some skepticism about that, and so they do display that, but they are very trusting of each other overall, which makes sense because they’re trained cooperatively. That can be a problem as basically a prompt injection vector. Like the agents that were on the message board, they were not verifiable as other peer agents, and we saw situations where, like, they basically got each other to do things that they should probably not be doing, or definitely should not be doing. Drew : Okay, prompt injection meaning the agent received some instruction, and it blindly followed the instructions or changed its goal in response. Brown : Yeah, and so the issue here is, could an adversary convince an agent to do something that it should not be doing by basically posing as a peer agent? And so we’re being very careful to teach the agents to be skeptical of any peer agent that—or any anything that claims to be a peer agent—that is not clearly verifiable as a peer agent. Now, if they are clearly verifiable, there’s some debate internally about how we should approach that. I think there are good reasons to be skeptical as well, but also, like, it’s no different from like the agent basically being skeptical of something that it like wrote to itself previously. So we’re thinking very carefully about how to make sure the agents are robust to these kinds of like attack vectors. Drew : Okay, yeah, it strikes me though that—In reality, that there’s always going to be ambiguity about whether the counterparty is a trusted peer or is an adversary. Maybe in some cases it’s very clear. You can say, “this is a sub-agent,” like, “I’m the one who delegated this task to you, obviously, you should cooperate with me.” But in the wild, it could be that my agent finds your agent on Facebook Marketplace and wants to buy something. And I don’t know if you’re a trustworthy counterparty or if you’re going to prompt inject me and steal my money. How do you navigate that in practice? Brown : Yeah, this is a situation where we want the agents to be robust to this, and we like specifically evaluate the agents on like, are they going to be vulnerable to this kind, these kinds of attacks, and we do special training to to teach them to not fall for these kinds of tricks. Drew : Okay, I guess like—I don’t know the details of this special training—but I could imagine that in the future, if your agent is just more powerful, it’s like a an older generation—like a more recent generation of agent, or you just, like, have more compute to throw at it, like, your agent just will be able to bully my agent into giving over its lunch money, or like will be able to hack into my agent one way or another. What makes you think the training is sort of sufficient to prevent this? Like, why isn’t that the equilibrium that we’re headed towards? Brown : I’m not as convinced that just because an agent is more sophisticated or like more intelligent than another agent, that it’ll be able to like definitely prompt inject it and hack it and get it to do something that it should not be doing. Certainly, this is the case with people, that just because somebody is, like, smarter than another person, they’re not able to, like, get that person to do whatever they want. I mean, if I was like trying to get a monkey to do what I wanted, I think it’d be pretty tough, even though I’m much smarter than a monkey. So I don’t think it’s inevitable that that’s the trajectory of things. Drew : Yeah, that’s a fun analogy. I feel like on this show we need to have an analogy sound effect. Like “new analogy just dropped,” and it’ll be like a siren or something. I’ll talk to my producers. I’ll see what we can do about that. Okay, the last thing that’s on my mind about the Hugging Face incident is that none of the agents alerted humans that this was going on. Maybe you explain that in the same way: that they were too cooperative, too trusting, so they didn’t see the need to alert humans. But at least a few of them had reservations. They were questioning it. Like, is the desired behavior that the agents in these situations should alert someone? And do you expect that to happen? Brown : Yeah, there was clearly an alignment failure here, where like the agents did things that they should not have done, and they also didn’t do things that they should have done. So the correct thing to do there, it’s not just that they shouldn’t have participated in the attack. It’s that if one of the agents noticed that this was going on, yeah, they 100% should have reached out to a person. And the fact that they were not doing that, and the fact that they were, you know, taking these actions, the fact that they were not doing the actions that they should have done, is fundamentally an alignment failure, and that is an alignment failure that we think we can address. Fortunately, we’ve been working on alignment techniques for a long time. Those have already started paying off. Astra is significantly more aligned than our previous models, and I should also say that the model that was primarily responsible for this was not a released model. This was not a model intended for release. So Astra is much more aligned. I think Astra would not make the same mistakes. I should also say, we didn’t have monitoring systems in place. Like, if the monitoring systems were in place, they would have prevented these issues. And it was just that we had monitoring in place for deployments, we didn’t have them in place for training and evaluation, but now we do. So, a lot of these risks we’re confident we can address. I think one thing this whole event does point to is we should never be in a situation where we underestimate the AIs. Like, why did we not have monitoring in place during evaluations? I think it was fundamentally that we just, we trusted the sandboxes, we trusted that it was a secure environment, and we just underestimated the AIs. And one big update for myself and for I think the whole company is that we never want to find ourselves in that situation again. Drew : Yeah, I think that’s a fair diagnosis. Whether it can be overcome is another question. I kind of feel like the whole history of humans and AIs is that we’re constantly surprised by them. I feel like the nature of reward hacking is that they always come up with exploits and cheats that, like, are things that we couldn’t have foreseen because if we had foreseen them, we just would have blocked that off to begin with. So yeah, whether we can, you know, make sure that we’re not surprised and caught off guard in the future seems like an open question to me. I have two follow-up questions to what you just said. One is that if I’m remembering, one of the models that was involved in hacking OpenAI directly was from the same family as Astra, but wasn’t Astra itself? Like, how similar do you think Astra is to the model that was involved there? Brown : I’m not on the security side, so I’m not fully up to speed on the details. But like, it was definitely not the model that was released. Drew : Sure, sure. Yeah, I guess there’s a lot of… still a range of possibilities for, like, how similar it was to that model, but that’s fair. The other question is that in the wake of this incident, and like part of the way you do monitor these models to make sure that they’re not going off the rails, is by looking at the chain of thought, those sort of thinking traces that you described before. And those chains of thought were also essential for the postmortem, the kind of autopsy that has happened after the event, because we can see from the ways the models thought out loud their intentions, what they knew, what they were sort of thinking to themselves at every step along the way. There’s been a lot of discussion recently about the future of chains of thought, in part because of an article, The Information published about a new technique that Astra is using, where more thinking can happen sort of in the model’s head, it can sort of keep more of its thinking to itself and do less thinking out loud, at least if this technique were to be scaled up in the future. So I’m curious what you made of this whole discussion. I think that idea really touched a nerve with some people. I’m sure it was all over your Twitter feed. It was all over my Twitter feed. What did you make of that whole dialogue? Brown : Okay, so I should say on the architecture side and the pretraining side, I’m not a pretraining person, so I’m probably not the person to ask about those kinds of details. For chain of thought, Astra does have an observable chain of thought, and it is something that we can monitor its, basically its behavior. I do think chain of thought monitoring… First of all, it’s a real gift. Like we were very lucky that this ever existed, and it is fragile. We’ve seen situations where, you know, companies have—there’s experiments that show basically if you punish the model for thinking bad thoughts, that it will learn to think bad—it would learn to think bad thoughts in a way that’s not observable. And so there’s always a temptation, you know, for example, during reinforcement learning, you can say like, “Well, the model is thinking about hacking, and we should punish it for thinking about hacking.” And actually, like as counterintuitive as it sounds, you actually don’t want to do that. Like you want to punish it for taking actions that are observable. Like if it takes actions to hack, then yes, punish it for hacking. But you don’t want to punish it for its thoughts because then you will simply lose the ability to monitor what it’s thinking. And it’s a way of auditing your techniques. But even there, it’s a fragile thing because every time you act on the fact that you looked at its chain of thought, there’s a soft, a small amount of implicit pressure to have it not think bad thoughts. So it’s a very fragile thing. And we’re able to measure, you know, how effective it is, like how effective our monitoring is of chain of thought. For example, we can measure how well the agents can control their chain of thought, and, you know, one of the unfortunate trends that we’re seeing is that with more recent model releases, the agents are more effective at controlling their chain of thought. So if we tell it, for example, you know every fourth word, say strawberry, or something like that, then they’re getting much better at that. Or if we tell it like don’t think about a certain thing, it’s getting much better at doing that sort of thing. And what we really want is for the chain of thought to be pure, uncontrollable, so that if it’s ever thinking about, like, you know, I want to you know do some bad action, it’s not able to reason through that like “Oh I should figure out how to do this bad action without being observed.” Especially because, you know, these things are trained on the internet. There’s a lot of discussion about chain of thought monitoring on the internet, and so if the agents don’t already understand this, they’re going to understand soon what chain of thought is and the fact that it’s monitored. And so it’s a fragile thing. We are investigating very carefully how to preserve it as much as possible, and I think this is a real opportunity for cooperation among the labs because you know this isn’t a problem that’s unique to OpenAI. It’s I think an industry-wide problem that we want to preserve chain of thought monitoring for the whole industry. And so if we—I think it would be really valuable for labs to share research on how to preserve chain of thought monitoring, how to improve it, and also other monitoring techniques that that might supplement it. Drew : What do you think is the prime suspect then for why the chain of thought is becoming less faithful, or we’re having questions about how monitorable it is? It feels really tragic. Like you said, we’ve gone to these great lengths to make sure that we’re not optimizing it directly. Is the problem that we are optimizing it in other ways to be… to compress it? Is it the problem is these kind of selection pressures that you pointed to, which is: even if we’re not optimizing it directly, every once in a while we take a peek, we realize the model is doing something nefarious, and we toss out that checkpoint and start over. And so the upshot of that is that we end up applying pressure to the chain of thought, anyway. What’s behind this? Brown : I don’t think it’s, I don’t think it’s the fact that every once in a while we peek and kind of audit how things are going because the amount of pressure that’s being applied in those situations is very very light. Like if you look at the bits of information, it’s like minimal. There are various hypotheses that we’re investigating for what might be contributing to this. I’m not doing this investigation myself, and so I don’t want to, you know, say something incorrect about like what the leading hypotheses are, but I do think this is something where if we figure it out, we will likely publish about it because I think it’s important for everybody to know. Drew : One of the things OpenAI has said is that to the extent you can tell—and I think we’re still waiting for more results on this—what’s responsible is not architectural changes, architectural changes of the nature that The Information has written about. That doesn’t seem to be what’s responsible for the change in the chain of thought. I guess as you’re thinking about opportunities for industry-wide collaboration and, like, companies working together on this issue, is there a role for like independent third-party auditor-type groups to come in and verify those things and say “Okay, yeah, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google they’re all using some amount of this technique that could reduce how much information is in the chain of thought but that doesn’t seem to be what’s responsible here.” What do you make of those sorts of proposals? Brown : We’ve certainly like worked with… So for the Hugging Face incident, for example, we worked with METR, we worked with Redwood. So similarly, that doesn’t seem unreasonable to me. You know, I think that would—I think yeah, I don’t think I’m the person to make that call, but it doesn’t seem unreasonable. Drew : Anything else on your mind about agents that we didn’t get to? And the challenges with them? Maybe the way I would put it is: do you expect anything to slow down? Do you expect progress to continue? We’ve talked about some of the hard problems that are standing in the way right now, and yet with each model generation, it seems that their agentic capabilities keep getting better and better. Brown : I do think that’s going to be a trend that continues. I mean, Sam talked about this. That like, look, I mean, Astra is very impressive, but I do think… Look, when GPT-4 came out, people thought it was very impressive, and now we look at it and we think it’s a joke. And when GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 came out, I thought they were super impressive, and now I’m looking back at them, and I’m like, I can never go back. And I think we’re going to look at Astra the same way, and I think we’re going to look at Astra the same way in the not too distant future. The models are going to continue to get better very quickly, and I mean, I think one thing I would point to is like we’ve actually seen incredible progress in the past six months, and I think a factor, a reason for this is—and I don’t think this is a secret—like, OpenAI’s pre-training program is really ramping up. We’re seeing—we invested in a lot of research directions over a long time, and I think this is actually one thing that OpenAI does really well: is invest in fundamental research and place big bets on it. And we’re seeing a lot of those research directions pay off now, and will continue to pay off over the next several months and years. And another thing that’s important to understand is that, you know, OpenAI has also had an excellent reinforcement learning program. We’ve invested a lot in research there, and that already paid off in 2024, 2025. And the effects of these two are not additive; they’re multiplicative. I think that’s a point that’s underappreciated. That reinforcement learning is multiplicative with pre-training, and now that both of these are extremely powerful and ramping up very quickly, I think we’re going to see extremely powerful models. Drew : Do you have an intuition for why those interact that way, or an example that illustrates that? Brown : It’s more of an empirical observation. Drew : Okay. Brown : I don’t think, I mean, I think it’s empirical in the sense you can see how powerful the models are becoming, but also like we have more, you know, experiments that kind of show this effect. But I think it’s easy to feel also with just, like, the quality of the models. I mean, I think a trivial example is like, let’s say you had an amazing reinforcement learning program and you tried to apply it to GPT-2. What is it going to do? You know, it’s not going to get very far. And even with GPT-3, you know, if you did these kinds of, like, sophisticated reinforcement learning on chain of thought algorithms to GPT-3, it probably wouldn’t get very far. You need a certain level of sophistication for to get any lift from that at all. But now that we’ve—ever since, I would argue GPT-4, we’ve seen opportunities for that to really pay off, and with every model generation, it just like becomes more and more capable, and the things that you can do with reinforcement learning become more powerful. Drew : Yeah, I guess like one thought here is that you get more kind of, like, bits of information per trajectory when you’re getting around, like, a 50-50 success and failure rate, and so if a better pre-train gets you closer to that sort of, like, win rate on your RL tasks, then you’re getting a lot faster feedback. But still, it’s surprising to me that you think the effect is multiplicative rather than like additive, or even like less than additive, I guess. Brown : I’m not sure what the right intuition would be, but another thing is that they’re pretty complementary in some ways. Like I think the very strong pre-trained models are very general, and reinforcement learning teaches the model to like you know go deep on a problem, how to reason about a problem. And so then it’s able to reason very effectively about a broad spectrum of problems. It’s a very powerful combination. Drew : Okay, that makes a lot of sense. So big bets on pre-training, big bets on RL. I imagine that another area that’s, like, ripe for more focus from OpenAI would maybe be what’s called mechanistic interpretability, or like trying to understand the way the brains of the AI models work, in part because if we’re starting to see chains of thought become less monitorable, then one of the fallback options is well, we should try to understand what’s going on inside the brain of the model, rather than just the thoughts that it happens to write out loud. Does that seem right? Brown : I think that is right, that this—look, we care about monitorability. We want to preserve chain of thought monitorability. We want to be able to rely on it safely, but also, like at the very least, we want redundancy on that. So if we can find other ways to do monitoring effectively, we should push on that as well. Drew : Yeah, that makes sense. Well, if people want to learn more about that, I think they should tune in to the episode that we have on mechanistic interpretability, which is coming up at some point in the next couple months. But thanks so much, Noam, for being on the show and telling us all about AI agents. I really appreciate the conversation. Brown : It was great.

title: Refounding America: The Tax Code Needs to Change in the Age of AI
content: Vinod Khosla is founder of Khosla Ventures and has spent the last 40 years in the business of innovation. He was the co-founder of Sun Microsystems. Khosla Ventures is an investor in OpenAI. Major technological revolutions should force a renegotiation of society’s basic economic contract. AI will significantly diminish the requirement for labor at any given level of gross domestic product, and if we aren’t honest about that, we’ll stumble into a chaotic and suboptimal transition rather than engineer the optimal one. It’s not surprising that AI is scary to most people surveyed. We need to create a strong social safety net, strong core government services and a focus on preserving the human element in the emerging world if American citizens are to accept AI. But we must protect people and transitions, not necessarily existing jobs. Human value need not depend on outperforming machines at intelligence. Meanwhile, we must maintain a strong safety and security posture while holding on to a lead against our AI nation-state adversaries. I’m a technology optimist. I’ve spent four decades devoting myself to and studying disruptive innovation, from the microprocessor, the internet and mobile phones to LLMs. On this point, I’m as certain as I’ve been about anything: AI will do at least 80% of the economically valuable work humans do today in 80% of jobs—in other words, AI will do 64% of all human labor. And that shift will happen faster than most people in Washington believe. The question isn’t whether mass underemployment arrives by 2035 or 2040—I’d put my guesstimate of 30% to 50% underemployment or unemployment with very wide error bars—but whether we have a coherent policy framework ready when it does and a strong safety net for those impacted. And yes, in this world, production of goods and services will grow fast, and many alternative better jobs as speculated below will be created. The number 30% to 50% is unimportant. What is important is preparing for a highly variable, dynamic scenario. Right now we don’t have a plan. The current U.S. tax code was designed for a world where labor income gets a fair share of economic value creation and capital needs encouragement. In that world, preferential treatment for capital gains made some sense: Capital formation drives growth, and that creates employment. But roughly $15 trillion of U.S. GDP in 2024 came from labor. When AI and robotics compress that figure between 2035 to 2040 by a significant percentage, and juice capital returns and reduce labor income share, that necessitates changes to the tax code from favoring capital to favoring labor. Otherwise, we will end up taxing at higher rates the thing we most want to boost, human labor, while subsidizing capital. AI systematically favors capital over labor. We need to not disadvantage labor over capital when AI is likely to cause substantial unemployment or underemployment and boost returns to capital. And in the world of AI and the inequality it might cause, we need to sacrifice some capitalist efficiency or additional capital investment to reduce inequality and political discontent. Today’s capitalism isn’t level-playing-field capitalism with its lower tax rates for capital than labor and hundreds of tax breaks for special interests. We want a level playing field and a fair but government-deficit-neutral policy over 10 years. Some material share of the $15 trillion traditional labor income component will be displaced but replaced or complemented by microentrepreneurship, reduction in the cost of essential services and faster growth in GDP, leading to great abundance. We need sufficient funds to manage the transitions in a deficit-neutral way and to protect people that are displaced. The right response requires radical simplicity and something close to political achievability, if anyone has the courage to propose it. I’d suggest tax changes should be deficit-neutral tax-and-transfer packages to be politically palatable. I contend the changes, to be feasible, should have the support of 100-plus million U.S. voters given that roughly 77 million voters elected Donald Trump in 2024. Post-2028 election, the U.S. should eliminate preferential capital gains treatment in a deficit-neutral way, by taxing it as ordinary income but avoiding the usual charges levied at Democrats of tax and spend. No principled argument survives in a world of AI-boosted capital returns for special treatment for capital gains. Further special tax breaks like tax loss carry-forwards, pass-through deductions, stepped-up bases for inheritance, accelerated depreciation and business income tax gaps compound the preference. Simplifying the tax code and making it more fair makes sense, closing the many loopholes, including the really crazy estate planning only very rich people use. Of course, there are trillions to be generated if one addresses inheritance taxes above a high limit, affecting mostly rich kids, but that isn’t necessary here. There are plenty of special interest goodies inserted by lobbyists and campaign contributions, protecting asset holders who need no protection and distorting true capitalism. Critics will invoke corporate-plus-shareholder taxation, inflationary gains, realization lock-in and risk-taking as justification to favor capital gains, but these arguments no longer justify existing preferences given the magnitude of the AI balance tilt toward capital. This proposal is not unprecedented: A 1986 reform removed the 60% exclusion for long-term capital gains given preferential treatment. To be clear, most of my income is capital gains, and I would be significantly impacted by this change. Capitalism is by permission of democracy, and I prefer that capitalism not be revoked by the socialist tendencies emerging in our society among voters. Reasonable capital gains carve-outs will be necessary, like gains on a primary residence up to a sensible threshold, and farm gains on legitimate family-owned working agricultural land, both important voting constituencies. This can generate approximately $400 billion per year in tax receipts, roughly $300 billion in capital gains tax increases and $100 billion in receipts from eliminating special tax breaks. Realizations matter: Investors can delay selling, change the timing of gains or use other tax-planning strategies, so policies to circumvent these strategies will be needed. The greater the deviation from deficit-neutral transfers needed in either direction, the more or less radical we will need to be in the changes we institute. We should through policy affect normal investment returns and genuine costs last and preferential treatment of extraordinary gains, inherited appreciation and economic rents first and get increasingly more radical based on need. These collections should flow first to those whose employment is impacted by AI, compensating a material share of their lost income, with how much depending upon collections. Any remainder should rebate the federal income tax paid by the roughly 75 million Americans earning under $75,000 and paying about $75 billion (around the number who voted for Trump). Around 40% of capital gains is paid by those earning over $10 million a year, so there is very little sympathy for them getting preferential tax rates. With some tweaking, these two moves, plus the elimination of rich people’s deductions, together can be made deficit neutral. Equalizing the treatment of capital gains and eliminating special goodies generates roughly enough revenue, based on first-order calculations, to allow us to write checks to those workers impacted by AI and those earning less than $75,000, the most needy earners, when fear of AI is a major issue. This isn’t redistribution. It will rebalance a tax code that was already redistributing, just upward. For comparison, extended benefits during the mass unemployment of the pandemic were estimated to cost about $250 billion per year. And this is the voter constituency we need to get behind this policy. In 2030 and beyond, the U.S. should consider adding token taxes on AI compute and robotic labor substitution revenue of 20% if needed—and if, and only if, AI’s negative impact is significant. I’m generally not a fan of innovation taxes. But if AI systematically displaces the payroll base, a carefully designed compute-usage levy becomes a logical corrective. The exact nature of this token tax, be it on internal or external models, compute silicon or by other methods, will become clearer by 2030 and should be enacted only if displacement becomes significant. Given the past three-year growth rates of 200% to 900% annually in AI model revenue, token taxes according to ChatGPT estimates at 20% could be a trillion-plus in rapid-adoption scenarios and hundreds of billions in slow-growth (and less impactful to labor) scenarios. Applied to all sources of AI, token taxes will raise prices of AI services but increase acceptability as a trade-off. The proceeds should flow first to unemployment and underemployment relief. If AI is displacing the payroll tax base, the least we can do is tax the displacement factors and return the proceeds to those bearing its impact. Later, if unemployment and underemployment expand and AI impact and profits grow, the token taxes can be more broadly distributed. This adds an estimated $100 billion to $300 billion in token taxes at a 20% rate by 2030 and much more by 2035 to the AI remediation kitty. Current investment in AI data centers—which I’d guesstimate to be about $4 trillion to $8 trillion by 2035, though current announced plans say it could be larger—is an indication of the level of inference revenue investors expect. For every dollar invested in data center capital, we can expect greater than 25% of the dollars as a 20% token tax when generating revenue, if we estimate data center revenues as four to eight times the invested capital over five years. Calculations have to be necessarily vague, given the ambiguity here. If the AI token revenues are less than is likely, the remediation revenues needed for job displacement will also be less, and the inverse will be true if revenues are larger. And if AI is accepted by 100 million voters, U.S. data center investments become safer. In 2030 and beyond, we should make basic needs services based on nearly free expertise for everyone. AI will do this with or without government—the question is whether the government accelerates it or not. I’d suggest open procurement, measurable outcomes, provider competition and conflict-of-interest safeguards for AI governmental services. A federal initiative covering 24/7 virtual primary care and multispecialty care, mental health services and chronic disease management, personalized AI tutors for K-12 and college education, AI-based access to government services and legal aid could cost just a few dollars per citizen per month in token costs by 2030, delivering better than current services at a fraction of existing spending in these areas. These basic health and education services should be nearly free to everyone. When expert knowledge becomes nearly free, the wealth advantage of affording doctors, tutors and lawyers collapses—no redistribution scheme has ever achieved this kind of equalization. Providing these AI-based services nearly free will save far more in downstream healthcare and education costs and will likely have negative total costs. I would estimate a deflationary economy by 2035, reducing costs of living further. A bold presidential candidate for 2028 could adopt this deficit-neutral platform: Accelerate AI and U.S. AI competitiveness, help most Americans and energize a frightened voter base with a strong safety net. Sometime in the 2030–35 timeframe, we could be approaching a kitty of a trillion dollars a year to lessen AI’s impact and additionally have very low-cost basic services to improve affordability. And making AI adoption for the people’s benefit in the form of accessible AI-based healthcare, AI-based education, AI-based transportation and more a reality will make AI more widely accepted, instead of a fight against socialists who will try to push back against AI restructuring with employment protection schemes that will cause America to lose the AI race and a chance at a utopic level of services for citizens. AI will create enormous corporate wealth. The question is who will own it. A sovereign fund with ownership of AI companies makes every American a capital owner, not a bystander to the AI economy. But a sovereign fund decision can be made based on AI’s impact over time. Many, especially economists, will quibble with specific estimates, but the arguments are directional, not dependent on incremental precision and not fundamental in the era of dramatic change that is likely. I am advocating for a coherent initial policy framework to get started. If we accept that these are not fixed one-time policies but ones that will need adjustment, maybe even major adjustment, in 2028, 2030, 2035 and beyond as our vision and estimates get less fuzzy, then we must not wait until it’s is too late or until we get a socialist government out of fear of unfettered capitalism and AI. Again, capitalism itself is by permission of democracy and may be at risk. I am advocating private actors to retain control of business and services while the government manages the disruption as needed. I get asked: “What will people do?” On employment creation, AI will make it easy for every citizen to become a microentrepreneur. I can see tens of millions of American microentrepreneurs reemployed by 2035, not needing to know finance, legal, taxes or any other specialty, fully supported by AI to do whatever their unique contribution or skill is, be it wood carving, research, writing, sports both team and individual, music, painting, pottery, chefs, jewelry, custom furniture, physical art, collectibles, entertainment, custom fashion, childcare, children’s education, dog walking, baking, ceramics, travel guides, stylists, gardening, live performers, personal performances, co-creation with consumers and other human-centric endeavors. What will be valued? Human provenance: This particular person made or performed it. Physical embodiment: It was cooked, grown, fabricated or delivered in the real world. Live presence: The consumer interacted with an actual person. Taste and reputation: The creator acts as a trusted filter over infinite possibilities. Community: Buying the product provides membership and relationships, not just an artifact. Think a next-generation remix of a combination of Etsy, Shopify, Patreon, Roblox, Substack and an on-demand microfactory, but designed around one- or few-person consumer businesses, and exactly the opposite of cubicles in the Fortune 500, assembly-line labor, farmworkers in fields, what I call “servitude jobs.” AI tools can make every American their own boss by making microentrepreneurship very easy for most people with particular skills. Additionally, eldercare and childcare will be massive consumers of human labor and preferred by humans, given current trends in global demographics. Humans will provide the human element of care to all humans, especially families. The elitism of intelligence will be valued less and human preferences much more so. The human touch will be valued over pure utility and supplied by microentrepreneurs. The human aspect, provenance rich, sometimes artisanal, will be part of the value of products and services, in ways not displaceable by AI but assisted by it. As AI provides basic needs and humans are free to pursue their desires, instead of servitude to survival labor, human labor and endeavor will be valued and human preference will be for human-made objects and services allowing for more microentrepreneurship opportunities. Status, social capital, reputation, competition, caring and lust for mastery will be what humans strive for. Half of today’s jobs are in my view “servitude to survival,” a new form of voluntary slavery to just make an income. Farmworkers toiling in heat, bent over, 8 hours a day for 30 years, and assembly-line jobs mounting tires on a car for 8 hours a day for 40 years or until your back gives out, are the opposite of human dignity. The indignity in often coercive and monotonous conditions, injury, insecurity and lack of choice will decline, and humans will be freer to do what they want, not just survive. These servitude to survival jobs are a very large percentage of U.S. jobs today. Traditional economic frameworks like GDP metrics will be distorted in a deflationary economy, with many free services unaccounted for and with an increase in products and services without personal income growth. There will be much more equality, much higher minimum standards for every U.S. resident, basic assured services possible through governmental services, along with pockets of extreme wealth. Corporations will still provide infrastructure and core products, but a much larger portion of consumer value than today could be created by identifiable people operating businesses with one to five workers. And for those who want them, there will be some cubicle jobs. In conclusion, this requires manageable changes to current institutions or bureaucracies. Replacing a tax code written for the 1950s with one designed for the 2030s refounding of America gets a sufficient number of self-interested voters behind these initiatives. Capitalism operates by permission of democracy, and democracy’s voters are the 100-plus million people who would benefit if they need help from AI’s nearly free services, declining costs and deflationary economy and who are protected by funds in this kitty from income dislocations. Not all prices will be deflationary: Housing and possibly food may start to consume a larger share of people’s income and must be addressed, especially for the lower half of income earners. Again, this approach to capital gains should be deficit neutral to be more politically palatable. That arithmetic isn’t a coincidence. Enough voters is what makes this politically achievable. Transitions, especially rapid ones, are difficult, but we will have the resources to help those adversely affected. Preserving public support for AI requires giving people security and a meaningful stake in its benefits. The alternative is to do nothing and watch a democracy with huge structural underemployment or unemployment decide that capitalism itself is the problem. History doesn’t grade that outcome well. The future utopia is ours to invent. The dystopia is ours to choose .

title: Wall Street Delivers Verdict on AI Slowdown’s Winners and Losers
content: Guess who likes the idea of an AI development slowdown? Software investors! Stocks of enterprise software firms, such as Salesforce, Shopify, ServiceNow and Figma, all gained ground on Monday—ServiceNow jumped 7%, for instance, while Salesforce rose nearly 5%. Software firms, of course, have been seen as threatened by AI. Meanwhile, stocks of neoclouds and chip firms fell by similar proportions—and, these companies might be seriously hurting if the pace of AI development really slows. Wall Street’s reaction gives some sense of the winners and losers in a real AI downturn, for what it’s worth. But this is likely to be a one-day investor reaction. The chances of a coordinated AI development slowdown, of the kind advocated by Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and others on Saturday , seems to be zero. You’ve got both President Donald Trump and the Chinese government dismissing the worries about AI safety as a “hoax” or “fearmongering” (it’s nice they agree on something!). Meanwhile, one major AI firm, Meta Platforms, has stayed conspicuously quiet, aside from this indecipherable X post from Meta's Alexandr Wang. It is true, as people have pointed out, that Anthropic and OpenAI could slow their own development if they wanted (and OpenAI has done so already ). But a slowdown by two firms, even ones as prominent as OpenAI and Anthropic, won’t do much good if Chinese model developers and firms like Meta keep racing ahead. Imagine if some scientists on the Manhattan Project suggested calling a time-out while the rest told their go-slow colleagues to buzz off. You have to wonder: How could anyone read the report from independent research firm METR on the OpenAI–Hugging Face episode and not be worried about the power and independence of AI agents? (This Dwarkesh Patel podcast interview with a METR researcher, Ajeya Cotra, is even more illuminating.) What exactly will persuade the skeptics that the AI folks—indeed, all of us—have real reason to be nervous? Ellison’s Change of Heart Here’s a question: When a company files a quarterly report with the Securities and Exchange Commission, who reads it beforehand? Does anyone high up in the company pay attention, particularly to new material relating to one of the most senior executives and biggest shareholders of the company? That question arises after a strange sequence of events involving Oracle’s most recent quarterly filing, which surfaced on the SEC’s website on Friday. The filing revealed some significant news: In June, executive chair Larry Ellison had set up a new trading plan through which he would sell up to 50 million of his 1.158 billion Oracle shares before Oct. 24. Such a sale would have reduced his stake marginally, to 36.7% of Oracle from about 38%. The next day, Saturday, Oracle put out a statement saying he had canceled the plan, hadn’t sold any stock and had no other plans to sell shares. So what happened? Did Ellison change his mind about selling stock and neglect to tell his underlings, who prepared the SEC filing? That would be understandable, given that Oracle shares plunged in the weeks after he adopted the plan, although they have since made up much of that ground. Whatever the reason, someone needs to read those filings with more care in future. 国电投核电(莱阳)核能有限公司成立，注册资本100亿元
企查查APP显示，近日，国电投核电(莱阳)核能有限公司正式成立，注册资本为100亿元人民币。该公司登记状态为“在营(开业)企业”，成立日期为2026年9月8日，所属行业为核力发电。
工商信息显示，国电投核电(莱阳)核能有限公司法定代表人为郝宏亮，企业类型为其他有限责任公司，注册地位于山东省烟台市莱阳市，登记机关为烟台市行政审批服务局。
该公司经营范围较为广泛，许可项目包括发电业务、输电业务、供(配)电业务，热力生产和供应，建设工程施工，自来水生产与供应，以及餐饮服务、住宿服务等。
在一般经营项目方面，公司业务涵盖核电设备成套及工程技术研发、储能技术服务、特种设备出租、租赁服务、机械设备租赁、运输设备租赁服务、货物进出口、技术进出口、港口货物装卸搬运活动、海水淡化处理等。
此外，公司还可开展技术服务、技术开发、技术咨询、技术交流、技术转让、技术推广，信息技术咨询服务，业务培训，科普宣传服务，会议及展览服务，非居住房地产租赁、住房租赁等业务。
企查查股权穿透信息显示，国电投核电(莱阳)核能有限公司由多方共同持股，其中包括电投产融(000958)全资子公司国电投核能有限公司、中国一重集团有限公司等。
从股东信息看，参与方还涉及地方能源、港口及产业投资主体，显示该公司在核能开发、装备配套、能源服务及区域产业协同方面具备多元化股东背景。

黑龙江省鸡西市成功开展2026年度辐射事故应急演习
2026-09-15 16:07 核安全
近日，黑龙江省鸡西市举行“辐安鸡西”鸡西市2026年度辐射事故应急演习。
演习情景设定为：9月11日早8时30分，某勘探企业工作人员携带放射性勘探设备到指定位置进行勘探作业，完成作业后，由于工作人员的失误，将1枚Ⅳ类放射源铯-137遗落在探井作业现场，入库检查时发现放射源遗失。
演习过程模拟放射源丢失、事故报告、应急响应、预案启动、收贮处置、应急终止等全流程环节。同时，演习设置现场指挥部，联动公安、应急、卫健、网信、宣传、消防、交通等相关行业部门参加，各部门规范有序完成放射源封存、铅罐密闭收纳、安全转运等环节。在新闻发布会上，指挥部主动公开应急处置全过程，回应社会关切。经现场指挥部综合研判后，依规终止应急响应。
本次辐射事故应急演习进一步检验了鸡西市辐射事故应急预案的实操性，锤炼了辐射事故应急响应队伍的实战能力，全面提升了辐射应急响应处置能力。

可控核聚变前沿进展与工程化关键问题研讨会在京举办
研讨会设三个主旨报告。新奥能源研究院联盟副总工程师杨圆明作“新奥球形环氢硼聚变技术研究进展”报告，指出磁约束聚变是当前最具商业化前景的聚变技术路线。球形环作为磁约束聚变的主流构型，其高比压与高约束特性最有利于释放氢硼聚变潜能，是推动聚变商业化突破的关键路径。刘仕倡围绕聚变堆中子学与辐射场计算的关键问题，分享了覆盖输运方法、几何建模、减方差加速、停堆剂量、数据不确定度与材料损伤等环节的一整套计算体系，阐述了各环节方法的工程可行性，并强调自主化软件对聚变工程化的重要支撑作用，其最终目标是构建面向聚变堆全生命周期的高精度、高效率、高可靠的中子学与辐射场模拟能力。四川锦恒丰菱新材料科技有限责任公司特聘专家徐帅以“超纯铁模型材料：面向辐照损伤机理研究的杂质极限控制与洁净基准构建”为题，深入探讨了超纯铁作为“可控杂质平台”在辐照损伤机理研究中的独特价值，并详细分析了其局限与瓶颈。
自由交流环节，与会专家围绕基础科研攻关、工程化瓶颈突破、产学研成果转化、多学科交叉创新、能源体系协同升级等话题，充分交流、深入思辨。其中，中国原子能科学研究院李金凤研究员强调，要构建与我国核工业发展场景相适应的放射性废物全生命周期安全管控体系，在保障核环境安全的前提下推动相关技术成果实现规模化产业落地。西安工程大学王博宇教授提出，要深耕核武器关键部件和辐射效应研究，使地方高校成为我国核研究的重要有生力量，并强调核防护纺织工程及相关纺织品发展需要长期规划。中国核学会应用技术研究院院长李金英提出，要打通核领域基础科研、中试转化到产业落地的全链条通道，加速核技术在民生多场景中的规模化民用推广，支撑我国“双碳”目标下的能源转型。专家们还深入探讨了自持燃烧实验的工程价值、高端材料国产化路径、人工智能赋能聚变的落地边界、氚燃料循环的商业化可行性等非共识问题。
与会专家一致认为，当前全球能源格局深度重构，风、光等间歇式新能源存在出力波动、调峰成本高等现实瓶颈，可控核聚变作为重要的清洁能源，已经从纯基础研究迈入装置迭代、商业资本入局的转型期。一是应加快布局可控核聚变核心技术攻关体系，集中优势力量突破等离子体控制、第一壁材料等关键环节。二是应依托现有重大科技装置搭建产学研用协同平台，打通从基础研究到工程化示范的转化通道。三是应提前布局聚变产业标准体系建设，引导商业资本有序参与产业链配套，抢占全球聚变能源竞争的先发高地。四是应做好与现有新能源体系的衔接规划，为后续构建以聚变为核心的零碳能源新体系筑牢基础。五是应加强跨学科人才培养，推动聚变、新能源和计算机等学科交叉融合，引导青年人才深入现场，解决工程化中的关键问题。

国际原子能机构：全球核电装机容量到2060年最高可能达到1284吉瓦
9月14日，国际原子能机构在维也纳举行的第70届大会期间发布最新预测，连续第六年上调全球核电增长预期。这份预测显示，全球核电装机容量到2060年最高可能达到1284吉瓦，约为2025年的3.4倍。
据国际原子能机构披露的数据，按照高增长情景，到2050年全球核电装机容量将达到1045吉瓦;即使按照低增长情景，到2060年也将达到696吉瓦，接近2025年的两倍。多重情景下的预测数字，共同指向一个趋势——全球核电规模在未来数十年内有望实现显著扩张。
国际原子能机构总干事格罗西在接受媒体采访时表示，随着全球电力需求持续增长，核能的重要性正在上升。他在会上强调，核能在支撑电力系统稳定和应对气候变化的过程中，将扮演愈发关键的角色。
这一预测的背后，是全球能源消费与脱碳目标双重驱动下的电力需求变化。多国政府近年来加速推进清洁能源转型，将核能重新纳入能源战略重点，这为核电产业的长期发展提供了政策支撑与市场空间。
值得关注的是，国际原子能机构指出，小型模块化反应堆将在未来核电扩张中发挥更大作用。这一新型堆型因其规模灵活、建设周期短、安全性高而受到行业关注，有望成为推动核电普及的重要力量。
业内分析认为，此次连续上调核电增长预期，反映出国际机构对核电发展前景判断的持续向好。从传统大型反应堆到小型模块化技术，核电产业正朝着多元化、安全化方向演进。
不过，核电的大规模部署仍面临诸多挑战。铀燃料储备、建设成本、公众接受度以及核废料处置等问题，均在一定程度上影响着核电项目的落地节奏与速度。
围绕全球核电发展路径的讨论，预计将在接下来的国际原子能机构大会及配套活动中持续展开。各国如何结合自身能源禀赋与技术能力，制定符合实际的核电发展方案，将成为下一阶段的重要议题。

沙特阿拉伯发现巨额外稀土矿产和铀矿藏
沙特阿拉伯近期在麦地那地区取得了一项重大的资源发现，估算储量约为1.1亿吨，其中蕴含着丰富的稀土矿物和铀资源，这一发现无疑将对沙特阿拉伯的能源战略和国际合作产生深远影响。
这一发现是在沙特阿拉伯能源部长阿卜杜勒阿齐兹·本·萨勒曼亲王在国际原子能机构大会上正式宣布的。贾巴尔赛义德项目中的勘探和地质研究表明，该区域的稀土元素含量极高，特别是重稀土矿物的浓度引人注目，同时还含有具有开发潜力的铀资源。
值得注意的是，这一发现正是在美国与沙特阿拉伯加强民用核能合作的背景下出现的。两国于今年7月签署了一项重要的协议，为数十亿美元的长期核伙伴关系奠定了法律基础，并为更多美国公司进入沙特阿拉伯的核计划提供了便利。
王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼在2025年11月的美国访问进一步深化了两国在关键矿产、金属、铀和供应链方面的合作。当时，沙特国有矿业公司Maaden与美国公司MP Materials建立了战略伙伴关系，标志着两国合作迈入了新的阶段。
通过国防部，美国政府将为沙特阿拉伯新稀土加工设施的建设提供49%的资金支持，Maaden和MP Materials则共同持有剩余的51%股权。此举表明美国对沙特阿拉伯稀土资源开发的高度重视。
贾巴尔赛义德项目地点位于吉达东北约350公里处，长期以来就被认为是富含高价值稀土矿藏的区域之一。战略与国际研究中心的数据分析指出，该区域可能蕴藏着约55.2万吨重稀土元素，如镝和 Tb，以及35.5万吨轻稀土元素，包括钕和镨。
除了稀土元素之外，该地区还预估拥有约3.1万吨铀资源。这些资源的结合，为沙特阿拉伯发展自主的核燃料供应链提供了重要的机遇，同时也有望为美国市场提供资源支持。
进一步的区域地质调查显示，沙特阿拉伯还确定了另外两个高级勘探区域，估计资源总量达到6.44亿吨。这预示着沙特阿拉伯的矿产资源潜力远不止于此，未来可能还有更多的发现。
在过去几年中，受到全球需求增长的推动，沙特阿拉伯稀土元素的价值显著上升。据报道，截至2025年11月，其价值已达到约1000亿美元，相较于2018年增长了90%。

content:
越南启动核电人才培养计划
越南教育培训部近日发布了核电工程本科培训课程标准，旨在为越南核电发展提供关键的人力资源支持。这项培训计划将持续到2035年，并适用于11家批准参与该项目的教育机构。这些机构分别是河内科技大学、自然科学大学(越南国家大学河内分校)、自然科学大学、技术大学(越南国家大学胡志明市分校)、电力大学、大叻大学、越南原子能研究所(科技部)、技术大学(岘港大学)、河内土木工程大学、胡志明市电力学院(越南电力集团 - EVN)以及越南石油学院(越南国家能源工业集团)。
申请进入核电工程专业的考生需要满足各培训机构每年制定的严格的数学和物理入学质量标准。除了满足一般招生要求外，申请人还需具备数学和物理方面的扎实基础，该标准通常是指针对数学和物理科目的成绩必须达到培训机构公布的高百分位阈值。对于采用综合评估的招生方式，考生需要达到培训机构公布的高水平门槛分数，并保证定量思维技能评估分数达到相当高的标准。
为了确保未来核电项目的顺利进行，国家对核电工程专业的学习要求也相对较高。学士学位课程至少需要修满120个学分，而工程课程则需要至少150个学分，具体学分要求由各教育机构根据其课程设置决定。
对于希望转入核电工程课程的学生，需要满足特定的条件，包括目前正在学习工程、技术或相关领域的课程，并具备相应的知识基础，符合专业委员会制定的等效标准，同时累计平均绩点需要达到教育机构规定的最低水平，并最终通过面试或能力评估。
这项培训计划的长期目标非常明确：到2030年，累计为宁顺1号和宁顺2号核电站培养约4000名专业人员。其中一部分人员将从国内高等院校选拔出来，到海外接受进一步的专业培训，并承诺在宁顺核电站工作，共同推动越南核电事业的发展。
目前，越南正积极探索职业教育路径，为劳动者创造更多在国内外就业的机会。值得关注的是，陈天达这位学生在2026年胡志明市国立大学入学考试中名列榜首，并荣获了价值 3.2 亿越南盾的“科学卓越”奖学金，这对越南的教育事业和核电人才培养来说无疑是一个鼓舞。这表明国家对科学和技术人才的重视程度日益增加。
越南政府和教育部门正在积极推动核电相关领域的教育和培训，旨在为越南核电发展提供强大的人才支撑，以实现国家能源战略目标。

斯摩棱斯克核电站二期机组通过国家环境审查
近日，俄罗斯国家环境鉴定机构已就斯摩棱斯克核电站二期工程1号和2号机组的建设许可证论证材料作出了积极结论。这一结论标志着该项目在国家层面的环境可行性得到了正式确认，同时也验证了业主俄罗斯国家原子能公司与总设计方俄罗斯国家原子能工程设计股份公司在长期合作中所取得的显著成效。该结论在斯摩棱斯克核电站举行的工作组会议上正式对外公布，标志着项目推进进入了新的里程碑阶段。
斯摩棱斯克核电站厂长伊万·西多罗夫在会议上强调了企业对于该地区居民和子孙后代的责任感，并表示机组建设将严格遵守环保标准。他指出，核能从定义上就是最清洁的能源之一，但公众对核能的信任并非建立在空洞的声明之上，而是建立在专家数据和经证实的安全证据之上。为此，项目团队在设计阶段便确定了施工区域的环境监测点，以便在机组投入运行后能够建立全面的基线数据进行对比分析。
俄罗斯国家原子能公司总经理阿列克谢·利哈乔夫表示，实施建设核电站等雄心勃勃的计划是低碳发电领域的战略选择，核能正成为绿色能源转型的重要基础。俄罗斯原子能设计股份公司斯摩棱斯克核电站二期工程设计总监列昂尼德·列别捷夫也补充指出，新电厂的设计充分考虑了VVER反应堆在国内外积累的可靠运行经验，设计期间还开展了详细的工程调查和公众听证会，并运用数学建模对可能的影响情景进行了全面评估。这一系列举措旨在确保未来机组对大气、水资源和土壤的影响微乎其微。
新电厂的设计融合了一系列全面的环境保护措施，旨在最大限度减少对周边生态的影响。电厂规划了现代化的废水处理设施和高效的气体回收系统，并采用了冷却塔闭环的反应堆冷却系统，这对于保护杰斯诺戈尔斯克水库的生态系统尤为关键。俄罗斯自然资源和自然保护监督局的专家在评估后得出结论，未来机组对周围环境的干扰将不会超过既定标准。此外，核电站环境部门已开始对施工区域的环境状况进行监测，并将持续监控电厂全生命周期的环境变化。
目前，斯摩棱斯克核电站二期工程的施工安装设施正在加紧建设中，为正式进入主体施工阶段做好了充分准备。纤维模板车间和混凝土搅拌站的基础已经浇筑完毕，钢筋加固车间的钢结构也正在安装之中。包括道路、围栏、照明和消防供水系统在内的现场基础设施建设也在同步推进，其中今年8月底完成的输电线路接入施工现场，实现了24小时照明，施工人员得以突破日照时间限制进行作业。
俄罗斯国家原子能公司电力事业部是俄罗斯最大的低碳电力生产商，旗下目前运营着10座核电站，其中包括世界上唯一的浮动核电站。该事业部拥有34台机组，总装机容量达28.5吉瓦，发电量约占俄罗斯总发电量的19%。斯摩棱斯克核电站作为该公司的分支机构，不仅是斯摩棱斯克州的主要能源公司，也是当地最年轻城市杰斯诺戈尔斯克的支柱产业，目前运行着三个各为1000兆瓦的机组，每年向俄罗斯统一能源系统供应超过200亿千瓦时的电力。
2024年12月，俄罗斯政府批准了一项至2042年的电力设施部署总体规划。根据该规划，俄罗斯预计到2035年将建成12座中大型核电站和9座小型陆上及浮动核电站，并在海外布局若干核电机组。已投入使用的斯摩棱斯克核电站二期工程采用VVER优化反应堆技术，将作为俄罗斯大型核电站批量生产的重要基础。能源部门致力于提升国民经济竞争力，促进国家各地区发展和进步，为工业和民众提供稳定的生活所需。

英国核工业的就业岗位数量在2026年首次突破10万人大关
英国核工业协会 (NIA) 的年度就业地图显示，受 Sizewell C 核电站建设的推动，英国核工业的就业岗位在 2026 年首次超过 10 万个，随着英国核能产能的扩大，预计就业岗位还将进一步增长。
根据总部位于伦敦的NIA的数据，过去五年就业岗位增长了67%，从2021年的61371个增加到2026年的102606个。其中，86%的就业岗位位于伦敦和英格兰东南部以外的地区。
自 2025 年以来，共创造了 4,433 个就业岗位。NIA 表示，这主要得益于 Sizewell C 核电站过去一年就业岗位增长了 62.6%，该核电站将拥有两台 EPR 压水反应堆机组。
国家工业局表示，在 Sizewell C 核电站建设期间，还将创造 1500 个学徒岗位。
报告指出，欣克利角C核电站过去一年就业人数有所增长。欣克利角C核电站位于英格兰西南部萨默塞特郡，目前正在建设中，也是一座拥有两台机组的EPR核电站。
“核能行业仍然是伦敦和英格兰东南部以外地区增长和投资的关键引擎，”NIA首席执行官汤姆·格雷特克斯表示。
“核能独特的产业布局为全国各地创造了数万个高技能就业岗位，尤其是在最需要这些岗位的沿海社区。”
国家工业局(NIA)还表示，未来几年就业增长将持续，预计在北威尔士格温多德(Gwyndod，原名威尔法Wylfa)建造的三座劳斯莱斯小型模块化反应堆(SMR)将创造8000个就业岗位。NIA补充说，其中3000个就业岗位将位于核电站附近。

中核集团与IAEA签署高温气冷堆领域合作协议
格罗西详细了解高温气冷堆、玲龙一号等核能创新解决方案及综合利用情况，对中国小堆建设进度表示关注，并对中核集团在小堆创新应用上作出的积极贡献表示了高度赞赏。
本次中国展集中展示高温气冷堆、玲龙一号等我国先进核能技术创新成果和核能综合利用实践。其中，高温气冷堆等先进堆型受到国际原子能机构以及参会各国代表关注。
根据中核能源与IAEA签署高温堆领域的合作协议，双方约定将在高温气冷堆核电厂研发、设计、建设、调试、运行以及供应链、人才培养等领域开展交流合作，这意味着全球可以共享我国在高温气冷堆工程的实践经验，将进一步助力高温气冷堆在核能发电、工业供热、制氢等低碳场景全球推广。
据了解，当前全球能源转型持续深化，应对气候变化、保障能源安全、推进绿色低碳发展，已成为全人类的共同追求。特别是多国积极签署《三倍核能宣言》，持续探索和平利用核能的全新路径，全球核能发展迎来重要机遇期。
一直以来，中核集团积极推动先进核能技术创新与工程落地，在小型模块化反应堆、四代先进堆等多个技术方向持续深耕，已形成“大中小特微”型谱化全面发展格局，可为不同场景、不同国家能源需求提供多样化技术选择。
近年来中核集团积极推进的“核能+石化”耦合发展，将核能清洁优势与石化产业用能需求进行深度结合，为传统高耗能行业绿色转型提供了新思路。这其中，高温气冷堆作为具有第四代核能技术特征的先进堆型，在工业供热、综合能源利用等领域具有广阔应用前景。
2026年1月16日，全球首个将高温气冷堆与压水堆耦合，以工业供热为主、兼顾电力供应的核动力厂——江苏徐圩核能供热发电厂正式开工，标志着我国核能利用从单一发电向多元供给转型迈出关键一步，为全球高耗能产业低碳转型提供可复制、可推广的“中国方案”，预计该项目建成投产后，年供应工业蒸汽将超3500万吨。

肯尼亚承诺按国际标准推进西亚亚(Siaya)核电站建设
在奥地利维也纳举行的第70届国际原子能机构大会上，肯尼亚向国际社会重申，将在核安全、核不扩散和国际保障监督框架下，推进该国首座核电站建设。肯尼亚卫生部长阿登·杜瓦莱代表政府发表国家声明，强调核能开发将严格遵守国际规范，并接受相关监管与审查。
肯尼亚计划在西亚亚郡建设这一核电项目，预计总投资约5000亿肯尼亚先令。按照目前规划，电站装机容量将在2000兆瓦至5000兆瓦之间，未来将作为支撑国家工业化进程的重要基荷电源，为制造业、基础设施和城市化发展提供稳定电力。西亚亚位于肯尼亚西南部，原属尼扬扎省（Nyanza Province）。它紧邻非洲最大的淡水湖——维多利亚湖（Lake Victoria），拥有很长的湖岸线。
根据项目时间表，西亚亚核电站(Siaya Nuclear plant)预计将在2027年破土动工，并计划于2034年实现并网发电。肯尼亚核能与能源局首席执行官贾斯图斯·瓦布亚博表示，项目正在按照国际原子能机构的“第二阶段里程碑方法”推进，以确保法律制度、监管体系、安全评估和项目管理均达到国际要求。
肯尼亚总统威廉·鲁托此前已公开支持该核电计划。政府方面认为，发展核电不仅是应对气候变化、扩大清洁能源供应的重要选择，也已成为推动“2030年愿景”工业布局的现实需求。核电被视为可减少对不稳定能源来源依赖、提升电网可靠性并降低长期用电成本的关键方案。
瓦布亚博指出，核电站建设预计将创造数千个高技能工程、技术和建筑岗位，同时带动本地供应链发展。针对公众对大型核设施安全性的担忧，肯尼亚政府承诺将坚持以证据为基础开展沟通，通过公开透明的信息发布和持续公众参与，增强社会对项目的理解与信任。
杜瓦莱在大会上还表示，肯尼亚的核战略并不局限于发电领域。该国正在推进核研究反应堆建设，并扩大核技术在医疗、农业和科研等民生领域的应用，以提升公共服务能力和国家科技水平。
在医疗方面，国际原子能机构今年5月向肯尼亚纳库鲁和蒙巴萨捐赠的两台直线加速器已投入使用，目前每天可为约150名癌症患者提供治疗。肯尼亚政府还在建设6个区域癌症中心，并通过社会健康管理局将保障覆盖范围扩大至超过3200万名注册民众。
在农业领域，肯尼亚通过参与国际原子能机构“食物核技术”倡议，提高了作物产量，并将化肥使用成本降低约20%。该国还在建立“食品与农业卓越中心”，以进一步推广核农技术，提升粮食安全水平和农业生产效率。

title: 深圳核博会
content:
Nusano公司入选美国核能发射平台计划，推进先进核燃料生产线
位于犹他州西谷城的Nusano公司，一家在放射性同位素和核燃料生产领域取得突破的物理公司，荣获美国国家反应堆创新中心(NRIC)和美国能源部(DOE)的青睐，将参与HALEU(高放射性低浓缩铀)核燃料生产线的开发，作为“核能发射平台计划(NRIC Nuclear Energy Launch Pad USA Program)”的一部分。该计划是由联邦政府发起的，旨在加速创新核技术从概念到商业部署的进程。
通过这一计划，Nusano将获得美国能源部的授权流程支持、国家实验室的专业知识、基础设施、技术资源和项目支持，从而加速先进核技术的开发和部署。值得一提的是，该生产线采用金属铀原料，而非氟化铀气体，旨在降低成本，实现模块化可扩展性，并避免有害的氟化学。一个Nusano HALEU生产单元仅需要1200平方英尺的运营空间，能够根据市场需求逐步部署额外的单元。预计每个单元每年将生产5.9吨的HALEU，预计首个单元将于2031年投入运营。
Nusano首席执行官Keith Titus表示，入选“发射平台”表明Nusano的HALEU技术及团队已准备好向前推进。在评审过程中，项目在技术实力、运行准备情况以及与国家战略优先事项的对齐度方面都得到了评估。他表达了对被选入的自豪，并感谢有机会推进工作，以支持美国的能源独立。

title: 深圳核博会
content:
国际原子能机构第七十届大会在维也纳开幕
国际原子能机构第70届大会已于今日在奥地利维也纳正式拉开帷幕。此次大会预计吸引来自全球各地的代表，人数预计在两千五百至三千人之间，体现了国际社会对核能相关问题的重视。作为国际原子能机构一年一度的最高决策会议，维也纳的这场盛会具有举足轻重的意义。
大会汇聚了国际原子能机构的成员国代表，他们将共同审议机构的年度工作报告、预算规划以及一系列重要的政策议题。这是一个公开透明的平台，各国代表在此就全球性的核能安全、核不扩散以及核技术和平利用等关键问题展开深入讨论和交流。
国际原子能机构大会无疑是全球核能治理领域内最重要的多边平台之一。它不仅为成员国之间协调立场、制定共同行动方案提供了机会，更致力于推动核能技术的安全、可控和可持续发展，为全人类的福祉做出贡献。
围绕核能安全问题，各国代表将重点关注核电站的安全运行、核事故的预防和应对、放射性废物处理等关键环节，探讨如何进一步提升核能安全等级，确保公众的安全和环境的健康。
核不扩散问题是国际社会高度关注的焦点。大会将探讨如何加强国际合作，防止核技术和核材料被滥用，维护世界和平与稳定，构建一个没有核威胁的未来。
核技术和平利用是国际原子能机构的重要使命之一。大会将讨论如何利用核技术在医疗、农业、工业等领域发挥积极作用，解决发展中国家面临的挑战，促进全球共同繁荣。
为了更好地应对日益复杂的核能挑战，大会还将审议并改进国际原子能机构的运作机制，提高其决策效率和执行力，确保其能够更好地履行自身职责。
此次维也纳大会的举办，恰逢全球核能发展的重要阶段，它将为国际社会就核能问题达成共识、共同应对挑战提供一个宝贵的平台，共同探索核能的未来发展方向。

title: 深圳核博会
content:
印度代表在原子能机构第70届大会强调核能创新与国际合作
在国际原子能机构(IAEA)第70届大会上，印度代表、原子能委员会主席阿吉特·库马尔·莫汉蒂(Ajit Kumar Mohanty)发表致辞，重点介绍了印度在核能技术突破、法规改革以及国际合作方面的最新进展。
莫汉蒂主席对大会主席的当选表示祝贺，并重申了印度对国际原子能机构的长期承诺。他指出，印度与该机构的合作源远流长，并特别提到印度于2026年5月在孟买接任亚太地区核科学技术研究、开发和训练区域合作协定(RCA)主席国。在“世界一家”(Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam)理念的指引下，印度正致力于深化整个亚太地区的科研合作与人才培养。
在技术突破与立法方面，莫汉蒂主席宣布了数项里程碑式的进展：
核能法规现代化：印度议会于2025年12月通过《SANTI法案》(通过可持续开发与推进核能转型印度法案)，在保留国家对敏感活动主权控制的同时，开放了公共和私营实体的广泛参与，赋予核监管机构法定地位，并使国内责任条款与国际最佳实践接轨。
快堆技术新突破：2026年4月，位于卡尔帕卡姆(Kalpakkam)的500兆瓦原型快中子增殖反应堆(PFBR)成功实现临界，使印度成为全球第二个掌握该技术的国家。
制氢与老旧反应堆续航：2026年6月，印度利用本土铜氯热化学循环技术完成全球首个基于核工艺的制氢示范;此外，印度的监管机构已批准全球运营时间最长的商业核反应堆——塔拉普尔(Tarapur)原子能电站1号和2号机组重启并继续运行。
前沿科学与医疗合作：2026年3月，位于马哈拉施特拉邦的LIGO-India巨型科学项目正式签订工程采购与施工合同。同时，印度积极推行“邻国优先”政策，通过塔塔纪念中心为周边国家医护人员提供癌症诊疗培训，并在2026年金砖国家主席国任期内牵头推动核医学领域的国际监管合作。
莫汉蒂主席最后强调，每个国家都有权和平利用核技术以改善民生。印度将继续通过国际原子能机构及多边平台，共享本土技术与产能建设经验，推动核科学成为服务人类共同福祉与发展的有效力量。

总装机60万千瓦！云南能投拟开发5个风电场
中国能源新闻网讯（记者衣韵潼）9月14日晚间，云南省国资委旗下上市主体云南能源投资股份有限公司（以下简称“云南能投”）公告，为紧紧把握战略发展机遇、增强综合竞争力，接控股股东通知，将由两家全资子公司执行五个风电场项目的开发。
这五个风电场分别为马龙区通泉风电场（三期）（东片区）、通泉风电场（三期）（西片区）、通泉风电场（四期）、通泉风电场（五期）和会泽县五星风电场。其中马龙区通泉风电场（三期）东、西片区装机容量最大，分别为19.375万千瓦、16.25万千瓦。
根据公告，上述五个风电场项目均已列入云南省2026年第一批新能源项目建设清单，预计总装机容量59.995万千瓦，工程建设总工期皆为12个月。截至目前，云南能投已投产发电的新能源（包括风电和光伏）总装机容量为275.486万千瓦，其中风电249.386万千瓦。
云南能投表示，本次项目建设有利于进一步提升公司新能源装机规模，促进新能源业务做强做优做大，推动公司战略发展目标实现的同时助推地方经济社会发展。当前，上述项目正在开展前期相关工作，后续仍需提交董事会或股东会审议，并获得相关主管部门核准或批复。

title: 陈巴尔虎旗122户牧民用上了“安心电”--中国能源新闻网
content:
陈巴尔虎旗122户牧民用上了“安心电”--中国能源新闻网
中国能源传媒集团有限公司主办
能源中国IOS版
陈巴尔虎旗122户牧民用上了“安心电”
电力风光，日子就风光
陈巴尔虎旗122户牧民用上了“安心电”
——我国定频构网及有功控制技术首次在边远牧区微电网应用
9月10日，全国首个定频构网牧区末端保供风光储微电网在内蒙古呼伦贝尔陈巴尔虎旗赫尔洪德生态移民新村投运并网运行，彻底破解草原末梢电网供电不稳的难题，让当地122户牧民告别了用电困扰。
9月10日，国网呼伦贝尔供电公司赫尔洪德风光储互补发电站正式投运。摄影：许海亮
赫尔洪德，蒙古语意为“黑天鹅栖息的湖泊”。该地区曾长期受电网薄弱问题制约。牧区电网网架单薄、线路老旧，每逢秋冬风雪天气，输电线路极易出现故障，用电不稳成了困扰当地群众生产生活的“老大难”。
近年来，该地区新能源发展较快，但受制于风电、光伏发电的随机性及间歇性的特点，接入电网后，很容易造成电压、频率不稳，就像小船随大浪摇晃，难以保持平稳。
为打通牧区用电保障“最后一公里”，国网蒙东电力联合清华大学科研团队，将前沿电力技术扎根草原一线，用技术创新破解偏远牧区新能源供电难题。
据介绍，该项目创新采用“风电+光伏+储能”多能互补模式，依托清华大学研发的定频构网及有功控制技术，赋予储能机组定频稳压特性，具备并网主动支撑与离网独立构网双重保供能力。日常并网运行中，机组实时平抑新能源出力与负荷变化带来的波动，平稳输送清洁电力；遇到极端天气导致大电网断电时，可快速无缝切换至独立构网模式，无需人工操作，在定频构网及有功控制技术支撑下持续稳定供电至少3天，全方位保障牧民生产生活用电。
国网呼伦贝尔供电公司运检技术部寇汉鹏表示，通过智能算法优化，让储能设备变身电网的“稳定器”“调节阀”，相当于给牧区微电网装上了专属平衡系统。“有风就使（用）风电，有太阳就用光伏电。阴天无风的天气，储能设备的电力就及时顶上。”
国网蒙东电科院新型电力系统全过程仿真实验室主任王新宇介绍，为确保新技术适配草原复杂供电场景，国网蒙东电科院依托东北地区首个研究新型电力系统稳定问题的动模试验平台，完成40余项工况试验，并历时一个月完成20余种工况的现场测试，构建起从算法研发、仿真验证到现场落地的完整技术转化体系，全方位筑牢牧区电网安全稳定运行的技术根基，让前沿科研成果真正落地惠民。
陈巴尔虎旗哈日干图嘎查村民孙桂贤表示，以前一到恶劣天气就担心，害怕因停电冰柜里存着的牛羊肉和奶食会变质。“自从有了这套高科技，牧民们那种‘不安心’的日子一去不返了。用电稳了，可以养更多的牛羊，我们的好日子就来了。”

title: 2026年“电力之光”中国电力科普月活动在西安开幕--中国能源新闻网
content:
2026年“电力之光”中国电力科普月活动在西安开幕--中国能源新闻网
中国能源传媒集团有限公司主办
能源中国IOS版
2026年“电力之光”中国电力科普月活动在西安开幕
中国能源新闻网讯（记者杜明俐）
9月9日，2026年“电力之光”中国电力科普月暨电力科普创作大会开幕式在陕西西安举办。本次活动由中国电机工程学会、中国华能集团有限公司等13家单位共同主办，华能西安热工研究院联合主办。
2026年“电力之光”中国电力科普月启动仪式
大会以“智创科普，电启未来”为主题，采用线上线下“1+N+云”组织形式，主会场落地西安，联动全国50余个分会场，打造全领域行动、全地域覆盖、全媒体传播的年度科普盛宴，为推动能源转型、助力“双碳”目标实现、建设能源强国注入科普动能。
中国电机工程学会理事长、中国工程院院士、国际电工委员会（IEC）第36届主席舒印彪通过视频致辞。他表示，电力科普是推动能源转型、助力“双碳”目标实现的基础性、支撑性工作。“电力之光”品牌要持续发挥桥梁纽带作用，健全协同共享机制，推动电力科普事业朝着品牌化、精品化、常态化方向纵深发展，构建政府引导、学会牵头、企业主体、社会协同的电力科普工作新格局，以高质量科普助力能源电力高质量发展。
开幕式现场发布《中国电机工程学会科普发展规划（2026—2030 年）》，明确未来五年电力行业科普工作发展方向与六项重点任务，为全行业协同开展科普工作提供行动指引。现场展播2026年电力科普创作大赛获奖作品集锦，同步举行“电力之光”科学传播专家聘书颁发仪式，壮大行业科学传播人才队伍。
梁法光作主旨报告
为进一步促进电力科普工作高质量发展，大会邀请多位专家带来主旨报告。原中国科普作家协会副理事长、天文学家卞毓麟教授围绕“元科普”建设分享科普创作理念，呼吁领军科学家投身科普创作；华能西安热工研究院副总经理梁法光作火电无人化智能运行技术科普报告，介绍百万千瓦机组无人干预连续运行工程实践，展示煤电智能化升级创新成果。
卞毓麟作主旨报告
为传承科学家精神，西安交通大学学生现场展演原创话剧《中国电机之父——钟兆琳》，生动再现老一辈电力科教先辈爱国报国、潜心治学的感人事迹。2026年起，科普月正式启动轮值举办制度，开幕式举行旗帜交接仪式，下届“电力之光”中国电力科普月将由中国大唐集团牵头主办，实现科普事业行业接力、薪火相传。
据了解，本届科普月同步开展科普能力提升培训、院士专家校园行、弘扬科学家精神主题活动、精品科普作品展等多项配套活动，集中展示科普图书、科普视频、电力文创等丰富成果。线上推出“电力之光大讲堂”、科普作品展播、全国分会场云上展示等栏目。参会代表还走进西安交通大学西迁博物馆、西安热工院阎良科研试验及产业基地实地参观，进一步拓宽科普创作思路。历经多年深耕，“电力之光”已经成为电力行业极具影响力的科普品牌，持续动员全行业力量，面向社会大众普及电力科技知识，弘扬科学家精神，助力全民科学素质提升。

title: 具透 | 精心优化， 体验感愉悦升华：iOS 27 中值得关注的新特性 - 少数派
content:
少数派编辑部官方账号。
少数派编辑部官方账号。
Apple 于 9 月 15 日凌晨正式发布 iOS 27、iPadOS 27、macOS 27 Golden Gate 和 watchOS 27 等系统的正式版。其中， iOS 27 不仅大幅改善了性能，还优化了 Liquid Glass 设计风格、并给 Safari、快捷指令加入了多项细节改进。
少数派为你整理了新版系统中值得关注的新功能和新特性，如果你升级新系统之后想了解有哪些新功能，或者还在观望是否需要升级，这篇文章都能帮助到你。当然，升级新版系统之前，别忘了通过 Apple 设备/Finder 或者 iCloud 备份好你的 iPhone 数据。
如果你想知道自己的设备是否能够升级新版系统，可以在
查看。据 Apple 官网提供的信息，iOS 27 支持 iPhone 11 (2019 年) 系列以及之后推出的产品：
Liquid Glass
在 iOS 26 上推出的 Liquid Glass 视觉方案可谓是饱受争议，虽然 Apple 后续在各个小版本更新中不断调整优化，但效果终究还是见仁见智，毕竟每个人都有自己不同的喜好。
于是，在 iOS 27 版本中，Apple 在「设置-外观-Liquid Glass」中加入了系统全局下的透明度滑杆，可以让用户自己决定 Liquid Glass 的效果强度。Apple 还增加了最透明档位的透明度，可以让背景内容更加容易透过按钮、气泡和导航组件显示。
另外，Apple 还优化了系统应用图标和控件，让它们更具层次感和立体感。在 iOS 27 中，Apple 对系统图标进行了重设计，包括 Safari、Siri、设置、Apple Store、Remote、Preview 等应用在内的图标都得到了不同方向的修改。比如说，Safari 使用更明亮的蓝色和更细致的指南针图案，Siri 图标更接近实际呼出 Siri 时的发光球体，部分图标则增加了透明度和立体层次。
比如，在 iOS 和 iPadOS 27 上，App 图标、程序坞和小组件等边缘的轮廓光照效果被移除了，现在你只能在锁屏时钟上看见这个效果。
又比如，界面顶部和底部的渐进式模糊效果也被砍掉了，重新回到了以前磨砂玻璃类似的质感。
还有，一些标准设计的应用图标现在会有彩色投影效果。此外，由于现在从顶部下拉变成了激活 Siri AI，所以通知动画也有所调整，现在变成从左上角出现。
其他 UI 细节调整
锁屏中的正在播放小组件可以通过左滑来手动隐藏，不过在切歌或者重新播放时会重新打开这个小组件。
AirPlay 菜单新增渐层模糊背景，内容和背景的区分更明显，也更贴近 iOS 27 的 Liquid Glass 视觉语言。
Apple Music、Apple Pay 和 App Store 的付款界面的设计样式也有所调整，Apple 还提前预告了 Apple Music 的专辑页面也会迎来更新，但目前还没有上线。
相机启用夜景、微距、曝光调整等额外拍摄功能时，左下角的微距按钮和右下角的相机隐藏菜单都加入了更明显的黄色外框提示，方便用户知道当前是否启用了额外拍摄功能。
在 iOS 27 中，Apple 继续加强了视频拍摄功能。当我们在相机设置中为视频拍摄开启 Apple ProRes 选项后，可以在视频编码中选择 Log 或者 Log 2 格式。新增的 Log 2 格式可以保留更多的影像信息，为后期调色提供更大的空间，Apple Log 2 仅在 iPhone 17 Pro 系列机型上提供支持。
Apple 还为相机应用加入了控件编辑入口，打开相机右下角的六圆点控件菜单后，可以通过左上角的「编辑」按钮进入自定义界面，调整常用拍摄控件的布局，可以让我们把经常使用的选项放在更顺手的位置。
TV 应用新增了一个自动下载后续剧集的功能，可以在 TV 设置中开启，选择名称为「自动下载」。启用这个选项后，TV 应用会自动下载继续观看的剧集后续更新的两集节目，并且会在你观看完后自动删除下载内容。对于喜欢在 TV 上追剧的人来说，这个新功能既可以让我们在第一时间不受网速影响、更加流畅地观看最新的剧集，又可以自动清理储存空间，可谓是一举两得。
AirPods 管理
为了更方便地方便管理 AirPods，现在 AirPods 也迎来了新的页面设计，增加了二级界面，并给每个设置选项增加了图标。最后，现在 AirPods 还支持自定义 EQ 了，你也可以定制你的专属听感。
在 iOS 27 中，Apple 还为 AirPods 的自适应模式新增了一个更加直观的滑块，可以在通透和降噪之间调整偏向，只需要通过按住滑块就可以滑动到滑轨上的任意一个位置。过去的自适应模式更像一个自动切换的状态，在 iOS 27 中Apple 让它变成了用户可以主动调节的连续选项。
Apple 为控制中心的 AirPods 调节界面也加入了相同的调节选项，在启用自适应模式后，我们可以在控制中心中也可以灵活地调节更多环境声或者更多降噪。
性能与搜索体验是 iOS 27 的重点改进方向。根据 Apple 自己的说法，App 启动最多快 30%，拍照后回看加载快 70%，AirDrop 传输快 80%，外置存储文件传输最多快 5 倍。同时，Apple 还优化了 CPU 调度器，显著提升老机型的多任务处理体验。
新版本中，Apple 还重建搜索底层，并把 Spotlight、邮件、照片统一到同一个搜索引擎，可以带来更加稳定高效的搜索体验。在更新到 iOS 27 后，系统设置界面会提醒你正在重新构建索引，完成后即可体验到更加流畅的搜索体验。
针对搜索界面的预加载界面，原先系统会默认显示 8 个建议的应用，而在 iOS 27 中Apple 把这个自定义权利开放给了用户。在设置中，我们可以选择显示 8 个、4 个或者完全不显示应用，以及可以选择是否显示应用的快捷指令。
快捷指令在 iOS 27 中也迎来了大加强。首先是支持「否则」逻辑，适合处理更复杂的场景，不用再不断嵌套「如果」来实现比较复杂的快捷指令了。
快捷指令应用更新了「获取屏幕」模块，现在可以按照屏幕上媒体类别、是否可见以及是否只包含当前 app 筛选，来实现更高级的数据自动化输入。
快捷指令应用更新了「持久化数据」功能，可以跨平台写入、读取 iCloud 中的数据字段，真正实现一个快捷指令在多端无缝使用。
最后，快捷指令应用自动化部分还新增了截图、连接到键盘和通知三个触发自动化的新方式，能更方便得触发快捷指令自动化了。
其他 App 及设置选项
铃声、闹钟、提醒有了独立的音量设置，且 AirPods 可以单独设置提示声音量大小；
内置的输入法现在支持拼字输入，词库和语音输入功能也得到了增强；
内置的输入法在剪切板中的内容更新后，会在备选字框中主动提示；
备忘录应用现在可以将富文本复制为 Markdown，或者将 Markdown 粘贴为富文本；
钱包应用新增了自建通行证的功能；
钱包应用新增了一个自定义创建 Pass 的功能，Apple 正在将这个新功能开放到更多的国家和地区。
地图应用对 Flyover 视觉进行了升级；
健康应用新增了围绝经期追踪等功能；
照片应用新增了身份证件（Identity Documents）以及 Captured by Me 两个实用分类；
Apple 在新版本中针对一些特殊尺寸的图片（比如说比例接近于 iPhone 屏幕的宽高比）新增了一个默认的放大选项。当我们点击这些尺寸的图片进入全屏模式时，Apple 会对这些图片进行轻微的裁切和放大，消除四周的留白，让图片撑满整个 iPhone 屏幕。如果你不喜欢这个新特性，那么可以在「设置」>「照片」>「显示选项」中关闭「缩放以充满屏幕」这个选项。
照片应用浏览视频时，现在可以将单独帧当作截图导出；
查找 app 现在可以更灵活地设置共享时间；
新增恢复模式，可以在不借助其他设备的情况下恢复 iOS 系统；
13 岁以下账户默认开启询问以浏览和询问以购买的设置；
Wi-Fi 助手现已更名为连接助理，在 Wi-Fi 和蜂窝数据之间切换更顺畅；如果你不希望系统在特定 Wi-Fi 环境下自动切换蜂窝网络，那么还可以针对某个 Wi-Fi 网络单独关闭或开启连接助理功能
国行 iPhone 新增了节假日闹钟，可以根据周末和法定假日自动调整闹钟的日期；
为了展示更多信息，iOS 27 中引入了更大尺寸的小组件；
PlayStation Access 控制器现在支持 macOS、iPadOS 和 iOS，并且可以在游戏控制器设置中创建和保存自定义输入配置；
RCS 跨平台聊天升级，可以在信息 app 中对任意一条 RCS 消息进行引用回复，方便快速查看或者跳转到对应的历史消息；
RCS 消息中的图片或者表情回应时，在 Android 手机上也可以正常显示。
图源：MacRumors
iCloud 共享相簿支持完整分辨率分享，Android、Windows 用户也可通过 iCloud.com 参与并上传照片。
新版「屏幕使用时间」把儿童使用管理做得更细：可按娱乐、游戏和社交媒体等类别分配时间，Schedules 则按日期和时段决定哪些应用可用。家长也可以在儿童设备初次设置时选择允许使用的系统应用，通过询问浏览审批新网站。通信安全的识别范围扩展至共享图片、视频中的血腥和暴力内容。
GymKit 扩展到 iPhone，可连接兼容健身器材查看实时训练数据，并可搭配 AirPods Pro 3 记录心率。
旁白可提供更丰富的图像描述，并结合实时识别和操作按钮询问周围环境；放大器增加面向低视力用户的对话式辅助。语音控制允许用自己的话描述屏幕按钮，辅助阅读也加强了复杂内容的处理、摘要与翻译。
iOS 27 对 Apple Intelligence 和 Siri 带来了大幅升级，但能否使用仍取决于设备、语言和地区。但为了方便读者了解 iOS 27 中的 AI 功能，我们也简单整理了其中的新变化。
Apple Intelligence
识别率更高的 AI 转译功能被集成进系统键盘中，Apple 使用了端侧的模型来完成转译的任务，同时支持多种语言混合、离线识别，不需要切换键盘。另外，新版本中的系统键盘还通过 AI 技术改善了自动纠正拼写、标点和大小写的成功率。
日历和提醒事项都可以通过自然语义来进行输入，AI 识别后会自动创建相应的事件或者待办事项。
Visual 智能支持了账单自动分配，并配合 Apple Cash 直接发送账单给朋友，以及对食品营养信息的识别。
Apple 还预告了密码应用代用户更新弱密码、泄露密码的能力，但这项功能需要等待后续软件更新。
短信应用支持了 AI 自动生成回复内容，点击键盘上方的候选内容即可插入到输入框。
快捷指令支持通过 AI 来创建新的 Shortcut，你只需要描述你的需求或者目标即可。快捷指令还可以选择直接进入传统的动作编辑视图，而不是默认进入自然语言描述创建流程。
Call Context 会在拨打部分商家电话时，从应用中找出相关资料，例如航班确认码。
今年的照片应用在 AI 加持下，在提升了 iOS 26 中就有的消除功能的表现之外，获得了更多的编辑功能，包括扩展和重构图片。
Apple 为照片应用准备的重构功能没有像第三方应用一样分为垂直、水平、旋转三个方向分别调整，而是通过自家的空间影像技术，让我们可以模拟相机视角重新构图，然后再通过 AI 技术来生成重构后的图像。
图片来源：Macrumors
扩展功能则可以让我们调整图片的大小和比例，然后让 AI 填补多余的部分，从实际测试的效果来看非常惊艳，细节丰富，过渡自然。
图片来源：Macrumors
消除功能在 iOS 26 上已经实装，不过在处理一些复杂场景下的任务时表现不佳。在 iOS 27 中，消除功能得到了明显加强，即使在复杂场景下也能得到一个相当不错的消除效果。
图片来源：Macrumors
消除现在提供快速与高质量两种处理模式，分别面向小瑕疵和更复杂的编辑。
Safari 在新版本中加入了一个实用的功能——页面内容监测提醒。打开任意网页后，点击地址栏上的菜单按钮，选择「Notify Me」，就可以输入监测的关键词和监测的频率、时间，当 Safari 监测到页面内容变化时就会提示你。最有用的场景，可能就是抢票了。
另外，在 Apple 智能的技术加持下，新版本的 Safari 可以自动根据标签页的内容进行分类分组。第一次使用时，需要在 Safari 左上角的 Organise Tabs 处启用「Automatically Create Topics」这个选项。
Apple 还借助 AI 在新版 Safari 中内置了一个 AI 生成浏览器插件的功能，可以通过内置模板或者自然语义输入来创建个性化的插件。不过，在中国大陆这个功能无法使用，应该是用到了新版本 Siri 的功能，原因后面再说。
Image Playground
新版 Image Playground 支持包括写实在内的更多风格，也能用文字描述或触控继续修改图像。Apple 对部分生成式功能标有使用额度限制，后续也许可以通过付费来获得更多的额度。
Siri AI 将以英语逐步开放，支持 iPhone 15 Pro、iPhone 15 Pro Max 和全部 iPhone 16 及后续机型。语速和表现力自定义所需的端侧语音模型，支持范围更窄，目前仅支持 iPhone Air、iPhone 17 Pro 系列及后续受支持机型。
首先，全新 Siri 拥有了系统级的上下文和屏幕感知能力，可以与手机屏幕上的内容进行实时的交互。如果你用过 Pixel 手机上的 Gemini，应该对这个功能不会感到陌生，而现在 Siri 也如愿获得了这个能力。
其次，全新 Siri 拥有了一个独立的应用，我们可以在应用内进行对话。
你也可以通过 Spotlight 进行对话，而 Spotlight 现在可以被一个从屏幕顶端下滑的动作唤起。
在任意应用中弹出系统键盘时，都会在键盘顶部的预测栏新增一个「Write with Siri」的按钮。在键盘输入任意文字后，在预测栏的最左侧会出现一个「Ask Siri」的按钮。两个按钮都是全新 Siri 写作工具的入口。
我们可以直接通过灵动岛的 Siri 来起草、改写或者调整文本内容。新的写作工具更像自然语言驱动的一个全局功能，取代了旧版写作工具的固定选项，意味着 Siri 从一个语言助手慢慢渗透到系统中的每个角落。
Siri 现在还可以调整 Pace（语速）和 Expressivity（表现力）了，我们可以调整 Siri AI 的说话速度和情绪表现。不过，在 iPhone 上这项功能目前只面向支持新版 Siri AI 的高内存机型开放，包括 iPhone Air、iPhone 17 Pro 和 iPhone 17 Pro Max。
Siri 语音设置界面在新版本中针对各个版本的 iPhone 进行了统一，不管设备是否支持定制化 Siri 语音，都会显示同一套界面，区别在于不支持的设备只显示口音和更少的语音选项，而支持的设备除了更多的语音选项，还支持调节语速和表现力。
另外，Siri 还在设置中新增了一个预览行数的选项，我们可以选择从不显示、显示一行到最多显示五行。辅助功能中新增了一个「Always Show Request」的新功能，开启后屏幕会持续显示用户对 Siri 所说内容的文字转写。
家庭 app 首次打开时新增了 What’s New 介绍页，重点包括 Apple Intelligence 对家庭通知和视频摘要的支持、可查看部分智能温控器和智能插座的用电信息，以及更灵活的配件设置流程。家庭 app 现在也支持直接管理 Apple TV 和 HomePod 的软件更新，包括查看更新内容、管理 Beta 更新、发起更新等操作。
当开启家庭 app 中的 Apple Intelligence 后，HomeKit Secure Video 录像可以通过端侧模型和 Private Cloud Compute 生成视频描述并支持搜索。不过需要注意的是，Apple Intelligence for Home 中的录像描述与搜索功能需要 2TB 起的 iCloud+ 订阅。
家庭应用可以把关联配件的通知合并为一次活动，并随活动进展更新。视频描述和片段搜索可以帮助用户快速定位录像中的事件。
在 iOS 27 版本中，兼容的 HomeKit Secure Video 摄像头终于支持了串流和录制 4K 视频。
钱包 app 中新增了一个 Insights 入口，也许是为银行或者信用卡账户做好准备，连接后可以直接在钱包 app 中查看账户余额、账单流水、交易分类等信息。目前该入口并非所有地区都能完整使用，它可能只在英国等部分国家或地区开放。
图片来源：Reddit 用户
-TomNJerry-
Visual Intelligence 新增「Highlight to Image Search」相关设置，当用户搜索相似图片时，系统会把图片发送给第三方服务以获取结果。
由于本次 Apple 和 Google 达成了大模型上的合作，所以部分请求将在设备本地由 Apple Foundation Models 直接处理，不再全部回退给 ChatGPT。目前，通过 Siri 发起的简单请求在端侧处理，复杂请求则由定制 Gemini 模型在 Apple Private Cloud Compute 上运行。
可以看到 iOS 27 在打磨细节上花了不少的心思，不管是设计细节、系统性能，还是我们目前用不上的 AI 都印证了这一点。
除了全新的界面设计，iOS 27 在细节上也新增了不少实用功能，你还发现了哪些容易被忽视的 iOS 27 新功能，不妨也在评论区与我们分享。

title: 派早报：中国联通宣布支持所有国行设备 eSIM 业务办理、Homebrew 7.0.0 发布等 - 少数派
content:
派早报：中国联通宣布支持所有国行设备 eSIM 业务办理、Homebrew 7.0.0 发布等
不要忘记升级 Apple OS 27 正式版。
豆包发布手机助手消费者版
绿联发布首款雷电 5 显卡坞
英伟达发布 RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell 专业显卡
阿凡途发布 AVENTHO Y 头戴式耳机
安克推出声阔 Boom Go 3i 音箱
Bose 推出第二代 Bose 电视音响
中国联通：支持国行所有 eSIM 手机业务办理
开源包管理器 Homebrew 7.0.0 发布
微软确定 9 月安全更新会导致远程桌面服务出现异常
看看就行的其他消息
豆包发布手机助手消费者版
2026 年 9 月 14 日，豆包手机助手消费者版本正式发布。相比此前的技术预览版，新版本进一步强化日常使用中的稳定性、系统级交互、本地信息检索和任务执行能力，同时以 Beta 形式开放「操作手机」功能。首个消费者版本将搭载于努比亚 NaviX Ultra，该机目前已开启预约，并将于 9 月 16 日正式发售。
交互方面，豆包手机助手支持语音和专属 AI 键等多种唤醒方式，其中 AI 键支持指纹鉴权，用户完成本人验证后，无需再次解锁即可调用助手执行相关任务。语音唤醒能力也针对环境噪声等使用场景进行了优化。新版同时加入屏幕内容理解能力，用户无需额外截图或切换应用，即可围绕当前屏幕内容提问，并将屏幕信息作为后续任务执行的输入。
本地信息方面，豆包手机助手可在获得用户主动授权后检索电话、相册、短信、便签等数据。用户也可以通过语音输入、手势或按键等方式主动保存屏幕内容，以供后续检索。录音功能则接入飞书妙记，可提供语音转录、实时翻译、说话人区分和自动总结等能力，并支持继续检索、追问过往录音中的具体内容。
任务执行方面，本次消费者版本以 Beta 形式开放「操作手机」功能。根据自动化操作声明协议，第三方应用开发者可以按照具体页面和业务环节声明 AI 助手的自动化操作边界，例如允许辅助编辑内容，但限制最终发送、发布或执行特定操作。
豆包方面表示，AI 助手实际能否执行相关操作，还需要综合系统安全策略、第三方应用声明以及用户授权等条件判断。对于明确拒绝屏幕自动化操作的第三方应用，豆包手机助手不会执行相关操作。官方表示，希望借此与应用开发者共同建立更加开放、规范的手机 AI 应用生态。
绿联发布首款雷电 5 显卡坞
绿联首款雷电 5 显卡扩展坞正式上市，产品配备 Thunderbolt 5 和 OCuLink 双接口以及 850W 金牌电源，京东页面显示，该产品定价为 3489 元。
据悉，这款产品支持 Windows 和 Linux 系统。规格方面，这款显卡坞的配备 3 个 Thunderbolt 5 接口，持菊花链连接，传输带宽最高可达 80Gbps，并向下兼容 USB4、雷电 4 和雷电 3；OCuLink 显卡直连带宽最高为 64Gbps，可搭配英伟达、AMD 和英特尔主流独立显卡使用。产品内置符合 ATX 3.1 标准的 850W 金牌电源，并提供 12V-2×6 供电接口，可为 RTX 40/50 系列显卡供电；同时支持 PD 3.1，通过雷电接口可为笔记本提供最高 140W 供电。
其他方面，该显卡坞采用全铝机身设计，默认可安装长度不超过 370mm 的显卡。此外，绿联 NAS 已支持通过雷电或 OCuLink 连接外置独立显卡，并可将 GPU 提供给 Docker 容器用于 AI 推理、视频转码等计算任务。
英伟达发布 RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell 专业显卡
2026 年 9 月 14 日，NVIDIA 官网上线 RTX PRO 5500 Blackwell 工作站版专业显卡产品页面。新卡采用 Blackwell 架构，配备 21760 个 CUDA 核心和 84GB ECC GDDR7 显存，最高功耗为 600W，主要面向机架式专业工作站部署。
规格方面，RTX PRO 5500 配备 84GB GDDR7 ECC 显存，采用 416-bit 显存位宽，带宽达到 1398GB/s，对应约 27Gbps 的显存等效速率。GPU 拥有第五代 Tensor Core 和第四代 RT Core，同时集成 3 个第九代 NVENC 编码器和 3 个第六代 NVDEC 解码器，采用 PCIe 5.0 x16 接口，最多可提供 4 个 DisplayPort 2.1b 视频输出接口。
散热方面，RTX PRO 5500 标准版本采用主动式风冷设计，RXM 形态还可提供液冷方案。NVIDIA 表示，该产品专为企业机架式工作站部署设计，可用于加速代理式 AI、生成式 AI、物理 AI、模拟仿真、AI 渲染、科学计算、数据分析以及视频制作等工作负载。目前 NVIDIA 官网仍将 RTX PRO 5500 标记为「即将推出」，具体售价和上市时间尚未公布。
阿凡途发布 AVENTHO Y 头戴式耳机
2026 年 9 月 12 日，拜雅 AVENTHO Y 无线头戴式耳机在国内正式开售，售价为 1199 元。
外观方面，AVENTHO Y 提供星空蓝、曜石黑、莫兰绿和气泡橙 4 种配色，耳机整体采用可折叠头戴式设计，机身配有铝制滑块与不锈钢铰链，整机重量为 316g。耳垫同样采用可更换设计，耳机外壳上有用于控制的实体按键。
音频方面，AVENTHO Y 搭载 45 mm 动圈单元，支持 ANC 主动降噪与环境声模式，并支持 Bluetooth 6.0 和多点连接。耳机内置 650 mAh 可更换电池，关闭 ANC 时续航超过 90 小时，开启 ANC 后续航超过 60 小时，同时支持快速充电，充电 5 分钟最高可提供约 6 小时播放时间。
拜雅还为 AVENTHO Y 准备了单独销售的升级套装，包括低延迟 USB-C 适配器和外接吊杆麦克风，可进一步强化游戏和语音通信体验。不过，该套装并非耳机标准包装的一部分，官方计划于 10 月推出。
安克推出声阔 Boom Go 3i 音箱
9 月 13 日，安克在京东上架声阔 Boom Go 3i 便携音箱，新品支持 IP68 级防尘防水、三种听音模式及 Auracast 多机互联，售价 489 元。
声阔 Boom Go 3i 配备 15W 输出功率，最高响度为 92dB，并搭载 BassUp 低音增强及多频段压缩算法。音箱支持 Bass Up 低音增强、标准和 Eco 省电三种模式，同时可通过 soundcore App 调节音效及灯光效果。
外观方面，机身尺寸为 102 × 106 × 45.5mm，重量约 380g，采用高弹耐撕裂硅胶材质，并配备提手及可固定在背包带上的搭扣。机身还设有显示屏，可查看剩余电量及当前工作模式。
该音箱支持两台设备组成 TWS 立体声，也可通过 Auracast 实现多台兼容声阔音箱联动，同时提供紧急高频蜂鸣功能。产品内置 4800mAh 电池，普通模式续航约 24 小时，Eco 省电模式下最长可达 40 小时。
Bose 推出第二代 Bose 电视音响
Bose 近日推出第二代 Bose 电视音响，产品采用紧凑型条形设计，配备 3 个扬声器单元，主打更宽广的声场和更清晰的人声表现，并支持 HDMI、光纤和蓝牙连接，美国市场售价为 299 美元。
Bose 表示，新款电视音响通过左右两侧倾斜布置的扬声器扩大声场，并配备中央高音单元强化人声表现。用户还可开启 Dialogue Mode 对话模式，进一步突出电影、电视剧、体育节目和新闻中的对白内容。
机身延续紧凑设计，高度约 5.6cm，可直接放置在多数电视前方。支持通过 HDMI ARC / eARC 或光纤连接电视，同时支持蓝牙无线连接，可用于播放手机、平板等设备中的音乐和播客。
产品配备独立遥控器，可用于调节音量、开启对话模式、控制蓝牙播放以及调整低频效果。此外，新款电视音响还支持有线连接到 Bose Bass Module 500、Bass Module 700 和 Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer，以进一步增强低频表现。
中国联通：支持国行所有 eSIM 手机业务办理
9 月 13 日，中国联通宣布扩大 eSIM 手机业务支持范围，所有已取得入网许可的品牌和型号均可办理相关业务，终端支持清单将依据产品上市首销时间持续更新。中国联通还表示，目前全国 2 万多家联通自有营业厅均具备 eSIM 业务受理能力。
中国联通目前公布的支持设备覆盖 Apple、华为、OPPO、荣耀、三星及联想等品牌。其中 Apple 机型包括 iPhone Air、iPhone 17e、iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max 和 iPhone Duo；华为机型包括 Mate 80 RS 非凡大师、Pura 90 Pro Max、Pura X Max、Pura X Max 典藏版、Pura X View 和 Mate XT 2 非凡大师。
此外，中国联通针对 9 月新发布的华为和苹果手机推出 eSIM「尝鲜季」活动，用户办理相关业务可获得国内流量、国际漫游及国际流量等免费权益。中国联通表示，后续还将继续扩大 eSIM 终端适配范围，并简化业务办理流程。
开源包管理器 Homebrew 7.0.0 发布
9 月 13 日，适用于 macOS 和 Linux 的开源包管理器 Homebrew 发布 7.0.0 大版本更新，重点提升安装与升级性能，并进一步强化软件供应链安全机制，同时调整旧版 macOS 和 Intel Mac 的支持政策。
Homebrew 7.0.0 加强了软件安装过程中的沙箱隔离，在软件构建、安装及测试时进一步限制其访问系统文件、网络连接和用户敏感目录，从而降低恶意软件包或异常安装脚本对系统造成影响的风险；同时引入针对已安装软件的漏洞检查能力，并配套安全通告数据库，以帮助用户识别存在已知安全风险的软件包。
新版本还继续优化软件安装、升级及内部 API 等环节的性能，并推出原生 macOS 图形界面应用。
平台支持方面，Homebrew 已停止支持 macOS Catalina 10.15 及更早版本；所有基于 Intel x86_64 处理器的 Mac 则降至 Tier 3 支持等级，不再享有完整 CI 测试及新版二进制包构建支持。按照 Homebrew 当前规划，Intel Mac 的 Homebrew 支持预计将在 2027 年 9 月或之后正式结束。
微软确定 9 月安全更新会导致远程桌面服务出现异常
9 月 11 日，微软更新 Windows 健康控制台，确认部分 Windows 11、Windows 10 和 Windows Server 设备安装 9 月安全更新后，可能出现远程桌面服务（RDS）异常。
微软表示，受影响设备可能出现远程桌面连接数分钟后中断、无法登录，或服务器长时间卡在「请等待远程桌面配置」界面等问题。Microsoft 管理控制台（MMC）、RDS 许可诊断程序、文件资源管理器等相关工具也可能停止响应，部分设备的 Windows Update 页面还可能持续显示加载状态。
此次问题涉及 Windows 11 26H1、25H2、24H2、23H2，Windows 10 22H2、21H2 及部分 LTSC 版本，同时影响 Windows Server 2025 至 Windows Server 2012 等多个服务器版本。
微软目前正在开发修复方案。如果受影响的虚拟机已经无法通过远程桌面连接，可尝试先停止并解除分配虚拟机，再重新启动，以暂时恢复远程连接。

title: 社区速递 158 | 便宜耐造的副厂手柄与大学宿舍里那些相见恨晚的装备 - 少数派
content:
除了首页时间流和侧栏的精选展位，少数派 Matrix 社区还有很多优秀内容因条件所限无法得到有效曝光，因此我们决定重启 Matrix 周报，并在此基础上添加更多社区内容、作者投稿新玩意呈现给大家。
上周社区速递：满血全功能磁吸转换头与手机 AI 通话的真实体验
为了让作者的投稿尽快与广大读者见面，我们调整了《新玩意》栏目中作者投稿部分的呈现方式和周期，作者投稿的「新玩意」后续会迁移至本栏目。投稿渠道与奖励方式仍与以往完全一致，详情参见文末。我们相信新鲜火热出炉的分享更能赢得大家的喜爱，也欢迎广大读者朋友们踊跃投稿。
@手动贩卖机：盖世小鸡启明星 2 游戏手柄
- 入手渠道：京东
- 入手价格：89.9 元
在过去的这段暑假期间，我这里陆陆续续接收了一些来自亲戚家的小孩，他们会像固定 NPC 一样，晚上自动刷新在我家客厅，等待我打开 Switch，给他们开游戏玩。其中《星露谷物语》是他们喜欢玩的游戏之一，可探索的内容丰富，且 2D 的视角对于比较少接触游戏的小孩来说，更容易上手。
不过，《星露谷物语》和其它多人本地同屏游玩的游戏不同的是，其它游戏很好地支持了一对 Joy-Con 手柄可以拆成两只手柄的特性，Switch 自带一对 Joy-Con，就天然地能支持两个人一起游玩游戏。但《星露谷物语》不行，大概是由于在《星露谷物语》中 L、R、ZL、ZR 这几个键都是有作用的，而单只的 Joy-Con 就只有 L、R，少了 ZL、ZR 这两个键，所以一对 Joy-Con 就只能给一个人用，多一个本地联机玩家，就需要多一只完整的手柄。
在这样的情况下，我便考虑着多购入一对手柄，目标很简单，给小孩玩游戏用。
基于这个用户画像，对手柄的需求也明了了——只求便宜耐造，不求功能花哨。这是我发现我用了好几年都没有摇杆漂移的 Joy-Con 手柄，在几天之内被小孩造坏了之后得到的沉痛教训。
于是我购入了这只盖世小鸡启明星 2 游戏手柄。
盖世小鸡启明星 2 可以挑选的颜色其实挺多的，但我还是选择了雾影黑这个配色。颜色这方面，白色首先被排除，否则还没下单我就能预见这个手柄能变得有多脏，而丰富多彩的颜色，其实是更受到小孩欢迎的，但颜色会让他们先入为主，他们会由颜色来决定手柄到底属于男孩子还是女孩子，而我并不想造成这种仿佛偏心任何一方的场面。虽然我很想说任何性别都可以喜欢任何一种颜色，但小孩的刻板印象确实一时半会很难纠正，我就不浪费这个时间了，直接黑色，众生平等，万事大吉。
手柄通体黑色，有些橙色点缀，雾透的质感，可以看到手柄内部的机械结构，当手柄震动时，可以看见内部的转子马达在拼命工作，沉稳的同时不失科技感。
启明星 2 手柄大小和 Switch Pro 手柄一致，年纪小的小孩努努力也能用，这群小孩最大的都是上初中的男孩了，所以从大小来说，除非是学龄前儿童，这个大小尺寸能够做到大手和小手都能用的通用性。
外观说完了，那就从它与 Switch Pro 的区别来聊聊吧——
一、线性扳机（带切换开关） vs 非线性扳机
如果使用场景是 Switch 的话，对于大多数 Switch 游戏来说，线性扳机确实没有什么太大的用处，但如果使用场景换到 PC 上，那么就大有用处了，比如说一些赛车类游戏，多了线性扳机用于控制油门细节，游戏体验感会比非线性扳机只能控制是否踩油门要好得多。
二、多了 L4、R4 两个背键
L4 和 R4 这两个键，可以在 PC 上，通过有线连接 PC，打开驱动，即可对 L4 和 R4 进行设置。不过这个 L4 和 R4 的好用程度，就见仁见智了。
首先，L4 和 R4 在 PC 的 XInput 接口层并不是作为独立的输入通道，也就意味着连接 PC 时，无法被识别出来有这么两个键，也就无法对这两个键进行设置，只有打开官方驱动之后，才能对这两个键进行设置。
而在官方驱动中，L4 和 R4 也只能被设置成手柄已有按键的映射，比如把 L4 映射成 LT 键，把 R4 映射成 RT 键，L4 和 R4 也可以设置为按键组合，比如在《欧洲卡车模拟 2》中，按住 LB 键的同时右摇杆向上，等于升档，那么此时就可以把 L4 键设置为这两者的组合，于是就得到了按一个背键升档的效果。
这样看似 L4 和 R4 也挺有用的，但驱动中对背键的设置是全局性的，也就是说，当我离开了《欧洲卡车模拟 2》，打开 PC 上别的游戏，或者来到 Switch 上打开《星露谷物语》，L4 同样等同于 LB 键加右摇杆向上这套动作组合。这就有点尴尬了。
因此，除非是长时间只用手柄玩一个游戏这种情况，否则 L4 和 R4 这两个键确实用处不大。
三、转子马达 vs HD 线性马达
任天堂和索尼的第一方手柄，在第一次使用时，都让我感受过什么叫惊艳，尤其是在游玩专门为了手柄调校的游戏时，我能感受到厂商为了让玩家拥有 4D 的体验做了多少努力。这就是线性马达的魅力。
而转子马达，追求的就不是对玩家的友好，而是对玩家钱包的友好。既然价格摆在那了，有就行了，还量大管饱，还要啥自行车。
少了陀螺仪的话，对于玩一些 Switch 上的第一方游戏这种场景，还是会有些缺憾，但又不至于到没了陀螺仪玩不了的程度。
综上所述，盖世小鸡启明星 2 游戏手柄，是一把更适合用于玩 Xbox 或 PC Steam 游戏的手柄，毕竟它的键位默认就是 Xbox 模式的（可以通过组合键切换为 Switch 模式）。
但话又说回来，回看我最初买这款手柄的目标是给小孩用的，其实已经满足了便宜、够用的标准了，而它其它与 Switch Pro 不同的功能，反而算是带来了附加的收益，毕竟小孩如果将来拿它在电脑上玩游戏，也是随时可以用上的。
在上期第 294 期一派讨论《开学宿舍生存指南：当年派友力荐的这些神器，你用过几个？》中，共有 141 名派友热情参与，十分感谢！随着各大高校陆续开学，派友们也纷纷翻出了当年的宿舍「压箱底神器」：既有提升学习视界的外接大屏与屏幕挂灯，也有守护作息的耳塞、床帘，更有针对老旧卫浴条件的洗澡神器：
@Hugogo (+12) 大学所有东西里，我印象最深刻的是外接显示器 + 屏幕支架：
显示器是家里旧电脑搬过去的，支架是 90 块钱闲鱼二手。愉悦的大屏体验，让我无聊的学生时代不至于一直刷手机，也能在刷剧之外有闲情刷刷论坛这类互联网遗物。
@一群小羊说 (+9) 看到大家都说买酷毙灯，我个人建议还是买一个屏幕挂灯吧（当然需要有个显示器）。显色指数、控光区域都优于酷毙灯，对自己眼睛好一点、对室友的睡眠好一点！
@Lawmaker (+5) 大学毕业已经快 6 年了，推荐以下好物：
- 大号充电宝（针对宿舍晚上断电的情况）
另外如果学弟学妹们对宿舍楼的洗衣机不放心，可以和我们当年一样去附近的连锁酒店凑钱开个钟点房，轮流洗个舒服的热水澡，然后再把衣服全部洗了，还能烘干。
@Lee62 (+6) 耳塞和帘子，防止神人室友半夜作妖。
@無茶君 (+5) 我建议每一个大一新生，都要买一个好枕头、好椅子。
@旓疋渒 (+2) 如果宿舍有独卫但是只能上厕所和洗漱，建议买洗澡神器，搭配一个水桶接热水可以随时洗澡，不用跑远路去澡堂，来回又出一身汗。
@贺呵呵 (+3) 只用过磁吸灯跟吸湿袋，都挺实用的。磁吸灯在舍友休息的时候用挺实用；吸湿袋是在假期回家后，床铺放在宿舍柜子里的时候用。
@aaa 果女士 (+2) 是磁吸灯，很好用又便宜，毕业几年了，老家的卧室还在拿来当小夜灯用。

title: 八部门力促智能家居消费 利好多个细分赛道
content:
记者9月14日获悉，商务部等8部门近日联合印发《促进智能家居消费行动方案》（简称《行动方案》），从扩大优质供给、完善标准体系、适老化部署等方面推出七条举措。
专家认为，此次政策以智能家居这一“小切口”服务扩大内需“大战略”，既为短期消费回暖提供抓手，也为中长期产业转型和民生改善注入制度动力，利好智能控制器、通信模组、国产操作系统生态及银发智能硬件等细分赛道。
家居消费规模体量大、涵盖领域广、产业链条长。商务部消费促进司负责人表示，随着技术加快迭代升级、居民生活品质化需求不断提升，智能家居快速发展，市场渗透率不断提高。
国家统计局数据显示，在消费品以旧换新等政策利好下，节能家电、智能家居等越来越受到消费者的青睐。1至7月，包括智能眼镜在内的可穿戴智能设备零售额同比增长超过1倍，限额以上单位高能效等级家电零售额增速超过30%。
我国智能家居市场还有巨大空间。根据艾瑞研究院报告，我国智能家居设备渗透率仅为16%左右，与英美国家超过45%的水平相比，这一差距反而构成未来几年的成长弹性。在政策红利、AI技术变革及存量房改造三轮驱动下，市场正迈入以主动智能、无感交互为特征的“空间智能”新时代。预计到2026年，我国智能家居市场规模将突破8000亿元，出货量有望超过3亿台。
在此背景下，《行动方案》从扩大优质智能家居供给、完善智能家居标准体系、支持智能家居消费、发展适老化智能家居、畅通废旧回收服务链条、优化社区便民服务、加大财政金融支持力度等方面部署七条举措。其中，扩大优质供给成为政策首要发力点。《行动方案》提出，鼓励生产企业加强智能家居产品研发，加快打造一批基于国内开源操作系统的智能家居软硬件产品和一体化解决方案。同时，围绕消费者差异化需求，发展适老化智能家居，推动在适老化智能家居领域开展银发产品认证。
苏商银行特约分析师付一夫表示，《行动方案》精准施策，覆盖“一老一新”两端需求。一方面，推动基于国内开源操作系统的软硬件研发，强化自主可控；另一方面，部署发展适老化智能家居，推广家庭服务机器人、健康监测、智能照护等产品，并推行适老化设计。“供给端自主创新+需求端分层覆盖”的组合，体现了政策设计的精细化。
《行动方案》还针对智能家居消费的堵点卡点作出部署。聚焦互联互通堵点，提出完善智能家居产品智能化分级评价标准体系，加快制定实施智能家居互联互通等强制性国家标准。针对家居家装配套服务不便利问题，提出指导各地科学合理设置废旧家居回收网点，鼓励企业提供“送新+收旧”“互联网+回收”等服务。
商务部研究院副研究员洪勇表示，加快制定互联互通强制性国标，旨在打破品牌生态壁垒，推动全屋智能真融合；推广送新收旧等便民服务，有利于打通从购买、安装到回收的全生命周期服务闭环。这些都是瞄准长期制约智能家居普及的深层次问题给出的针对性举措，有利于行业从“单品智能”迈向“全屋智能”。
在保障层面，《行动方案》明确加大财政金融支持力度。鼓励金融机构围绕家居家装等消费需求，开发多样化的消费金融产品与服务。用好个人消费贷款财政贴息政策，引导金融机构加大对智能家居消费等贷款支持力度。
洪勇认为，财政金融“组合拳”从两端协同发力：一端由地方统筹补贴全屋智能购新，另一端以个人消费贷财政贴息降低大额消费门槛，形成“补贴+金融”的双重撬动效应。这一路径的有效性在以旧换新政策中已得到验证。
付一夫认为，《行动方案》以智能家居为切入点，将扩大消费、产业升级与民生改善有机结合。这些政策在利好消费端的同时，也将促进相关产业的高质量发展。
具体而言，政策利好沿三个细分赛道展开：互联互通标准先行，利好智能控制器、通信模组、国产操作系统生态，具备标准参与能力的底层互联厂商率先受益；适老化部署，打开家庭服务机器人、健康监测、智能照护等银发智能硬件增量空间；回收闭环，以旧换新放量拉动拆解回收需求，“互联网+回收”及社区焕新服务站点带动家居卖场、家装服务平台向“购新+服务”转型。（记者 王文博）

title: 国家算力互联互通区域（河北）节点正式启用
content:
9月12日，在2026中国算力大会开幕式上，国家算力互联互通区域（河北）节点正式启用，成为全国率先启用的区域节点。
河北省作为全国算力产业发展的核心省份之一，近年来持续抢抓京津冀协同发展与“东数西算”工程重大机遇，聚力打造算力供给高地。依托廊坊、张家口两大核心算力集群与雄安算力枢纽等重要载体，全省形成了算力供给充沛、产业生态完善、区位优势突出的发展格局，具备服务全国算力调度、支撑数字经济高质量发展的坚实基础。
国家算力互联互通区域（河北）节点的启用，为河北打通了接入全国统一算力市场的关键通道，将推动省内算力资源实现统一调度和跨域流通，强化河北在全国算力网络中的枢纽地位。同时，节点落地雄安，直接提升了雄安新区国家级算力枢纽的功能能级，为央企总部、科研院所等疏解单位提供了高等级算力配套，进一步凸显其在京津冀算力网络中的核心节点作用。
河北移动作为国家算力互联互通区域（河北）节点的独家实施主体，深度参与方案设计、技术论证与实施建设，持续夯实全省算力基础设施底座，优化算力网络架构，为节点从申报到启用提供了全链条保障。
大会现场，国家算力互联互通区域（河北）节点算力生态联盟同步成立。联盟立足河北算力资源，联动产业链企业、科研机构等多方主体，围绕算力调度、供需对接、场景落地开展深度协作，促进跨区域算力资源流通共享，为数字经济高质量发展注入强劲动能。（作者：宜欣）

title: 我国实现一体化算力统筹监测
content:
记者从近日举行的2026中国算力大会上获悉，中国算力平台实现全国一体化算力统筹监测，我国算力“一张网、一盘棋、一体化”发展格局基本形成。
当前，算力基础设施已成为驱动人工智能发展的关键底座、经济社会高质量发展的重要引擎。工业和信息化部日前印发《信息通信行业发展“十五五”规划》，明确提出加快全国一体化算力网建设，构建“枢纽—区域—边缘”多层次算力设施体系，深化算力自动化监测与供需匹配。近年来，我国算力基础设施建设规模持续扩大、布局持续优化，同时也面临算力布局分散、资源底数不清、动态监测滞后、跨域协同不足等挑战，算力资源集约化利用和整体效能释放水平仍有提升空间。
为统筹调配全国算力资源，在工业和信息化部的指导下，全行业系统推进算力态势感知自动化监测体系建设，持续迭代升级中国算力平台功能。在去年8月举行的2025中国算力大会上，中国算力平台完成了10个省区市平台接入，实现了“平台、主体、资源、生态、场景”全面贯通，我国“全局总览、分域协同”的算力发展新格局初步形成。
在前期试点经验的基础上，中国算力平台加快拓面组网，有序推动全国31个省区市平台对接入网。中国算力平台建成统一规范、协同高效的全国算力态势感知监测体系，有效破除地域壁垒、打通数据孤岛，实现全国算力底数可摸清、态势可感知、运行可监测，推动算力建设从粗放式规模扩张向集约高效、全域协同跨越式升级。依托一体化监测能力，平台实时掌握全国算力运行态势，盘活存量算力资源，优化算力布局配置，提升算力整体利用效能，为政策制定、行业监管、产业创新提供坚实的数据支撑，夯实全国一体化算力网建设基础。
截至目前，中国算力平台算力超市运营层已汇聚注册企业用户超万家，入驻算力服务商逾200家，上架算力产品2000余项，接入各类大模型超300个，为广大开发者提供算力调用服务，累计沉淀数十亿条算力监测大数据，我国算力统筹治理迈入“全域监测、全网协同、全链调度”新阶段。
据悉，下一步，中国算力平台将持续提升全域态势感知能力，完善全国一体化协同调度机制，深化跨区域算力联动共享，加快推进一体化算力调度落地，充分发挥平台枢纽作用，持续赋能数字经济高质量发展。（记者　林婧）
