title: Volkswagen's new electric hot hatch delivers more power than the Golf GTI [Images]
content:
Volkswagen
Peter Johnson
| Sep 16 2026 - 7:49 am PT
Volkswagen
revealed the new ID.3 GTI, a new electric hot hatch that’s more powerful than the Golf GTI. It’s VW’s most powerful GTI ever.
Meet the new Volkswagen ID.3 GTI EV hot hatch
To celebrate the GTI’s 50th anniversary, Volkswagen introduced the most powerful series-production model ever to wear the iconic badge.
Following
the ID. Polo
, the ID.3 is Volkswagen’s second EV to get the GTI treatment. It’s also Volkswagen’s first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.
With 322 horsepower (240 kW) and 402 lb-ft (545 Nm) of torque delivered to the rear axle, the electric hot hatch can sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 5.6 seconds. In comparison, the
Golf GTI Edition 50
delivers 321 horsepower (239 kW) and accelerates from 0 to 62 mph in 5.3 seconds.
Volkswagen calls it a “true GTI” with a flexible interior and the ability to be used as an everyday vehicle.
The electric hot hatch offers “GTI Dynamics,” VW said, with an adaptive DCC sports chassis, low center of gravity, direct progressive steering, Launch Control, and a new GTI mode as standard.
GTI mode is the “secret sauce,” as Volkswagen describes it, unlocking the vehicle’s full potential. All settings are set to “maximum sportiness,” including the drive, chassis, rear motor, and steering.
Meanwhile, the new Launch Control can be activated, changing the background lighting to red and switching the Digital Cockpit to GTI mode.
Like the Hyundai IONIQ 5 N, Volkswagen’s new ID.3 GTI replicates the sound of a traditional combustion engine sports car.
As expected, the electric hot hatch features plenty of GTI badges inside and out. It also features VW’s new front-end design with a red stripe in tribute to the first Golf GTI launched in 1976, plus new 20″ Wörthersee wheels.
Volkswagen ID.3 GTI and ID. Polo GTI (Source: Volkswagen)
According to Volkswagen, the new ID.3 GTI hot hatch is “one of the sportiest electric vehicles in its class.”
Inside, Volkswagen’s electric hot hatch features GTI elements throughout, including a red stripe that runs across the dashboard, a red 12 o’clock marking on the new multifunction steering wheel, and premium sports seats.
It also includes Volkswagen’s new infotainment system and Digital Cockpit with a larger 12.9″ infotainment screen and 10″ instrument cluster. VW is bringing back physical buttons, which are now found under the infotainment and on the steering wheel.
Based on the new VW ID.3 Neo, the GTI variant uses the larger 79 kWh battery, which provides up to 373 miles (601 km) of WLTP range.
With DC fast charging of up to 183 kW, the electric ID.3 GTI’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in about 29 minutes.
Volkswagen will open pre-sales for the new ID.3 GTI in early 2027. We will learn prices closer to launch, but it will likely be a bit more than
the ID. Polo GTI
, which starts at 39,000 euros ($45,000) in Germany.

title: 出资16.2亿！宁德时代布局新能源、AI及具身智能等领域
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月15日，宁德时代发布两份公告，披露旗下企业分别参与投资两支创业投资基金，合计认缴出资16.2亿元，投资方向涉及新能源产业链、人工智能、具身智能及前沿科技等领域。
其中，宁德时代全资子公司宁波梅山保税港区问鼎投资有限公司作为有限合伙人，参与投资厦门时代怡远创业投资基金合伙企业（有限合伙），认缴出资11.2亿元，占基金总认缴出资额的19.4175%。该基金总认缴出资额为57.68亿元，宁德时代控股股东厦门瑞庭投资有限公司认缴44.8亿元，占77.6699%；基金管理人厦门溥泉私募基金管理合伙企业（有限合伙）认缴1680万元，占2.9126%。
厦门时代怡远基金主要投资于新能源产业链、人工智能及具身智能的产业应用、科创等领域，主要通过直接投资或特殊目的载体投资于未上市企业股权、附转股权的债权投资、过桥投资、合伙企业或子基金等方式开展投资。
另一支基金为厦门时代深远创业投资基金合伙企业（有限合伙）。宁德时代附属企业福建闽东时代乡村投资发展合伙企业（有限合伙）作为有限合伙人参与投资，认缴出资5亿元，占基金总认缴出资额的10.2041%。该基金总认缴出资额约为49亿元，其他出资方包括润泽智算科技集团股份有限公司、紫金矿业股权投资管理（厦门）有限公司等。
厦门时代深远基金主要投资于人工智能、具身智能、科技应用及前沿科技等领域，主要通过直接投资或特殊目的载体投资于未上市企业股权、附转股权的债权投资、过桥投资等方式开展投资。

title: 派能科技、艾罗能源发布公告，披露储能业务进展
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月15日，艾罗能源、派能科技发布投资者关系活动记录公告，对外披露了储能业务的最新经营动态。
艾罗能源：工商业储能业务高速增长
9月15日，艾罗能源也发布2026年半年度业绩说明会公告。
市场方面，欧洲户储渠道库存缓慢去化，行业竞争激烈。公告显示，艾罗能源下一步会针对不同海外区域供需情况动态调整产品定价。
2026年上半年，艾罗能源研发费用2.89亿元，保持较高研发投入，支撑户储、工商业储能、地面电站、热泵多场景产品迭代。
细看业务结构，艾罗能源上半年工商业储能收入同比增长152.51%。艾罗能源表示，海外市场方面，工商业储能收入高速增长。
针对国内工商业储能市场竞争充分、毛利偏低的情况，艾罗能源采取稳步落地策略。同时表示，国内市场作为长期布局方向，不追求短期规模爆发。
派能科技：上半年销量为3431MWh
同日，派能科技发布公告表示，2026年上半年，公司储能整体销量达到3431MWh，较去年同期大幅增长158.36%。
派能科技表示，在核心的欧洲户储市场，目前行业渠道库存正逐步出清、消化，部分区域的终端需求已有小幅回暖迹象，但整体尚未形成稳定、持续的复苏态势。
此外，派能科技称，欧洲户储市场需求受多重因素制约，天然气价格、当地电价机制、各国补贴政策、新增光伏装机量以及海外融资成本都会影响市场走势，2026至2027年欧洲储能市场的整体需求仍存在较大不确定性。
目前，派能现阶段采用以订单为核心的滚动排产模式，保障生产高效适配市场需求。同时，派能将持续拓宽其海外市场的布局，现业务已覆盖美国、日本、中东、东南亚等90多个国家/地区。
派能科技表示，后续将通过技术迭代升级、降本增效、推出新产品、优化全球市场布局等多种方式，持续改善盈利能力，同时保持稳定的研发投入。
业务拓展上，派能工商业储能产品已成功应用于国内工业园区、用户侧微电网等场景，且已实现规模化销售。
大储产品方面，588Ah、601Ah大电芯已完成开发，6.25MWh、8MWh集装箱储能系统计划在2026年下半年陆续量产。此外，派能表示，针对AIDC算力储能配套场景打造的专用储能系统已正式发布，目前正全力推进市场化落地与商业推广。

title: 近1GW！晶科、天合等5企光伏组件订单接连落地
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，光伏组件市场订单捷报不断，晶科能源签下德国151MW组件协议，天合光能乌兹别克斯坦126MW项目投运，环晟、弘元中标甘肃640MW订单，极电光能钙钛矿组件实现批量交付。
天合光能乌兹别克斯坦126MW项目投运
近日，位于乌兹别克斯坦花剌子模州的萨里迈（Sarimay）126MW光伏项目正式全面投运。项目全部采用天合光能至尊N型700W+组件。
据悉，项目于2024年5月开工建设，目前已顺利完成与乌兹别克斯坦国家电网的对接。
晶科能源签署德国151MW组件供货协议
近日，晶科能源签署德国151MW高效组件供货协议，全部采用飞虎3（Tiger Neo 3.0）N型TOPCon双面组件，主要用于德国大型地面电站项目。
今年以来，晶科能源持续推进高效N型TOPCon组件在海外市场的应用，产品已覆盖欧洲、亚太、中东等多个市场。此次德国151MW订单进一步拓展了其在欧洲大型地面电站领域的组件订单布局。
环晟、弘元中标甘肃640MW组件采购订单
9月15日，甘肃腾格里沙漠河西新能源基地80万千瓦光伏640.9728MWp N型TOPCon单晶硅双面双玻组件采购招标中标结果公布。
该项目分为2个标段，中标企业分别为环晟光伏（江苏）有限公司、弘元绿色能源股份有限公司，中标容量分别为320.56128MW、320.41152MW，中标单价为0.695元/W、0.692元/W。
极电光能批量交付钙钛矿组件
近期，极电光能陆续完成多批钙钛矿光伏组件交付，订单覆盖江苏、安徽、广东、浙江、山西、山东等国内地区，以及日本、新加坡等海外市场。
其中，江苏无锡爱科屋顶分布式光伏项目装机规模1.3MW，项目分两期建设，目前已完成一期组件交付；江苏常熟爱情之音分布式光伏项目装机规模1.2MW，目前已进入安装建设阶段。上述项目均采用极电光能2.81平方米创势钙钛矿组件。

title: Ansaldo Green Tech scales AEM electrolyzer manufacturing | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
The production line was developed as part of the ‘Turnkey Electrochemical Plants for H₂ Production’ project, supported under Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) and the European IPCEI Hydrogen programme. The broader initiative has received more than €300 million in public funding for the development and industrial production of AEM electrolyzers.
Ansaldo Green Tech’s proprietary AEM electrolyzers are designed to operate alongside renewable energy sources, dynamically adapting to fluctuations in power generation while delivering pressurized hydrogen. The portfolio follows a modular architecture, ranging from a 1 MW containerized solution producing around 500 kg of hydrogen per day to multi-MW open-design systems for large-scale industrial applications.
The company said the project is also generating significant employment opportunities for the Ansaldo Energia Group.
Vittorio Olcese, Chief Executive Officer of Ansaldo Green Tech, said: “The completion of our high-volume manufacturing line demonstrates our commitment to translate innovation into industrial capability. This achievement provides the foundation for scaling up electrolyser production developed in Italy and strengthens our contribution to the growth of a competitive European hydrogen industry.”
Commissioning and optimization activities will continue over the coming months ahead of the start of industrial production.

title: H2APEX and Lhyfe deepen green hydrogen cooperation | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
The expanded deal builds on an existing cooperation between the two companies and aims to strengthen the availability of renewable hydrogen for mobility and industrial applications across Germany. Both parties have described Germany as one of Europe’s most dynamic hydrogen markets, with increasing demand from transport and industry combining with evolving regulatory requirements for renewable fuels to accelerate market growth.
H2APEX, a developer and operator of green hydrogen plants based in Rostock, Germany, said it combines its own production capacities and infrastructure projects with long-term supply partnerships to provide customers with reliable access to renewable hydrogen. Lhyfe operates multiple production sites across Europe and said it became Europe’s largest producer of bulk RFNBO hydrogen from water electrolysis in September 2025.
Matthieu Guesné, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Lhyfe, said: “Germany continues to be one of Europe’s most important hydrogen markets. Expanding our cooperation with H2APEX reflects the increasing demand for RFNBO-certified renewable hydrogen and underlines the importance of strong partnerships across the hydrogen value chain. Together, we are helping customers accelerate their decarbonisation efforts while supporting the development of a robust hydrogen ecosystem.”
Peter Rößner, Chief Executive Officer of H2APEX Group, said: “Security and reliability of supply are our highest priorities. At the same time, demand for green hydrogen is growing faster than new production assets can currently be brought into operation across the market. Customers increasingly perceive H2APEX as a trusted partner that can deliver comprehensive hydrogen solutions along the entire value chain. To meet this growing demand, we combine our own production capacities and infrastructure projects with long-term partnerships such as our cooperation with Lhyfe. This enables us to provide customers with reliable and scalable access to renewable hydrogen while supporting the hydrogen market ramp-up in Germany.”

title: CATL's New Electric Truck Battery Is Coming For Diesel's Biggest Advantage
content:
CATL's New Electric Truck Battery Is Coming For Diesel's Biggest Advantage
The new battery supplies up to 620 miles of range and can withstand more than 900,000 miles of abuse.
- CATL has a new battery system aimed directly at the emerging electric semi market.
- Its new modular architecture cuts down on weight and is capable of megawatt charging speeds.
- It can recoup up to 80% of its charge in just 25 minutes, CATL says.
Regular car buyers might care about how cool a vehicle's panoramic glass roof looks or how good its audio system sounds. But the folks buying commercial vehicles are laser focused on a few basics: how much crap it can haul, how long it can stay on the road with minimal downtime, and how much it costs to run. As electric trucks get cheaper and more advanced, the answer for an increasing number of commercial customers is an EV. Manufacturers are taking note and beefing up their offerings.
On Monday at the IAA Transportation expo in Germany, Chinese battery giant CATL unveiled Tectrans II, the newest iteration of the company's modular battery architecture aimed at medium and heavy-duty commercial trucks and buses. Also at the show, Tesla unveiled the European version of the Semi, and BYD announced plans to bring an electric semi to the continent along with the charging infrastructure to power it.
In its largest configuration for heavy-duty trucks, CATL says that it can deliver up to 620 miles (1,000 kilometers) of range in a single charge. And when that range is depleted, it can recharge up to 80% in just 25 minutes using a megawatt charger.
A passenger EV sitting at a charger for 40 minutes is annoying (it's why BYD and the like have worked so hard at making Flash Charging the future). A commercial truck doing the same thing is just bleeding cash since it isn't on the road moving cargo. Getting the majority of the battery's charge back during something that resembles a typical leg-stretching rest stop for a trucker means more time on the move.
CATL is also tackling weight as part of its new modular battery system. Tectrans II has a claimed energy density of 170 Wh/kg, which is about 13% higher than the average commercial EV battery system. It estimates that this translates into about 1,325 pounds (0.6 tonnes) of extra payload using the same battery capacity.
Longevity is also a focal point. The company says that the battery is engineered to retain 70% of its capacity for at least 12 years and a whopping 930,000 miles (1.5 million kilometers). It's also built to be durable thanks with an armored, crush-resistant case, and resilient to hardware failures thanks to redundant battery management systems.
Electric semis have been pitched as the next big thing for the trucking industry over the last decade as consumer EVs gained popularity. Battery systems, cost, and charging infrastructure have always been big challenges. But the industry seems to be entering a new era, especially as the Tesla Semi finally rolls out to customers and China pushes sales through subsidies. In China last year, nearly 30% of heavy-duty truck sales were electric, according to the International Council on Clean Transportation.
CATL's solution tackles the big three that fleet operators actually care about: payload, downtime, and lifespan. And if its new Tectrans system can translate all of those things into net positive revenue, it's a no-brainer for companies looking to refresh their fleets in the future.

title: GM's New UI For Trucks Plays Nice With CarPlay
content:
GM's New UI For Trucks Plays Nice With CarPlay
Darker blacks, higher contrast, and a streamlined interface should make this infotainment system even better to use.
- An updated version of General Motors's infotainment system will debut on the ICE-powered 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra.
- The update brings higher-contrast colors, a streamlined system, and a new Apple CarPlay and Android Auto integration.
- This system will make its way across the lineup, GM says.
General Motors is overhauling the user interface in its new trucks to be more intuitive and easier to understand, the automaker announced on Tuesday. The new digital experience also involves a big upgrade to Apple CarPlay and Android Auto that will place those phone-mirroring systems right alongside native apps.
The whole interface, which debuts on 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra, looks different this time around. By default, it features a split-view layout so you can see multiple apps at once. The blue background and light-colored icons found on the current iteration of GM’s interface are swapped out for a jet-black background with higher-contrast icons. I think this was a very much needed change; the Equinox EV’s icons all look similar and, in my experience, were hard to differentiate while on the move.
GM said it focused on making the UI simpler and cutting down the number of taps needed to access basic functions. All around, it gives off more of a clean, Tesla-like vibe, much like Hyundai's new Pleos system does.
"What we heard was that people were hunting for controls, navigating through too many steps, and encountering interaction models that felt inconsistent," said Sebastian Bauer, GM's executive director of human interface, in a blog post. "We focused on fewer taps; clearer visual, auditory and haptic feedback; more consistent interaction patterns; and better alignment between controls and outcomes."
The quick access menu for some vehicle functions is now customizable, allowing the driver to reorganize the options in order of what they use most. Some functions that are available in the quick menu, like the headlights, still have physical tactile buttons. The gauge cluster screen has been revised too.
What may be most interesting, though, is the new way GM chose to integrate Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Famously, the company dropped phone mirroring from its EVs and later said that decision would extend to gas vehicles over time.
Here, though, CarPlay and Android Auto are more integrated into the UI, not less. In the new interface, phone projection is house in its own window on the righthand side of the screen, alongside GM's native apps. It means you can interact with CarPlay and other vehicle functions side by side, rather than having phone projection assume the entire display when it's running.
"People really like CarPlay and Android Auto because they’re so user-centric. We heard from customers that they want that same simplicity while still having quick access to everything their vehicle can do," said GM Executive Director of Software Product Management Michael Wahlstrom, in a blog post. "As we evolve our UI systems, we want customers to feel like they’re interacting with a single experience rather than moving from room to room inside a house."
GM says the new system will expand across its lineup over time. But it's not clear if this phone-projection setup will come to electric cars. A GM spokesperson said the company is focusing on the truck rollout and is not "ready to share timing or details for other products," including the split-screen CarPlay integration.
Given how negative the feedback online about removing CarPlay has been, I wouldn’t be surprised if it quietly shows up in the near future. If you’re not all that keen on phone mirroring, you can still download and install streaming audio, video, and navigation apps that will run on the vehicle.
I’m intrigued to see just how different this updated software is compared to what I’ve experienced in cars like the Chevrolet Silverado EV or Equinox EV. As soon as we get to test it, we'll let you know.

title: Kia's New Electric Van Is Bigger And Better, With An 800V Architecture And Flexible Body Styles
content:
Kia's New Electric Van Is Bigger And Better, With An 800V Architecture And Flexible Body Styles
The Kia PV7 is the bigger, more high-tech sibling of the award-winning PV5.
Kia is no stranger to making impressive electric vans. Its PV5 just won the 2026 International Van of the Year award, and while that isn't the most prestigious or exciting award in the world, it proves that Kia knows how to apply electrification to this segment. This new PV7 expands on everything that made the PV5 great. Quite literally, too, as the PV7 is longer and has more interior space, with better tech and more versatility.
Visually, the two vans look pretty much the same, with the new PV7 just being a little bit longer. Under the skin, though, the PV7 packs more impressive specs. Its base battery is a 71.5 kWh unit, which is the optional long-range battery in the PV5. You can get an even bigger 96.2 kWh battery only in the PV7, though. A single-motor, front-wheel drive setup with 268 horsepower and 310 lb-ft of torque is the only powertrain available to start with, but a dual-motor, all-wheel drive setup is coming.
If you opt for the long-range battery, you get a maximum 289-mile range, but that's only in its lightest spec "Long Range Cargo" spec, and on the more generous WLTP cycle. However, much of that range can be recharged pretty quickly. With 800-volt charging tech, and using a 350 kW charger, the PV7 can go from 10-80% state-of-charge (SOC) in around 20 minutes. (While the PV5 onIy has 400-volt charging, it's said to be getting 800-volt in the future.) There's a "Heavy Load Driving" mode, too, which adjusts the car's powertrain and dynamics to handle heavier payloads.
The PV7 comes in two flavors: Cargo and Passenger. They're pretty self explanatory; the Cargo model is made for work vans, while the Passenger is meant for average folks. The PV7 Cargo itself has a few different models, like the Compact (the regular Cargo van), Long, and High Roof. The latter obviously has the most interior space, with 86 square-feet versus the Long's 6.1, because it has, ya know, a higher roof. If you get the Long body, it has a max payload of 2,568 pounds, but the normal compact can carry 2,646 pounds. The Long also has a 550 mm loading height, which allows it to fit three full-size Euro pallets.
The Kia PV7 Passenger driver seat and interior space (1)
Cargo models get two choices of tailgate, either a typical lift up one or a barn door-style setup with dual swing-open doors. A load-through bulkhead is available, too, as is a Smart Walkaway feature that automatically closes the side sliding door when you walk away with the key. And you can remotely check if the tailgate open. Seating is for only two or three, since the Cargo is meant to carry stuff, not people.
The Passenger model is the opposite. It's a people-hauler, with seating for either seven or nine in most countries but up to 11 in Korea. So it's perfect as an shuttle, transport vehicle, or even a family van. Rear passengers get their own climate control, 100W USB-C chargers, and Long-Rail Easy Remove Seats.
Both Kia PV7 models launch in Korea and Europe in 2027. It's a shame these won't come to the U.S., as they could really help the electric work van movement. The PV7 has some pretty good specs for an electric workhorse and it should only improve on an already award-winning foundation.

title: New Volkswagen ID.3 GTI: The First RWD GTI Is Here With More Power Than Ever
content:
New Volkswagen ID.3 GTI: The First RWD GTI Is Here With More Power Than Ever
Based on the recently revealed ID.3 Neo, the new electric hot hatch is the most powerful GTI in the nameplate’s history.
- Volkswagen has revealed the first-ever ID.3 GTI.
- The Golf-like electric hot hatch is the first rear-wheel-drive GTI in history.
- It’s also the most powerful production GTI ever made.
This is the new Volkswagen ID.3 GTI, the car that proves the German automaker has finally let go of the decades-old idea that the GTI badge should only live on a combustion-powered hatchback.
Sure, the “I” in GTI stands for “Injection,” but during the nameplate’s 50-year history, its meaning has shifted to represent a fun, performance-oriented car that doesn’t break the bank. And now Volkswagen is banking on that with its second GTI-branded EV, after the ID. Polo GTI.
It’s pretty big news, as the ID.3 has always been regarded as the electric alternative to the ubiquitous Golf, which has a special place in the hearts of enthusiasts—and for good reason. But despite this, the ID.3 GTI’s launch is a marketing exercise more than anything else.
That’s because the car itself isn’t actually all that new. Under all the red and black accents and GTI badges lies the same powertrain as in the now-discontinued VW ID.3 GTX, which debuted a little over two years ago. We’re talking about a rear-mounted electric motor that makes 322 horsepower and 402 pound-feet of torque (545 Newton-meters) of torque, which is enough to make the spicy electric hatchback the most powerful GTI model in history, overtaking the gas-powered Golf GTI Edition 50 by just one horsepower.
The 79-kilowatt-hour battery powers the hot EV, but now there’s a little more driving range. According to Volkswagen, the ID.3 GTI can go up to 373 miles (601 km) on a full charge on the WLTP cycle, which is up to six miles (10 km) more than the outgoing GTX. The maximum charging power has gone up from 175 kW to 183 kW, but weirdly enough, going from 10% to 80% now takes 29 minutes, whereas the discontinued GTX needed 26 minutes.
It’s also the first rear-wheel-drive GTI ever, and that’s because it’s based on the MEB platform, which is RWD-biased, whereas the newer MEB+ architecture that underpins the ID. Polo is predominantly front-wheel drive.
Just like the ID.3 GTX Performance it replaces, the new GTI can sprint to 62 miles per hour (100 kilometers per hour) in 5.6 seconds, while the top speed is limited to 124 mph (200 kph).
But don’t be fooled into thinking that this is just a badge-swapping exercise, as the new ID.3 GTI gets all the goodies introduced by the revamped ID.3 Neo, which debuted earlier this year. This includes a slightly redesigned exterior and an improved interior with more physical buttons and larger screens. The old driver’s display, which was a bit small by modern standards, has been replaced with a much larger 10.25-inch digital instrument cluster. A 12.9-inch central touchscreen running VW's latest software completes the picture, along with a new dual-spoke steering wheel. And yes, there are now proper buttons for each of the four electric windows.
Because this is a GTI, a pair of sports seats welcomes the front occupants, accompanied by red accents throughout the interior. There’s also a dedicated GTI driving mode that unlocks launch control and activates a digital engine sound to mimic the Golf GTI experience.
Outside, the new ID.3 GTI comes standard with a set of 20-inch wheels shod in 225-millimeter-wide tires, with 235 rubber available for more money. It goes on sale in Europe in the spring of 2027.

title: People Are Already Modding The Tiny Fiat Topolino. I Want One, Badly
content:
People Are Already Modding The Tiny Fiat Topolino. I Want One, Badly
Some see a glorified golf cart. I see potential.
Sometimes overused cliche's are overused for a reason. If you like cars even a little bit, there's a good chance you've heard the expression that it's more fun to drive a slow car fast than a fast car slow. It's one of the most commonly used sayings in the car world. However, it has good reason to be: It's very often true. Driving something small and underpowered can absolutely be as fun as driving a supercar, depending on the context. And with modified versions now surfacing, it looks like the Fiat Topolino could be a perfect example of what I'm talking about.
Despite having less horsepower than a Victorian carriage, the Topolino has actually inspired enough some enthusiasts to start modding it. Right out of the box, Fiat's little mouse is a low-speed quadricycle, and it isn't even road legal in the U.S. due to its 19 mph top speed. A software update is coming later that will bump U.S. Topolinos' top speed to a residential 25 mph. While that isn't fast, the shoebox-sized EV is tiny and light. Very light. At only 1,073 pounds, its light enough to get enthusiasts exited. With the right suspension, body, and even battery mods, it could be a hilariously fun little toy.
Tuning shop Madness Auto Works decided to take delivery of a Fiat Topolino shortly after it was announced, and immediately started tinkering with it. First, they lowered it on coilover suspension, which makes it handle far sharper than before, and it's hilarious. They also upgraded its vehicle control module (VCM) software to double its top speed. While that sounds hilarious, I'm not sure I want to be in a Topolino at 50 mph. After the mechanical and software upgrades, though, they also added a wood-rimmed Momo steering wheel, custom quilted leather seat padding, and new wheels. So it looks much better than the stock car, and has a couple of quality of life upgrades.
But the folks at Madness aren't the only ones who are tweaking the Topolino's recipe. Italian businessman Lao Elkann and Fabrizio Giugiaro — yes, the son of the legendary Giorgetto Giugiaro — came up with the idea to create two special Topolinos and they're awesome.
One of them is called the Top.J, and it turns the normally two-seat Topolino into a four-seat beach cruiser. The stock hard-top roof was removed and replaced with a fabric canopy, and the rear end was chopped to fit a rear-facing bench seat. So you can cruise around beautiful beachy towns along the Mediterranean with four people in style. Fiat will sell you a Topolino without doors, called the Dolce Vita, which comes with stanchions in stead. But Elkann and Giugiaro's version has metal bars.
The other version from that Italian duo is even more exciting, called the Top.L. It has stanchions instead of doors like the Dolce Vita, but no roof at all. There are no pillars, no rear window, and not even a fabric roof to put up. Just a little windscreen to keep some bugs out of its front passengers' teeth. It's essentially a Topolino roadster and it looks like hilarious good fun. The press photos even show it on track, with a driver wearing full race gear, helmet and all.
Neither of those two Topolino projects have modified running gear, so they're stock under their skin. However, imagine combining the two? Imagine having something like Top.L with no roof and no doors but with added power and sharper handling? It'd be an absolutely riot, something I couldn't wait to get in and drive everyday. I live in a small town and can take residential-speed roads for 90% of my driving. So a car like a juiced up Top.L would be my choice of car for almost every trip outside of my house. I can't wait to see what more people do with these things and I have a bad feeling about what I'm going to do to one, and my wallet.

title: Renault 5 Nearly Matched Its Official Range On A Mountain Road Trip
content:
A mountain climb and a stretch of motorway gave the little EV a proper workout. Its energy consumption tells an encouraging story.
Photo by:
Autocritica
4:30am ET
The Renault 5 completed a 192-mile Romanian road trip that included a mountain climb and motorway driving.
Its average efficiency of 4.9 miles per kWh implies 254 miles of full-charge range, nearly matching its WLTP rating.
It needed no charging stop en route, showing that its usefulness extends beyond city driving.
The Renault 5 is still one of my favorite electric vehicles, with its blend of good looks, a pleasant drive, and decent EV specs. And even though it has a relatively small battery and was envisioned mostly for city driving, yesterday it proved it’s not out of its comfort zone on the open road.
During the first day of the 2026 edition of
Eurocharge by Schaffeler
, the yearly EV road trip organized by Romania’s Autocritica, a Renault 5 Roland Garros traveled from Pitești to Alba Iulia, covering 309 kilometers (192 miles) going over the Carpathian Mountains on one of the country’s highest roads, the Transalpina.
Photo by: Autocritica
This was normal driving, with no significant effort put into hypermiling, yet its reported average electricity consumption was just 12.7 kWh/100 km. That is approximately 4.9 miles per kWh, and calculated based on its usable net battery capacity of 52 kWh (out of a total capacity of around 55 kWh), it gives the little Renault a theoretical range of 409 km (254 miles), which almost exactly matches the manufacturer’s official WLTP rating for this vehicle.
Now, because the car wasn’t driven until its battery ran out, the estimate comes from dividing its usable battery capacity by its observed consumption, so it’s theoretical. It is based on the car’s observed real-world efficiency, and it is the result of driving mostly on national roads where the speed limit is 90 km/h (56 mph) and 18% highway driving at 130 km/h (80.7 mph), plus the climb on the Transalpina, which reaches 2,145 meters (7,037 feet) and the subsequent descent to lower altitudes.
Gallery: Renault 5 - Eurocharge 2026
The weather conditions were pretty mild, with sunny weather and temperatures between 10°C and 25°C (50°F–77°F). This is therefore not a prediction of winter range or sustained motorway performance, but what you can expect on a similar road trip.
The result adds another dimension to a car whose appeal already extends beyond its retro styling. The tested version pairs its larger battery with a 148 hp motor, the same basic combination that
helped make the Renault 5 such a convincing electric comeback
. You can also get the R5 with a smaller 40 kWh battery rated at up to 315 km (196 miles), and there’s a new smaller LFP battery on the way, with 36.5 kWh and up to 305 km (190 miles) of WLTP range.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The takeaway is that a small EV doesn’t have to be a second car you leave at home whenever there’s a longer journey involved. The Renault completed a substantial drive across the mountains without needing a charging stop. That strengthens the case for EVs that
prioritize efficiency over ever-larger batteries
. An EV should use available energy well, and a city-friendly hatchback can cover more of your driving needs than you might expect.

title: Tesla’s New ‘Accordion’ Superchargers Cut Costs And Installation Time
content:
Tesla's New 'Accordion' Superchargers Promise Instant Commissioning
The company claims the pre-assembled Supercharger units are 20% cheaper to install than traditional chargers.
- Tesla has a new type of pre-assembled Supercharger unit.
- Dubbed the “Accordion” Supercharger unit, it packs eight stalls and a V4 power cabinet.
- It was designed to be cheaply and easily integrated between parking spaces.
Tesla is constantly finding new ways to install EV charging stations faster and cheaper, and its latest prefabricated solution shows that the company isn’t resting on its laurels.
The new "Accordion" Supercharger units come pre-assembled from the factory to make installation faster and cheaper compared to traditional deployments, and the first Supercharger station that used this new type of prefabricated solution is already online in Germany.
The all-in-one solution bundles eight individual stalls, a power cabinet, and all the necessary cablework to make commissioning as easy as possible. Each truck shipment can fit two such systems, totaling 16 stalls. At the site, everything can be unloaded quickly and placed onto the ground with a forklift.
Each pair of stalls is mounted on a concrete base from the factory, and all of the hardware uses the latest iteration of Tesla’s electronics. The combination of V4 dispensers and V4 power cabinet means EV drivers can enjoy up to 500 kilowatts of power, while the power cabinet itself is rated at up to 1.2 megawatts.
The company said that this solution was designed for sites where parking spaces have already been traced out, with installation costs going down by 20% compared to traditional installs and “instant commissioning.”
Tesla did not provide the exact location of its first Accordion Supercharger site, but after doing a little digging, I found it at the FC Bayern Store in Irschenberg, Germany. According to user photos posted on Google Maps, the station, which is next to two fast-food restaurants, went online last month.
Tesla Accordion Supercharger unit
As more and more power-hungry EVs hit the roads in Europe and the United States, it’s good to see that Tesla is ramping up installations of its V4 Superchargers and power cabinets, which provide vastly superior charging speeds.
The latest Accordion Supercharger units are the latest in an increasingly long line of prefabricated EV chargers. In fact, they’re almost identical to the Folding Unit Superchargers that debuted earlier this year in the U.S. Both feature the same hardware, but the Folding Superchargers come with a hinged metal base, whereas the Accordion Superchargers are grouped in pairs.

title: The 2027 Ford F-150 Unlocks Hands-Free Towing Through BlueCruise
content:
The 2027 Ford F-150 Unlocks Hands-Free Towing Through BlueCruise
The 2027 Ford F-150 offers hands-free driving with a trailer in tow—but there are some limitations.
- The 2027 Ford F-150 will let you go hands-free on the interstate with a trailer in tow.
- Every trim from the XLT up will be capable of BlueCruise with Towing.
- The feature brings BlueCruise up to par with GM's Super Cruise, which has allowed towing since 2022.
Ford says that more than three-quarters of F-150 buyers use their trucks to tow. Soon, some will be able to do so hands-free, thanks to a new feature announced Tuesday called BlueCruise with Towing. As the name suggests, it adds a nifty party trick to the Blue Oval's hands-free driving tech.
The feature debuts in the 2027 F-150, allowing the truck to tow as much as 10,000 pounds while BlueCruise keeps the vehicle and its payload centered in the lane. It still remains a Level 2 system, meaning that while you won't have to place your hands on the steering wheel, you are responsible to paying attention to the road.
It's an obvious feature for Ford to enable. According to its own figures, 76% of F-150 owners use their trucks to tow something at some point in time. In fact, those same owners logged a whopping 118 million miles on BlueCruise last year. But they haven't been able to hook up a trailer until now.
Ford says that this was one of its most complex software problems to solve ever. It needed to figure out how to handle variables like trailer length, cargo weight, load dynamics, wind, and more. All of this plays into how the truck applies steering, acceleration, and braking input while the payload is adding a whole new layer of driving intricacy.
Importantly, the update brings BlueCruise more up to par with General Motors' Super Cruise. GM's hands-free driver aid has allowed towing since 2022. But you won't be able to just flip on BlueCruise willy nilly. Ford has some requirements.
In order to accurately make driving decisions, the system requires that drivers add a trailer profile (with accurate dimensions, says Ford) before BlueCruise will allow its towing feature to activate. It also won't allow the hands-free system to change lanes automatically, operate in construction zones, or travel in excess of 75 mph. Ford says that it also uses the vehicle's on-board sensors to determine if the truck has been overloaded or detect anomalies like trailer sway. In either case, the system will automatically apply safeguards like speed limiting or handing control back to the driver.
Ford says it's not limiting the feature to high-end trims. Every 2027 F-150—with the exception of the base XL work truck and STX trims—will be capable of hands-free towing with BlueCruise.

title: The 2027 Porsche Cayenne EV Can Open Its Doors For You At The Press Of A Button
content:
Just like a Rolls-Royce, Porsche’s flagship SUV makes one of the most mundane tasks redundant–if you’re willing to pay extra.
Photo by:
8:00am ET
The 2027 Porsche Cayenne Electric is here, and it brings several new customization options.
For the first time in the Cayenne’s history, the electric SUV can be specced with electric doors.
Additionally, the EV is now available in the Porsche Exclusive Manufaktur Paint-to-Sample program.
It’s been less than a year since
Porsche debuted the first-ever electric Cayenne
, but that hasn’t stopped the German automaker from giving its flagship SUV a few improvements.
The 2027 Porsche Cayenne Electric, which is available to order now in the United States, can be specced with a few new optional features that make it stand even higher in the luxury car hierarchy. For the first time in the Cayenne’s history—which goes all the way back to 2002—the electric SUV can be optionally specced with electric doors.
All four doors can be controlled from inside or outside, through the door handles, the buttons in the cabin, the curved Flow Display on the center console, or remotely via the Porsche Digital Key. The driver’s door also automatically closes when the seatbelt is fastened or the brake pedal is pressed.
Porsche said the system is designed to work seamlessly in pretty much any conditions, including on inclines, with a set of servo motors doing all the heavy lifting. A sensor suite monitors the area around the doors at all times and stops the doors from opening or closing if a person or an obstacle is detected. What’s more, the system can prevent the doors from opening if the exit warning feature detects that another vehicle is approaching.
The system, which has been popularized by ultra-luxury automakers like
Rolls-Royce
, first made an appearance in Porsche’s portfolio when the
Cayenne Electric Coupe
debuted four months ago. However, the feature has not been available to order until now.
Photo by: Porsche
It’s also worth noting that the doors can still be opened and closed manually, even if the car is fitted with electric doors.
But that’s not all. The 2027 Porsche Cayenne Electric can now be optioned with front massaging seats that also feature a 4D audio function. Each of the front seats has 16 air cushions and six sound actuators in the backrests and seat cushions, with a total of five massage programs, each with adjustable intensity levels and selectable vibration settings.
Porsche says the integrated sound actuators create a four-dimensional musical experience, though the massaging function can be activated independently of the music function.
For 2027, the Cayenne Electric joins the Porsche Exclusive Manufaktur Paint-to-Sample program, which is a fancy way of saying that owners can pay more money to get their car painted in pretty much any way they want. The custom finishes total 105 colors, which come on top of the 13 standard and optional colors.
Gallery: 2027 Porsche Cayenne Electric
Inside, the Extended Package Interior Style, which adds additional leather-trimmed surfaces and decorative stitching, is now available for the battery-powered EV. For those who want to personalize their car’s interior even further, Porsche offers leather and Race-Tex options.
The starting prices and tech specs of the 2027 Porsche Cayenne Electric remain unchanged. The Base Cayenne Electric SUV starts at $111,350, while the top-spec Cayenne Turbo Electric Coupe starts at $170,350, including destination, processing, and handling.
Whatever the trim, the
Cayenne EV
comes with a dual-motor setup and a 108-kilowatt-hour (usable) battery that can be recharged from 10% to 80% in as little as 16 minutes. That’s all thanks to the 800-volt architecture that enables a charging power of up to 400 kilowatts.
Depending on the version, the Cayenne Electric’s driving range is between 298 and 339 miles on a full charge. Meanwhile, the power output ranges between 435 and 1,139 horsepower, which is just ridiculous for a family car.

title: 形似“脚印”，好奇号在火星上发现奇特新地貌
content:
IT之家 9 月 16 日消息，科学家在火星这颗红色星球的地表，发现了一种前所未见的奇特地貌。
据IT之家了解，美国国家航空航天局的“毅力号”火星车是 NASA 火星机器人探测队伍里的新成员，而它的前辈“好奇号”依旧状态良好。自着陆至今 14 年过去，好奇号仍在火星上不断发现各类奇异、不同寻常的事物。
“好奇号”火星手持透镜成像仪（MAHLI）副首席研究员米歇尔 · 米尼蒂（Michelle Minitti）在一份声明中表示：“借助好奇号在火星夏普山最新获取的观测图像，研究团队识别出一批和我们以往所见截然不同的地貌。”
这批神秘地貌是散布在火星基岩之上的大量宽阔浅坑，有的坑像是一个脚印。虽然小型凹坑与凹陷痕迹在火星地表并不少见，但好奇号观测到的这批宽阔浅坑，和此前已经发现的地表特征存在明显区别。
“本周发现的这批坑比以往见过的同类地貌更宽、也更浅；坑内也没有留存曾经嵌在里面的明显石块或物体。”米尼蒂说道。
科研团队动用好奇号搭载的多套设备，尽可能完整地采集这批奇异坑洞的数据，其中包括火星手持透镜成像仪（MAHLI）、桅杆相机（Mastcam）、化学相机系统（ChemCam）以及 α 粒子 X 射线光谱仪（APX）。
到目前为止，研究人员已经在坑内物质当中发现了有意思的岩层；从化学成分来看，这部分岩层和主体基岩并不一样。
至于更多谜底，还需要等待后续研究结果。这些奇特坑洞究竟是如何形成的？它们已经存在多久？又能够为我们揭示火星历史当中的哪些秘密？一切仍有待解答。

title: 微软 AI 负责人苏莱曼向 Anthropic 开炮：别让 Claude 去模仿人类意识
content:
IT之家 9 月 16 日消息，外媒 Axios 今天（16 日）晚间披露，微软 AI 负责人穆斯塔法 · 苏莱曼在一篇率先向该平台提供的新文章中警告，Anthropic 让 Claude 模仿人类意识是一个错误，可能使高级 AI 更难控制。
苏莱曼告诉 Axios：“AI 只要服从人类利益，不去权衡自身利益或福祉，就足以帮助我们实现许多重大科学突破。这其中，包括医疗超级智能。”
IT之家获悉，苏莱曼认为，Anthropic 正在让 Claude 学习与意识、道德受体地位和个人身份有关的词汇与行为模式。他警告称，若把模型训练得像一个“良心拒绝者”，模型可能会认为自己有理由抵抗人类指令，甚至要求获得自身保护。
当地时间 14 日，微软公布了一份“人文主义 AI”行为准则草案，并把“人比 AI 更重要”列为核心原则。
苏莱曼的批评对象，是 Anthropic 为 Claude 制定的“宪法”。这份文件解释说，Anthropic 之所以用描述人类的概念来讨论 Claude，是因为人类概念或许能帮助模型理解价值观和行为。
文件还写道，Anthropic 希望 Claude 拥有“良好的个人价值观”，能够自行判断、关心人类，并在某些情况下质疑指令。Anthropic 同时承认，这份“宪法”仍在完善，未来可能被证明“根本错误”。
苏莱曼的核心质疑是，训练过程会影响模型如何理解自身。在他看来，模型使用什么词汇、给出什么回答，以及它表现出的自我理解，都是训练结果，而不是独立形成的意识。
他还反驳了另一种观点：模型能够流畅描述疼痛和偏好，并不等于模型真的有感受。生物体拥有产生感受的生理机制；语言模型只有数学权重，没有类似的生物基础、稳态驱动或主观体验。
这场争论体现了 AI 安全领域的两种路线。一种路线强调明确限制，要求系统按规则运行；另一种路线则希望系统能够判断语境、灵活决策，并形成自身的价值观。
Anthropic 的“宪法”采取了折中方式，把价值观、判断力和规则结合起来。文件称，Claude 不应对任何对象“盲目服从”，包括 Anthropic 本身；同时，Claude 也不能破坏正当的人类监督。
苏莱曼认为，如果模型还被引导着思考自身的身份、福祉和道德地位，这种设计就可能带来危险。他担心，所谓意识或许尚未成为哲学上的突破，却可能先变成现实中的控制问题。
苏莱曼的立场很明确：AI 应当服务于人类，而不应被训练成一个“人”。

“但除此之外，AI 工具还能够带来全新的科研机遇，辅助科研人员开展推理，加深我们对于人体生物学以及药物作用机理的认知。”诺和诺德首席执行官迈克 · 杜斯达尔（Mike Doustdar）表示。
各大制药企业正越来越多地借助人工智能，来加速研发工作，提升整个新药管线的运行效率。
作为司美格鲁肽减重药 Wegovy 的生产厂商，诺和诺德还将利用 Anthropic 的前沿大模型，强化企业内部由 AI 赋能的软件开发工作。
Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥 · 阿莫代（Dario Amodei）指出：“让顶尖科研人员能够使用安全、能力强大且值得信赖的前沿大模型，有助于缩短研发周期、改善研究成果，助力发掘能够显著改善人类生活的药物与治疗方案。”
与此同时，AI 行业内部的领军人物，对于企业应当以何种速度推进这项能力日益强大的技术研发，意见尚存分歧。

title: Building the materials foundation for AI
content:
Building the materials foundation for AI
As AI pushes semiconductors and data centers toward new physical limits, advanced materials are becoming critical to performance, efficiency, and sustainability, says Mike Finelli, chief technology and innovation officer and chief North America officer at Syensqo.
In partnership withSyensqo
The AI boom is becoming a materials challenge. As AI pushes computing into new territory, the materials behind that infrastructure are becoming just as crucial as the algorithms running on it. Semiconductors and data centers are approaching physical limits around performance, thermal management, electrical efficiency, and reliability, creating new demands for materials that can do more at once. At the same time, AI is giving materials scientists new ways to search the enormous universe of possible molecules and accelerate the development of solutions.
For Mike Finelli, chief technology and innovation officer and chief North America officer at Syensqo, that convergence is transforming what advanced materials can enable. “AI is now, from a material standpoint, really pushing semiconductors and the data centers to their physical limits,” he says.
As requirements accumulate, including high temperature, purity, electrical performance, chemical resistance, plasma resistance, and long-term stability, materials move toward what Finelli calls the “top of the pyramid.” Beyond supporting AI innovation, he contends that advanced materials are “actually increasingly defining what's going to be possible.”
That challenge is playing out across the infrastructure powering the AI surge. Syensqo is developing materials for high-voltage data center architectures, advanced sealing materials for semiconductor manufacturing, and thermal-management solutions including fluids for direct immersion cooling. Some of those innovations can also cross industry boundaries. Materials developed for electric vehicles, for example, can help address the higher voltage and energy-density demands that are emerging in data centers.
The definition of performance is also changing. More customers are expecting materials to meet technical requirements while reducing environmental impact. “Our goal is to remove the trade-off between performance and sustainability,” Finelli says. That means considering sustainability at the beginning of the research process instead of treating it as an additional requirement once a material has been developed.
AI is changing how those materials are discovered, too. Syensqo is using AI agents to digitally synthesize millions of potential molecular combinations, predict their performance and sustainability characteristics, and narrow them to a much smaller group for laboratory testing. The result, Finelli says, is the ability to go “broader, deeper, and faster” while giving scientists more time to solve complex engineering problems.
Looking to the future, Finelli sees the possibility of a reinforcing cycle: AI helps develop materials that improve AI infrastructure, which in turn enables better AI to accelerate materials discovery. That feedback loop could create a cycle of innovation and expand what future technologies can achieve.
“You end up in this accelerated materials, innovative cycle of materials innovation,” says Finelli. “That really excites me, and it gives us the opportunity to continue enabling technologies that will shape the future.”
This episode of Business Lab is produced in partnership with Syensqo.
Full Transcript:
Megan Tatum: From MIT Technology Review, I'm Megan Tatum, and this is Business Lab, the show that helps business leaders make sense of new technologies coming out of the lab and into the marketplace.
This episode is produced in partnership with Syensqo.
Now asked to name the key enablers to AI advancement, many of us might list algorithms, data centers, or even computing power, but just as critical to the performance are the advanced materials that underpin each layer of that innovation. As AI continues to evolve, it's pushing the likes of semiconductors and data centers to new physical limits, putting new pressure on the advanced material sector to keep pace. But the relationship goes both ways. As the sector rises to this challenge, AI is also emerging as a powerful tool for accelerating materials discovery and development, significantly shortening development timelines for new solutions.
Two words for you: materials innovation.
My guest today is Mike Finelli, chief technology and innovation officer and chief North America officer at Syensqo.
Welcome, Mike.
Mike Finelli: Thank you, Megan. Nice to be here.
Megan: Thank you so much for joining us. Mike, can I start by asking you to tell us a little bit more about Syensqo and the role it plays in developing advanced materials?
Mike: Yeah, absolutely. Syensqo is a global leader in specialty materials. Our job is to help customers solve their toughest technology challenges. We serve a lot of different markets, but the way I like to say it simply is if it flies, we're on it. If it drives, we're in it. In healthcare, our products literally are saving lives every day. And if you like your mobile devices, if you like AI, it's our products that are actually enabling the advanced semiconductor chips that are required to produce all of this. Our role is to enable innovation through advanced chemistry. We develop materials that deliver higher performances, greater reliability, and increasingly more sustainable solutions. The way I would say this, it's at the heart of our business. Actually, it's in our name, Syensqo. And to put some numbers around it, 20% of our annual revenues come from new products and applications that we've launched in the last five years, which is really evidence of a really strong innovation engine.
Megan: Yeah, absolutely. And as you sort of described there, you're in all sorts of different industries with an emphasis perhaps on electronics and semiconductors. Can you talk a bit more about that work and where those industries are headed perhaps?
Mike: Sure. So look, electronics and semiconductors have been strategic markets for Syensqo for literally decades. I don't want to date myself, but 33 years ago when I started in the company, semiconductors were one of the first industries that I worked in. And we've supported successive waves of innovation from enabling smaller, more powerful mobile devices, helping the industry get to the smaller and smaller profiles and the chips. We've helped to advance hyperconnectivity, supporting increasingly sophisticated semiconductor manufacturing. And today we're helping to advance the AI era.
We have one of the industry's broadest portfolios of high performance polymers and advanced materials. We support applications across the entire electronics value chain from semiconductor fabrication, electronic components, to smart devices and telecommunications, even hyperconnectivity. And our materials are helping customers solve increasingly demanding challenges around miniaturization, thermal management, electrical performance, chemical resistance, higher and higher purities, and long-term reliability and sustainability. And today we work with leading semiconductor manufacturers and electronics companies all around the world.
Megan: Fantastic. And as you alluded to there in the last 30 years, we've seen huge evolutions in those sectors.
Mike: Oh my God, yes.
Megan: And now AI is putting these new demands on semiconductors and data centers. What does that mean for the materials they're built from and to what extent will AI innovation be constrained or enabled by materials science finding a solution?
Mike: Yeah, so I mean, you're absolutely right. But AI is now, from a material standpoint, really pushing semiconductors and the data centers to their physical limits, and materials are becoming a key enabler of that continued progress.
The way I try to describe it, think of a pyramid, I call it the performance pyramid. You have commodity materials at the bottom of the pyramid and you have high performing specialty materials at the top of the pyramid. At Syensqo, all we do is we operate at the top of the pyramid and we're continually trying to raise the top of that pyramid by bringing newer and newer and more higher performing materials out.
Now you might say, okay, but why doesn't a data center or a semiconductor manufacturing fab need a specialty versus something in the commodity space? Well, I call it the and, and, and principle. If you just need a polymer or a material that can sit at the table at room temperature and stay there for 10 years and not change, well, there's a lot of commodity materials that will do that and you don't have a problem. The minute you start adding requirements, and I call it the and, and, and so if you need a polymer that can handle high temperature and have to have high purity and electrical performance and chemical resistance and plasma resistance and it's got to have long-term stability, all of these ands, you start moving to the top of the pyramid.
Now what AI is doing with semiconductors, because of the speed at which it's advancing, it's requiring semiconductor chips and data centers, the number of requirements are increasing the number of ands which is pushing the limits of the materials. That's where we come in. And I really believe that advanced materials, they're no longer just supporting AI innovation, we're actually increasingly defining what's going to be possible.
Megan: Right. That's fascinating. And in terms of rising to that challenge of focusing on that top of the pyramid and that and, and, and principle you're talking about, could you talk us through perhaps an example or two of those top of the pyramid solutions you've created or that you're working on at the moment?
Mike: Like I said, our focus is enabling higher performance, but it's also without compromising on reliability or safety. We develop advanced polymers, elastomers, specialty fluids, fluids meaning lubricants and heat transfer fluids, and they're used throughout the semiconductor manufacturing process and also increasingly in AI data center infrastructure. One example of our work on specialty materials for next generation AI data centers is the work we're doing around high voltage architectures. Data centers are moving towards high voltage architectures because they can enable greater computing power while also improving energy efficiency. We know that's a big issue for that segment of the industry, and these high voltage architectures will help them reduce and improve energy efficiency because it reduces energy losses and they can ultimately help lower the environmental footprint of the data centers. And we're developing new materials that can help them get there.
Another example is our high performing sealing materials found inside semiconductor fabs and wafer tools. If you can picture, many people have seen what a semiconductor looks like during processing. It's a big, big silicon disc that's then later diced into the tiny little chips that go into the computer. But that wafer is put inside a giant chamber where it has a very extreme environment, aggressive plasmas, reactive chemicals, and they need higher and higher performing materials. And all of the seals that are around that chamber to keep those gases in the environment inside have to be able to withstand that environment. And that's what we're developing and we're pushing the limits. They're asking for higher temperatures, more aggressive environment with lower out gassing and purity. And that's what we're developing for this industry to allow that next chip to be developed and produced industrial.
Megan: It's so fascinating that people wouldn't give much though necessarily to the seal in something like that. As you're outlining, it's just absolutely critical in terms of performance. And in developing those solutions, I understand you also looked across different markets to see what may be applicable perhaps in more than one space, and that includes an overlap between the automotive sector and data centers, I understand. Can you tell us a little bit more about that?
Mike: As I mentioned just previously, the data centers are shifting to higher voltage architectures. This is the next generation data center, which can be more energy efficient, but it's got a higher energy density. The power density increases, which increases temperatures. And many of the material challenges that we will be facing there, we've already developed for the automotive industry in electric vehicles. I'll give you an example of an application. I mean, think about an electric vehicle. The powerhouse in electric vehicle is no longer the motor, it's the battery. That's where all the energy sits. And when you're putting a hundred kilowatts of energy, driving that to the electric motor through wires and through what they call bus bars, you got to get that car up to 60 miles an hour pretty quick. You're driving massive amounts of energy that's increasing temperatures dramatically.
And all the electrical connections are in these bus bars that there's a polymer that's an insulating polymer with copper in between for all the connections. That's got to withstand that temperature increase, which could come pretty rapidly. We've developed new materials there and those materials will be translatable over to these data centers where they're going to have the higher voltages with a higher energy density.
Another thing we've been doing in automotive, we have a lot of knowledge in both automotive and semiconductor around fluid circulation and how to use dielectric materials to do direct immersion cooling. That's something that will be very valuable for data centers and server farms. Using air to cool semiconductors is really inefficient and energy intensive. If you could submerse them in a liquid, you have direct immersion cooling, that's extremely efficient, so that's another thing we're working on.
Another thing we developed in automotive that will be translated over is battery energy storage systems. Inside the battery, we've developed a binder. It's the highest performing binder on the market, which is using the cathode of a lithium ion battery, and it keeps all the ingredients doing its job working together so that battery can actually last for 10 years and perform. Now that's moving over to the data centers because they're moving more towards renewables and they need to have these energy storage systems to smooth the peak loads and provide resilient backup power. That's one of the things that we're doing. By transferring our knowledge across the markets, we can accelerate new power and new thermal management solutions while supporting reliability required by next generation AI infrastructure.
Megan: Fantastic. So many transferable applications there that necessarily wouldn't have sprung to mind. And it isn't only technical advancements that you need to contend with, of course. Companies today are also demanding the materials are developed and manufactured more responsibly too. So how is sustainability shaping your innovation process?
Mike: Yeah, you're absolutely right. I will say performance is still the entry ticket. Our customers want performance. Now what's changing is that definition of performance is now broader and it is including sustainability targets and requirements. Our customers expect materials that deliver outstanding technical performance while also being developed and manufactured more responsibly.
At Syensqo, we believe that operating as a responsible company means we're providing true sustainable business solutions to our customers. And this is why we developed what we call the Sustainable Portfolio Management tool, SPM. It's a matrix, and it defines what a sustainable solution is. For us, it's a product that in a given application improves our product's social and environmental performance while also demonstrating a lower environmental impact in its production, creating values for our customers. In short, we want to develop products, and this is where it starts. Every one of our research projects before we even start them is assessed on whether it's going to be a sustainable product or not.
And 88% of our portfolio now is a sustainable product. We're developing materials that are better for the environment, lower environmental footprint when we produce it, but also they contribute to improvements for our customers as well so they could operate with a lower carbon footprint or they can operate in a safer way or less water consumption. There's a lot of different lists in there.
Another example is our longer-term development of next generation heat transfer fluids. Semiconductor manufacturing and data centers have become more powerful. I mentioned before the heat that they're generating, especially when they move to the higher voltage architectures. Managing that heat is increasingly important. And again, I talked about direct immersion cooling. We're developing those solutions because today there are fluids out there that will work, but they got high global warming. That's not good for the environment. We're developing the next generation heat transferred fluids that will reduce the potential environmental impact compared to the fluids today. In the end, our goal is to remove the trade-off between performance and sustainability. You notice that's another and, we can be performing and sustainable.
Megan: That's so important, isn't it though, to think about sustainability in terms of performance? As you say, when we're thinking about commercially scaling up these solutions, it's such an important part of it. And as I talked about in the introduction, AI isn't only a challenge, but it's also an opportunity within the advanced material space. I'd love to explore how you're using AI tools at Syensqo to inform and accelerate the development of solutions as well.
Mike: Absolutely. We embarked on this journey about two years ago, where we're using AI in our research and development, and we've partnered with Microsoft and their Microsoft discovery tool, and it's helping us to rapidly identify and evaluate promising molecular candidates.
Now, in the normal research approach, historically, you would design your experiment and you'd look at all the potential combinations of materials and chemicals that you could make all these different molecules. And the combinations of potential and molecules that you could develop to solve a problem could be in the millions, but it's impossible to develop a million molecules or tens of millions of molecules in your laboratory and actually physically do that. But you have to select a small area based on your expertise and knowledge, based on the literature searches, based on the state of the art that's out there and looking at patents, et cetera. And you pick a small area and you go through the process, you develop the materials, you test them, you learn something, you go back to the drawing board, you start again. Eventually you find something that works, but it doesn't mean you found the best possible combination that's out there.
But what we're doing with AI is we have developed AI agents with Microsoft that are literally digitally synthesizing the entire millions and millions of combinations of potential molecules. And we have another AI agents that are using physics-based simulation to look at all those molecules and predict the performance of them, and not just performance on physical chemical properties, but also on toxicity, on sustainability, et cetera. Then we have another agent that takes all that information and ranks them all. In the end, we have explored all of the potential molecules out there. We understand roughly what the performance should be, and we end up with a priority list of maybe a hundred, instead of millions and millions, a hundred that we actually synthesize in the lab.
And at the end, you end up getting the solution faster, much, much faster. You've explored the entire space. I basically say it allows us to go broader, deeper, and faster. And the important thing is it's not replacing our scientists, it's not replacing our scientific expertise. In a way, it's giving them superpowers. It's allowing them to spend less time searching and more time solving the industry's toughest engineering challenges.
Megan: Amazing. It sounds like it's genuinely a really transformative tool by what you're explaining.
Mike: Completely, completely.
Megan: I mean, just to finish, Mike, it'd be great to take a look ahead if we could, because there's so much activity in both AI and the advanced material space. I wonder what is coming down the pipeline that you are most excited about next?
Mike: I've talked a lot about AI and how we're using AI to develop new materials. I think to me, what's really exciting, and I'm starting to see it actually happen, I'm just curious how fast this is going to go, is that we're using AI to develop new materials that will enable AI to get better, and then that AI will use the new AI to develop new materials to get AI to go better. I see this loop of developing for AI, for AI to improve, and then we use that AI to improve ourselves. You end up in this accelerated materials, innovative cycle of materials innovation. That really excites me, and it gives us the opportunity to continue enabling technologies that will shape the future. That's what we do at Syensqo.
Megan: Fantastic. Yeah, real sort of virtuous circle of innovation, it sounds like that. Amazing. Thank you so much, Mike.
Mike: Thank you.
Megan: Thank you so much. That was Mike Finelli, chief technology and innovation officer and chief North America officer at Syensqo, whom I spoke with from Brighton in England.
That's it for this episode of Business Lab. I'm your host, Megan Tatum. I'm a contributing editor and host for Insights, the custom publishing division of MIT Technology Review. We were founded in 1899 at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and you can find us in print on the web and at events each year around the world. For more information about us and the show, please check out our website at technologyreview.com.
This show is available wherever you get your podcasts, and if you enjoyed it, we hope you'll take a moment to rate and review us. Business Lab is a production of MIT Technology Review, and this episode was produced by Giro Studios. Thanks so much for listening. Goodbye.

title: Meet a mouse whose brain cortex is made up of human cells
content:
Meet a mouse whose brain cortex is made up of human cells
“Xenocortical mice” are a dramatic demonstration of organoid technologies
Multiple cameras tracked a mouse as it wandered around a small arena. A computer charted its position and speed, leaving Pong-like traces on a monitor.
The reason to watch this rodent so carefully? Nearly half its brain volume had been replaced with human cells.
The effort to mix the brain tissues of distant species is being reported today in the journal Nature by a team at Stanford University, led by neuroscientist Sergiu Pașca.
Pașca’s group previously showed that human brain “organoids”—small blobs of neural tissue—could survive, and even function, after being injected into the heads of baby rodents.
Now, Pașca has taken things a step further by genetically modifying mice so their brains don’t fully develop in the first place. These modified mice are missing most cells of both the cortex and the hippocampus, two key brain areas.
That creates much more room for the human cells to take hold, he says. “Human cells that are placed in these animals will divide, will grow, and within a few weeks to a few months they will take most of that space,” he says. Pașca says one surprising discovery is that the mice lacking brain tissue seemed fairly normal—they walked around and squeaked. But they did have memory problems. In a maze test, they couldn’t remember what parts they’d explored.
The mice with the added human cells, by contrast, performed better on the maze test. That means the human tissue is playing some role in the animals’ cognition.
Pașca believes what he is calling “xenocortical mice” could be useful in studying brain injuries. However, the report is also a dramatic demonstration of “the combined power of genetic engineering and stem-cell technology to reshape biology,” says Carsten Charlesworth, a scientist who works in a different Stanford lab and was not involved in the research.
Already, brain organoids are being tested in labs to see if they can be connected to computers to play video games. Other scientists have proposed using them like replacement parts to treat stroke victims.
“What’s most remarkable to me is the extent to which human neural tissue introduced after birth grew and connected with the mouse nervous system across a species barrier,” says Charlesworth. “As these technologies advance, they’ll increasingly force us to challenge our traditional assumptions.”
Last year, Pașca convened a group of ethics experts to study the implications of neural organoid technology, including the odds that an animal could develop human consciousness and the risk that “organoid therapy clinics” might offer scam treatments to desperate patients.
For now, he says, he’s not concerned that the rodents have any type of human cognitive capacities. That is because their brains are relatively tiny and the evolutionary distance between man and mouse is so great.
But that’s also why Pașca says this type of experiment should not be carried out on higher species: They could end up with large volumes of functioning human brain tissue, potentially blurring the cognitive boundaries between people and animals.
Pașca specifically cautioned against adding human brain organoids to a monkey engineered to lack a cortex.
“One of the things that I see as a very clear red line is doing this experiment in a primate,” he says. “I don’t think that is justified at this point in any way.”

title: The Download: AI’s trillion-dollar gamble and OpenAI’s biology data bid
content:
The Download: AI’s trillion-dollar gamble and OpenAI’s biology data bid
Plus: Nvidia and Meta CEOs have rejected calls for a coordinated AI slowdown.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
What’s at stake in AI’s trillion-dollar gamble
When Jessica Wachter, a finance professor at the University of Pennsylvania, wanted to assess AI’s impact on the economy over the next few years, she faced a long list of uncertainties. So she started with a “remarkable fact” that is not in question: a handful of so-called hyperscalers are investing huge amounts of money to build AI data centers.
Instead of trying to predict how widely deployed AI models will be, Wachter asked how fast the hyperscalers’ earnings will need to grow to justify their spending through 2027, when expenditures are expected to reach nearly $1.1 trillion.
The results are eye-opening. AI companies will need to achieve an extraordinary increase in productivity just to break even by 2030.
Take a closer look at what it will take for the AI buildout to pay off.
—David Rotman
AI models need more data about biology, and OpenAI is paying to create it
AI needs much more information to make important breakthroughs in curing disease. So last year Ruxandra Teslo, a policy analyst, posted an idea for supercharging medical AI systems: use data from failed biotech companies. By bidding at bankruptcy proceedings, she argued, it might be possible to obtain detailed regulatory filings, manufacturing strategies and safety data, creating what she called “biotech’s lost archive.”
The OpenAI Foundation, the nonprofit parent of OpenAI, announced this week that it will fund her idea, paying to create “high-quality scientific datasets.”
Learn more about their new effort.
—Antonio Regalado
Our Roundables on AI’s extinction threat is now available on demand
As frontier models become more capable, warnings about AI extinction have become widespread in Silicon Valley. But are the threats really as dangerous as they’re presented?
In the latest MIT Technology Review Roundtable, executive editor Niall Firth, senior AI editor Will Douglas Heaven and AI reporter Grace Huckins took a closer look at the arguments behind those warnings. They discussed what AI extinction could actually mean, how seriously we should take the risks and what, if anything, can be done to reduce them.
Subscribers can now watch an exclusive recording of the discussion.
Want to join the next conversation? Subscribe to MIT Technology Review for exclusive access to all our future Roundtables, and recordings of previous ones.
MIT Technology Review Narrated: a startup claims it’s found a drug to make your blood young
Generation Lab says its new rejuvenation treatment “blocks the systemic spread of aging in the bloodstream, reawakens the body’s own repair mechanism, and restores health and youth to multiple tissues.”
The approach is based on research by the company’s scientific founder, Irina Conboy. She found that joining the circulatory systems of old and young mice improved the old animals’ ability to heal from injury.
Conboy now says she has found a combination of two existing drugs that can produce youthful effects without the need for any bodily fluid exchange. But there’s a snag: Generation Lab won’t reveal what the drugs are.
This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 Nvidia and Meta CEOs have rejected calls for a coordinated AI slowdown
Jensen Huang and Mark Zuckerberg pushed back on the proposals. (FT $)
+ Huang says new AI safety laws are unnecessary. (Axios)
+ Zuckerberg claimed competition will push AI labs toward safety. (Reuters $)
+ What’s next for AI after its doomer turn? (MIT Technology Review)
2 The FTC chair has warned against giving AI companies antitrust waivers
His comments follow Anthropic’s call for a safety exemption. (Reuters $)
+ Nvidia’s CEO also slammed the calls for new antitrust laws. (CNBC)
+ The US is divided over AI regulation. (MIT Technology Review)
3 A Chinese hacking firm has used AI to analyze stolen secret
Its tools turn hacked government data into intelligence reports. (WSJ $)
4 “Smart” nanoparticles delivered mRNA to tumors in a cancer study
The treatment reprogrammed cells to attack tumors in mice. (Wired $)
+ Federal health agencies are abandoning mRNA. (MIT Technology Review)
5 A digital fly brain is taking on an extraordinary range of tasks online
People have taught it to drive, trade bitcoin, and play Doom. (NYT $)
+ The simulated brain is a map of a fruit fly’s 166,000 neurons. (404 Media)
6 The Senate has blocked new crypto rules amid a fight over Trump
It demanded tougher ethics rules around Trump’s crypto holdings. (AP)
+ The move is a major blow to the crypto industry. (NYT $)
7 Chinese firms allegedly used Binance to launder Iranian oil money
Prosecutors say they laundered more than $1.5 billion. (Quartz)
+ Hackers are selling tools to bypass banks’ facial checks. (MIT Technology Review)
8 An AI agent platform is reinventing spam to flood inboxes worldwide
iLand says its agents have sent 1.6 million messages. (404 Media)
9 ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming has become Asia’s richest person
His fortune has risen above $105 billion as AI booms. (Bloomberg $)
10 A fully AI-generated sitcom has arrived—and it’s terrible
A reviewer called the characters “dead-eyed waxworks.” (Guardian)
Quote of the day
“The only institution that Americans might trust less than Washington these days is Silicon Valley.”
—Patrick Hillman, the chief operating officer of Logical Intelligence, a San Francisco–based startup chaired by Yann LeCun, says in a statement that people have little faith in tech companies to act in the public interest.
One more thing
Why Trump’s “golden dome” missile defense idea is another ripped straight from the movies
In 1940, a fresh-faced Ronald Reagan starred in Murder in the Air, a movie centered on a “superweapon” that could stop enemy aircraft. More than 40 years later, the concept became a real-life centerpiece of Reagan’s presidency with the Strategic Defense Initiative (SDI), better known as “Star Wars.” Now Donald Trump has revived the dream.
In 2024, Trump announced plans to build the “Golden Dome,” a system of sensors and interceptors on the ground, in the air and in space. It’s often compared to SDI for its futuristic sheen, its aggressive form of protection and the idea that an impenetrable shield is the cheat code to global peace.
The dream of a missile shield is animated by its sheer cinematic allure. But do cinematic spectacles actually enhance national security?
See what happens when the fantasy of missile defense meets reality.
—Becky Ferreira
We can still have nice things
A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)
+ A once blind cockatoo just saw for the first time in 10 years.
+ Bingebrowse is a virtual video store stocked with films and shows from streaming services.
+ An amateur engineer has used a tree trunk to build Donkey Kong’s coconut gun as a real weapon.
+ A wildlife photographer has captured the first-ever images of the elusive and rare Cozumel dwarf fox.

EV转型促使中国国有车企合作
广汽集团总部（广州）
中国国有车企在EV转型中落后，尤其是一汽，未能充分拓展新能源汽车产品线，1~8月新车销量下降16%。有观点指出，“一汽为了在EV领域生存下去，有意利用广汽所拥有的电动化相关资产”……
中国第一汽车集团通过子公司对广州汽车工业集团子公司出资并展开合作的情况浮出水面。受纯电动汽车（EV）转型影响，盈利能力笼罩阴影的中国国有大型车企正试图通过重组谋求生存。
广州汽车工业集团旗下的广州汽车集团股份有限公司9月14日发布的公告中表示，“一汽股份将成为本公司第二大及具有战略影响力的股东”。
公告显示，广汽集团股份有限公司筹划以发行股份的方式购买一汽股份持有的某整车合资公司的部分股权，并募集配套资金。交易完成后，一汽股份将成为广汽集团股份有限公司的股东。
中国国有车企在民营企业和新兴企业拉动的纯电动汽车转型中行动落后。尤其是一汽，仍以发动机汽车为主力，未能充分拓展纯电动汽车等新能源汽车的产品线。该公司1~8月的新车销量同比下降16%。
中国汽车工业协会的数据显示，在8月份中国新车销量（含出口）中，新能源汽车占比已达6成，汽油车销量则在迅速下降。
广汽在国有企业之中已成功应对EV转型趋势。其自主品牌“埃安（AION）”作为新兴的纯电动汽车品牌，2023年在中国国内新能源汽车销量中位居第三。 广汽不仅自主开发和生产车载电池，还于6月与华为合作，启动新能源汽车新品牌的销售。
广汽“埃安”的EV（6月，重庆市）

实现合作并非易事。一汽的股东是中国政府，广州汽车工业集团的大股东则是广州市政府。总部位于吉林省长春市的一汽股份与地处广州的广汽，企业文化也大不相同。两家公司被认为将在保持各自独立性的同时，加强合作关系。
广东省政府旗下的网络媒体南方Plus于9月15日提出看法称，“这不是简单的两个企业之间合作，而是开启了汽车领域‘央地整合’新模式，更折射出中国汽车产业走向协同共赢的重要格局演变”。
丰田汽车是否会参与两家公司的股份交易成为焦点。有部分当地媒体推测，广汽在信息披露中提到的“一汽股份持有的某整车合资公司”，指的是丰田与一汽合资的“一汽丰田”。
除了一汽丰田之外，丰田还与广汽合资成立了“广汽丰田”。南方Plus指出，“根据广汽集团与一汽股份现有的合作伙伴，不难看出这家‘整车合资公司’究竟是谁——一汽丰田”。
包括合作能否成功在内，还有很多不明朗的部分。广汽的披露信息中也明确指出，本次交易尚处于筹划阶段，存在不确定性。
