title: 白天务农晚上码农，这个斐济农民跨越一万公里来拼多多取经
content:
< img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400">
那些数以亿万计的，仍在等待被市场看见的小农户们。
程浅 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI
谁能想到，“码农”这个词流行了十几年，终于活成了
一位来自斐济小岛的农民Cody，白天种地，晚上借助AI自学编程。
码了2000多个小时后，他终于为自己和当地的小农户码出了一套智能经营系统。
9月，Cody带着这套系统，几乎跨越一万公里，来到了
在卡达武岛，收割农作物要听船期。
卡达武岛位于南太平洋，是斐济东部的一个火山岛，面积约410平方公里，相当于一个北京海淀区；岛上坡地起伏，海岸曲折，山脊贯穿岛内，最高峰与八达岭长城高处齐高。
△卡达武岛村落｜图源斐济旅游局
受地形影响，这里的村庄大多分布在沿海地区，“何时来船”与“何时下雨”“何时换季”一样重要。农民必须要赶在货船开走前收割。
作物何时成熟是土地的事情，而它的成熟有没有“意义”，就要听大海的安排了。
31岁的农民Cody就在这座岛上生活，他热爱着种地。
他的父亲种了四十年地，三次获得卡达武岛“年度农民”的称号，还曾荣获斐济东部大区的“畜牧农民奖”。
在这里，照料作物是最重要的事。
卡达武农户们种植芋头、木薯、甘薯和卡瓦，前几样流向了家庭餐桌，卡瓦则流向了世界各地，是当地极重要的经济来源。这是一种胡椒科植物，其根部经过干燥、捣碎、揉洗、过滤，将被制成某种神秘棕色饮料。
△卡瓦｜图源flickr
实际上，Cody也曾离开过这样高度自给自足的农耕生活。
他上大学攻读数学与物理学的理科学位，但因为热爱农田，他还是选择了辍学。
他回到家乡，当七个雨季越过卡达武岛的时候，他在热带气旋、干旱以及与收购商的周旋中学习务农。
七年来他越来越发现了一件事——
仅靠种地是无法维持好一座农场的。
比如，作为小农户的Cody常在寻求当地金融机构或政府项目支持时遭到拒绝。
拒绝的原因通常是：
“你如何证明你是农民？”
这样的问题并不算太荒谬，因为一个农民的农事或曾在笔记本上被记录过，但这并不足以证明什么。
Cody说，整个斐济约有8.3万名农户，84%都是小农户。其中大量的农户缺少稳定的采购关系、融资渠道和规范的生产记录——与此同时，这个国家每年进口11亿斐济元的食品，食品出口额却仅为2亿至3亿斐济元。
这中间存在断层：买家找不到可靠的供货者，农资供应商找不到需要自己的农户，政府和非政府组织大量投入后又不知道具体产生了什么效果。而农民，被夹杂在这些关系中间，
往往要自己寻找下一笔资金和买家。
Cody想到，自己或许可以开发一个产品，把农场每天的工作记下来，再让这些记录流动起来，被需要的人看见。
△Cody在比赛现场
不过，请人开发产品需要钱，而Cody手里的钱要留给下一个产季。并且，就算找到了开发者，就能沟通清楚需求吗？农民农作的很多需求都是隐性的啊。
船期会影响收割时间；一份喷药记录要在四个月后仍能找到才算有用；亲友前来帮工未必留下工资单，却同样构成一季的成本……
Cody丝毫没有计算机基础。最初困住他的甚至是“寻找学习资料”而非“配置开发环境”。因为他不知道
该输入什么检索关键词
，也不知道搜索结果与自己要做的产品有何关系。
他零散地学了几年，才逐渐能够做出东西。
AI后来加速了这个过程。遇到问题时，他可以直接询问接下来该学什么，“缩短了从未知到已知的距离”。
就这样，Cody白天去农场照料作物，夜里继续学习软件开发。仅仅做出一个能够使用的产品原型，他就花了
2000多个小时。
种地的人擅长观察。植物发黄、枯萎时总会显露蛛丝马迹，供农人判断哪里出了问题。
但刚开始接触编程时，Cody却完全不明白程序为什么失败，代码也根本不care他是不是凌晨四点还在焦头烂额。
干脆别管了回去种地吧！他常想要放弃，但种地时遇到的那些问题，又会再次把他推到电脑前。
就这样，Cody在痛苦挣扎中逐渐搭起来了一套叫“Teivaka”的系统。
在Teivaka里，农户可以记录种植、用工、农资投入和资金往来，也可以学习课程，发布农产品信息，寻找买家，与供应商或机构联系。
系统中的AI助手则会依据斐济本地的土壤、作物、季节和农事规则提供建议，也能够读取农户自己的生产记录。
比如，当卡达武岛进入一段干旱期，AI助手会建议农户分批种植，避免把整个产季押在同一个月里；水源有限时，优先照顾受旱后难以恢复的幼龄卡瓦；必要时推迟播种，避免白白损失种苗。
诸如此类的种植、投入、用工、收获和交易留下的记录，将逐渐汇成一份按时间排列的农业档案。
Cody给它起了一个名字叫“农业护照”
，农户可以决定是否向银行等机构开放查看权限，由机构自行核查、作出判断。
目前，Teivaka以两座自营农场为试验场，正在组织首批100名用户参与，其中一半是农户，其余包括买家、供应商和机构人员。
接下来的一个产季，要回答几个实际问题：农民是否愿意持续记录，记录是否可靠，机构是否接受。
就这样，带着Teivaka和这些尚未验证的问题，
Cody来到杭州参加2026全球农创客大赛。
△Cody接受央视采访｜截图自《东方时空》节目
大赛由联合国粮食及农业组织、浙江大学和拼多多联合主办，迄今已有六届，而Cody的项目入围了大赛首次设置的“小岛屿发展中国家组”决赛。
他很想向拼多多请教——这家根植农产品业务的电商平台，成功地将分散的小农户与更大的市场连接了起来。
Cody想知道，最初，在没有农户从中挣到钱时，怎样让第一批人愿意尝试？消费者需要看到什么，才肯购买一个素未谋面的农民种出的东西？
Cody的故事只是本次农创客大赛的一个切片。
2026全球农创客大赛共收到来自49个国家的191份独立申请，其中137个项目符合参赛条件。最终，13支团队进入决赛，包括8支全球组团队和5支小岛屿发展中国家组团队。
这些项目最初面临的困境各不相同，但它们大多源自一个矛盾：当地并不缺少可利用资源，但资源却没有转化为人们可以获得的食物、收入或发展机会。
印尼的印德拉马尤是一个很典型的案例。
作为西爪哇北部最大的鱼类产区之一，渔村整日被高品质的鱼类包围，然而这里的许多儿童却长期
营养不良，发育迟缓
尽管渔船每次都会带回大量渔获，但由于渔民需要尽快获得现金，常把其中高品质的鱼卖掉。
留在本地的低值鱼，多被简单制成鱼干或咸鱼，由于这些鱼多刺、腥味重、处理麻烦，很多渔民更愿意食用方便食品。
渔业女性赋能项目负责人Resy称之为
印德拉马尤的另一种悖论发生在当地的
身上，这些女人大多一辈子生活在渔区，却很难成为渔业价值链中的生产者和受益者。
出海捕鱼大多是男人的工作，妻子只能在家里干等着丈夫回来，祈求渔获的同时更祈求买家们的到来。
Berikan Protein，这家由女性担任CEO的机构同时捕捉到了这两种困境，随之启动渔业女性赋能项目。
她们从价值链中被浪费掉的环节切入，使用酶水解技术，把低值鱼中的蛋白质制成鱼蛋白原料，再用于食品开发。
通过将鱼蛋白加入不同的食物中，在勿里洞岛，她们做出了鱼蛋白面条，而在印德拉马尤，则做出了鱼皮零食。
△印德拉马尤沿海社区的女性加工渔获｜图源Ocean/Berikan Protein供图
△项目参与者正在销售鱼蛋白零食｜图源Ocean/Berikan Protein供图
三年间，她们处理了72万公斤低值鱼，帮助6479人获益，产生的收入超过100万美元。
之后，项目面向30名渔民妻子开展技术培训，不仅帮助她们学习制作鱼蛋白面条和鱼皮零食，也开展包装设计、食品备案、基础经营和销售等系列培训。
不过后者的培训并不理想，团队随后改变了分工，让女人们继续负责自己熟悉的生产和线下销售，让社区中的年轻人帮助她们进行数字营销，开拓线上渠道。
△该项目获得了决赛银奖
目前，她们的产品已经走出了印德拉马尤的小社区，走到了雅加达、万隆和巴厘岛。
尽管技术进入农村、渔村的形式各不相同，但最终都要经过相似的检验：劳动者们是否愿意采用它，以及技术周围是否存在一套能够让它持续运行的关系。
这种检验，中国的农林渔牧行业并不陌生。
中国拥有庞大的农产品消费市场，生产端却长期由小农户构成，占到了全国农业经营主体的98%以上。
小农户总会面临无数问题，其中“如何种植”或许是最简单的那个。
包装、运输、销售、预知市场需求、为城市提供稳定且标准一致的持续供应……
过去，收购商、批发市场和合作社承担着这样的连接；农业电商出现后，又增加了一种组织方式。
在拼多多，这种尝试被称为“农地云拼”。土地仍然分散在各家农户手中，消费端的零散需求却可以先汇集起来，形成相对集中的订单，再由商家、合作社和产区组织供应。
对Cody和Resy这样的农创客而言，这些经验正是他们所需的。
因此全球农创客大赛并不只有现场路演一天，入围团队除了准备路演，还要参加共创工作坊，接受国际组织、研究机构和产业界的辅导，并与投资机构及农业企业交流。
三家主办方带来的经验各有各的分量。
联合国粮食及农业组织提供粮食安全、乡村发展和公共政策视角；
浙江大学提供需求评估、创新诊断和创业方法的训练；
拼多多则分享农产品市场、产消连接和平台规模化过程中的产业经验，依托“千亿扶持”计划为农业创新技术和模式提供支持。
对拼多多这样的企业而言，其参与不只在于提供资金或赛场。
平台在长期经营中积累的经验，原本只存在于业务流程和从业者的判断中；只有把它们整理出来，说明它们因地制宜的成立条件和曾走过的弯路，才能成为全球农创客者们所吸收的公共知识。
Cody最终没能从杭州把农创客大赛的奖杯带回斐济——他的项目还在落地阶段。
但他或许将带回更珍贵、更灿烂的东西。
比如，分散在不同岛屿和村庄的小农户，怎样被组织起来，获得稳定的订单？
市场需求怎样在播种前传回田间，而不是收获后才发现农产品无处可卖？
没有抵押物，也拿不出完整经营记录，农户怎样能获得贷款、保险和机构支持？
一座奖杯只能属于一支团队。
但这些问题的解法，属于斐济的8.3万名农户，也属于世界各地仍在等待被市场看见的小农户们。

title: 达卯科技算电协同2.0平台入选2026国际数字能源展重大成果发布

成果中唯一聚焦算电协同全链路运营的AI技术产品
9月15日-17日，2026能源绿色发展大会・国际数字能源展在深圳举办。展会首次以“一会一展”深度融合模式打造全球数字能源产业盛会，集中发布近百项前沿创新成果。达卯科技自主研发的「算电协同2.0平台・AIDC绿电直连能源运营操作系统」成功入选重大成果发布，也是成果中唯一聚焦算电协同全链路运营的AI技术产品。
本届展会规格高、链条全，超五万平米展览和会议空间围绕跨界、协同、融合主线，全景呈现能源产业数字化智能化前景。50余个国家和地区近400家企业参展参会，专业观众超7万人次。
人工智能产业爆发式增长，算力与能源的协同发展成为本次展会聚焦的核心产业议题。在政策体系持续迭代完善下，绿电直连模式为算力基础设施的建设发展打开全新格局。新型算力中心通过与新能源场站直连对接，既保障能源供给，缓解电网整体容量压力，又能推动高增长算力负荷的清洁低碳转型，实现系统能源利用最大化。然而，绿电直连当前却也普遍面临着“落地推进难、经济性平衡难”等现实挑战。
在重大成果发布现场，达卯科技CEO简煜忞表示：“问题的本质在于行业普遍仍局限于单一电能量市场的零和博弈思维。事实上，我国电力市场由多重市场共同构成，除电能量市场外，还涵盖调节性市场、容量市场，以及处于发展中的碳市场。算电协同的核心价值绝非简单的物理链路打通，真正决定绿电直连乃至风光火储一体化项目盈利水平的关键，在于如何用好人工智能技术，在多重市场中进行综合寻优，构建最优运行逻辑，才能真正将能源从算力产业的刚性成本项，转化为可运营、可增值的新型价值资产。”
他提出，达卯算电协同2.0平台的价值，就是通过AI技术，以可预测、可调节、可优化、可增值的运营能力协同转化为可执行、可核算的客户经营价值，将算力中心从“用电负荷”升级为“新型电力系统下可调度、可交易的柔性资源”。
算电协同2.0平台，采用行业首创的“融合推演智能+统筹博弈智能”双引擎技术架构，以能源大模型为底座、原子化多智能体为执行载体，实现负荷、发电、电价等多源时空、多市场数据预测和趋势感知，以及电能量、调节、容量、碳多重市场全局统筹、多目标最佳策略求解。平台在算力中心日内负荷预测实验室准确率超过98%，电价预测准确率较行业主流提升10%以上。针对绿电直连场景，平台以全量能源托管模式实现多重市场全局优化与多方收益智能归因，典型项目可实现10%～20%的综合电力成本优化，能源侧投资IRR提升30%以上。
此外，平台具备高度场景适配能力，可结合不同区域市场规则、地方政策和差异化的能源运营场景实现本地化快速配置。包括：针对不同运营方角色，分层提供运营驾驶舱、调度监控、交易持仓管理、算法统一治理等功能模块；部署模式支持从用户侧到电网侧、新能源侧分阶段落地，可灵活适配东部城市型智算中心调节市场运营、中西部节点型绿电直连大基地一体化协同等多元区域场景模式。
本次，达卯科技算电协同平台入选2026国际数字能源展重大成果发布，是行业的权威认可，标志着国内AIDC绿电直连规模化落地的运营范式正逐步成熟，算力产业绿色转型与数字能源生态深度融合已驶入快车道。

title: Space Data Centers Inch Toward Reality, With Caveats
content:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. – Orbital data centers are edging closer to reality, but significant technical and economic obstacles remain, according to industry and government leaders who discussed the future of computing in space at the AI Infra Summit, held Sept. 15-17.
Thermal, Bandwidth, and Launch Hurdles
Sumeet Singh, chief data and AI officer at Viasat, a satellite communications company, identified three
primary challenges
. The first is thermal management – the ability to keep orbital systems cool. In the vacuum of space, heat can only be shed through radiators, which must be large enough to dissipate substantial thermal loads. “With size comes weight. Weight is a huge currency when you think about orbital data centers,” he said during a panel discussion on Thursday, Sept. 17.
Singh also pointed to limited downlink and uplink capacity – the ability to move data to and from orbit – and the cost of launching the data centers into low Earth orbit (LEO). He said today’s costs of $2,500 to $3,000 per kilogram would need to drop to roughly $200 to $500 per kilogram for orbital data centers to make financial sense.
Related:
The Breaking Points 2035: A Data Center Space Odyssey
Joe Yaffe, COO and chief legal officer of Cowboy Space Corp., which is building orbital data centers and aims to launch them, agreed that those obstacles are real. He added that reliance on a
single dominant satellite launch provider
has become a bottleneck in its own right.
Yaffe said Cowboy Space is tackling the bottleneck by developing its own launch vehicle and using the rocket’s second stage as the data center itself. To address bandwidth, the company plans to use optical links. “We’re believers that data transmission needs to take place optically, uplink and downlink, in order to move what will be increasingly larger amounts of data,” Yaffe said.
Power is another constraint. Camille Bergin, chief marketing officer of Star Catcher, an in-space energy utility, said the company is working on laser-based power beaming to augment existing solar arrays, potentially delivering up to 10 times more power to orbiting systems.
Customer Readiness and the Road to Scale
Related:
Data Center Space Race: Can Orbital’s Satellites Overcome Doubts?
Singh, whose company, Viasat, wants to participate in the emerging orbital data center ecosystem, said the industry must prove itself incrementally – both technically and commercially. He cited StarCloud’s November 2025
of a satellite featuring an Nvidia H100 GPU as a promising sign, while noting a single-GPU demo is a far cry from megawatt- and gigawatt-class facilities. “We suddenly talk about megawatt- and gigawatt-class data centers. I think we need intermediate proof points … something in between where you have 100- to 500-kW-class compute,” he said.
Other key milestones, Singh added, include ensuring sufficient launch capacity to get these systems into orbit and demonstrating that customers will actually buy compute in space.
Bergin agreed on the need to “crawl, walk, run,” describing how her company first proved its technology on Earth before moving to space-based demonstrations. “There are a lot of people in this industry who have a tendency to just say, ‘This is the thing that we’re going to build, and it’ll just happen,’” she said. “I think from the orbital compute perspective, what are those incremental steps? How do we get from operating at 5% to 10% on a single H100 as a prototype to a megawatt-class, gigawatt-class data center? … We can’t just design something in space because we think it’s cool and it’s the next frontier. There has to be a real need and a real business model.”
Related:
Meta’s Space Solar Bet Highlights AI Data Center Power Gap
Bergin also argued that orbital data centers could address
community pushback against terrestrial facilities
. “All of us are super-familiar with the fact that people don’t like these data centers. They don’t want them in their communities. They are super-problematic. … So space [is] offering a solution if we can get there.”
Despite the challenges, Singh remains confident. “This isn’t a question of if it would happen. I think this is more of a question of the step function. When would this happen?” he said.

title: Climate XChange is giving away more EVs than ever before in its 11th Annual EV Raffle
content:
Climate XChange
Image: Climate Xchange
What would you choose with up to $120,000 to spend on a fully customized EV – a Lucid Air, Rivian R1S, Porsche Macan Electric, BMW i7, or perhaps two EVs instead of one?
Climate XChange’s 11th Annual EV Raffle
is now open, and the grand prize winner can choose any fully electric make and model on the market. Climate XChange will cover the taxes, too.
This year, there are three prizes across two separate raffles. Tickets start at $100, and anyone who buys before October 30 will also be entered for a chance to win a $10,000 Early Bird bonus.
How the Luxury Raffle works
A Luxury Raffle ticket costs $250, and only 5,000 will be sold.
Grand Prize: Choose up to two fully electric vehicles from any manufacturer, with a combined value of up to $120,000. You can put the entire amount toward one dream EV or divide it between two.
Second Prize (new this year!): Choose a fully electric vehicle from any manufacturer worth up to $35,000.
Taxes: Climate XChange pays the taxes on the vehicle prizes.
Ticket price: $250.
Ticket limit: Only 5,000 Luxury Raffle tickets will be sold.
That top prize leaves plenty of room to get creative. You could configure one high-end EV exactly the way you want it or put two new EVs in the driveway – as long as their combined price stays within the $120,000 limit.
How the Mini Raffle works
The Mini Raffle offers another route to a new EV, with tickets priced at $100.
Prize: Choose a fully electric vehicle from any manufacturer worth up to $50,000.
Customization: You select the make, model, trim, color, and options within the prize limit.
Taxes: Climate XChange pays the taxes on the vehicle prize.
Ticket price: $100.
Ticket limit: Only 4,000 Mini Raffle tickets will be sold.
A $50,000 budget puts EVs such as the Rivian R2 (we’ve reserved one!), Tesla Model 3, Chevrolet Equinox EV, Hyundai Ioniq 5, and plenty of other models within reach, depending on the configuration you choose.
The Luxury and Mini Raffles are separate, so you can enter either one or buy tickets for both.
Buy an early Luxury Raffle ticket for another chance to win
Climate XChange’s 11th Annual EV Raffle
launched on September 9, and every Luxury Raffle ticket purchased by 11:59 pm ET on October 29 will also be entered into the $10,000 Early Bird Drawing.
Buying early doesn’t remove your ticket from the main raffle. It simply gives you an additional chance to win.
EV prize drawing
takes place on
December 11, 2026
How to enter
, select the Luxury Raffle, Mini Raffle, or both, and purchase your tickets online.
The Early Bird deadline is October 29 at 11:59 pm ET, and the number of tickets is capped at 5,000 for the Luxury Raffle and 4,000 for the Mini Raffle. Full eligibility requirements and official raffle rules are available on the
raffle website
What your ticket supports
Climate XChange
is a nonprofit that helps states protect communities from pollution and rising energy costs. It’s a small, passionate team that works to move practical climate policies forward at the state level, where decisions can directly affect household energy bills, public health, transportation, and access to clean energy.
Proceeds from the annual raffle support that work, so every ticket also helps Climate XChange push for cleaner, more affordable energy.

After nearly a year of operation on a dedicated track line at the Jimblebar iron ore mine in Australia, BHP is proving that these 4,400 hp battery-electric powered heavy-haul locomotives are ready for prime time.
UPDATE 19SEP2026
: there’s a video!
We first covered the two battery-powered Wabtec locomotives working at the Jimbelar iron ore mine in Australia’s Pilbara back in August, discussing the engines’ massive 7 MWh battery packs and rail-trembling stacks of tractive power. And, just yesterday, the company released a new video explainer for its big BEVs.
I’ve included the new video, below, but above the original article. Check those out, then let us know what you think of Wabtec’s new BHP FLXDrive (apparently pronounced “Flexdrive”) locomotives in the comments.
Wabtec BHP FLXDrive electric locomotive
Australia’s first brand-new, purpose-built battery-electric locomotives (
) arrived in Port Hedland last November – and the two
Wabtec FLXDrive
BELs were immediately put to the test on BHP’s rail routes between its
Jimblebar
iron ore mines and Port Hedland operations in the Pilbara.
“The Pilbara has always been a place of big ambition, and these locomotives represent the kind of innovation that is needed to keep the region firing,” said Peter Thomas,
Wabtec’s Regional Senior Vice President for ANZ & SEA
. “Wabtec is proud to partner with BHP on this important step toward decarbonising rail operations. These locomotives are purpose-built to perform in one of the world’s most demanding environments, combining advanced battery technology and regenerative braking to deliver high efficiency and lower emissions.”
The train, itself
Wabtec locomotive, via BHP.
While most modern trains use electric drive motors, those are typically powered by diesel engines acting as electrical generators to haul up to 35,000 tonnes of ore. The Wabtec BELs are similarly powered by high-torque electric motors, but in these, the motors draw power exclusively from the locomotive’s batteries – and they are positively MASSIVE batteries!
Each of the Wabtec FLXDrive BELs is weighed down by a 7 MWh battery pack backed by advanced regenerative braking technology that can capture energy during downhill braking and feed it back into the battery.
On some long downhill runs and loaded up with ore, BELs with regenerative brakes could generate enough power to send the unladen train back uphill to get loaded up again, effectively meaning it’ll only need to be charged once,
and then never again
That kind of potential fuel savings is something every mining company will be looking at
– including BHP, who announced plans to add two additional BELs to its Pilbara operations for extended trials just this week:
In FY2026, we commenced commissioning of two purpose-built Wabtec FLXdrive heavy-haul battery-electric locomotives in Port Hedland, marking the beginning of the trial program. Two further locomotives from Progress Rail were delivered to Perth in FY2026 and to be transported to Port Hedland for commissioning and testing in FY2027.
Once locomotives from both original equipment manufacturers are in trial, we expect to be one of the first mining companies globally to conduct side-by-side evaluations of battery-electric heavy haul locomotive technologies from two suppliers within the same operating environment. This creates a unique opportunity to compare [different products] and accelerate learning in large-scale rail applications.
Using gravity to charge up heavily-laden mining vehicles on downhill runs is an idea that’s been put into practice for years
, with great success wherever the topography allows (
since 2017
, at least). Combining that clever use of gravity, traction braking, and battery storage for use on a rail system like this just seems smart, and it makes me think we’re just scratching the surface of all the clever ways electrification and battery storage will eventually get put to use.
I wonder what would happen if you threw some battery electric rail cars into the mix
, as well!? You guys are smart, head down to the comments and let me know.

title: Swaptopus inches towards reality as CATL reveals new semi truck battery
content:
Electric Semi Truck
battery swap
Jo Borrás
| Sep 19 2026 - 6:08 am PT
In a move that challenges
Orange Juicer
Buick Electra
for the highly coveted
Best Name in the EV Business
title, a new venture between CATL and Octopus Energy called “Swaptopus” has been formed to build out a European battery swap network for commercial trucks.
First announced at Octopus Energy’s Energy Tech Summit back in June
, the Swaptopus concept got a bit of a boost at last week’s IAA Transportation event in the form of TECTRANS II, a next-generation commercial vehicle battery solution built specifically to serve as a modular, universal electric truck platform that promises to eliminate long charge times and battery life concerns that have remained key barriers to commercial fleet electrification.
According to the original CATL press release for TECTRANS II,
the new battery system improves fleet economics in three ways
Higher energy density
– boasting a gravimetric energy density of 170 Wh/kg, around 13% above the industry average, the battery enables vehicles to  carry approximately 0.6 tonnes of additional payload at the same battery capacity. ­
Longer Range, Faster Charging
– its maximum configuration offers up to 1,000 km of range and 80% charging in 25 minutes with megawatt-level fast  charging, minimizing downtime on long-haul routes.
Higher energy efficiency
– the world’s first full-tab low-impedance design enables 96% system round-trip efficiency (RTE), reducing charging losses and delivering more usable energy for daily operations.
“Commercial vehicle electrification will unfold over more than a decade,” said Zhu Lingbo, CTO of CATL Global Business Unit. “With our deep technological expertise and long-term commitment, CATL is ready to be the most reliable partner for customers worldwide and for the global electrification of freight transport.”
Once in full swing,
CATL and Octopus claim their proposed network could support 300,000
+ electric trucks and unlock more than £30 billion in private investment while creating jobs and reducing Europe’s dependence on imported oil by replacing fossil fuels with sustainably produced electricity.
It takes a village
FleetBooster charging and energy-storage system; by FleetBoost.
Along with Octopus, CATL announced that it’s signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with global shipping giants
DHL Group
that aims to accelerate the electrification and decarbonization of road freight transportation across Europe by engaging a broad coalition of industry stakeholders that includes Xiaomi-backed mobile power plant specialists Quibo Energy and FleetBoost, who provide mobile charging and battery energy storage systems (
), including the “FleetBooster” trailer (shown, above) which integrates CATL battery technology.
This level of collaboration points to an industry united in a single goal:
avoiding high fuel prices
decarbonization.
Akin Li, Executive President of CATL Overseas Business, emphasized that sort of “holistic” approach to fleet decarbonization, saying, “by combining real logistics demand with vehicles, charging, energy storage, battery swapping and lifecycle services, CATL plans to work with DHL and other ecosystem partners to create practical and scalable solutions for zero-emission freight.”
For DHL Group, the partnership is a critical next-step toward its corporate goal of achieving net-zero logistics-related emissions by 2050, following other steps we’ve covered in these pages

title: 'Can't Be Done By One Company': This Startup Is Rallying A Team To Bring Solid-State Batteries To Life
content:
'Can't Be Done By One Company': This Startup Is Rallying A Team To Bring Solid-State Batteries To Life
Instead of going solo, Factorial is bringing battery companies together to make solid-state batteries a reality.
Massachusetts-based battery startup Factorial Energy said Thursday it's building a coalition of specialized battery makers to bring the long-elusive all-solid-state battery to market. The company signed a joint development agreement with Japanese firm Mitsui Kinzoku to use its solid electrolytes in Factorial's batteries, the latest in a string of partnerships the company has struck in recent months.
Unlike traditional lithium-ion batteries, which use a highly flammable liquid chemical to shuttle charge-carrying ions to power EVs, all-solid-state batteries swap that liquid out for a solid electrolyte. Battery scientists believe the technology can eliminate fire risk, substantially improve energy density, and deliver blistering charging speeds. But the technology has been bogged down by technical challenges for years, while conventional lithium-ion batteries keep improving on range, charging speed, and cost.
Factorial CEO Siyu Huang told InsideEVs in an interview that the company is tackling those challenges by bringing together specialized battery makers rather than trying to solve everything in-house. Huang said no single company can crack all-solid-state batteries alone, and that assembling firms that specialize in anodes, cathodes, electrolytes, and advanced manufacturing is necessary to get the technology into production.
“We’re driving a very strong coalition among all of the supply chain,” Huang told me. “There are still significant technical challenges to unlock. It’s very important for us to go beyond the existing mindset and framework for lithium ion and focus on a technology that goes beyond."
Factorial Energy CEO Siyu Huang holding the all-solid-state battery cell.
The company, which went public on the Nasdaq in June, is working with Korean anode and cathode specialist Posco Future M. It is exploring how to scale the technology with SK On and has also signed joint development agreements with Volkswagen Group’s PowerCo battery division and the Hyundai Motor Group. A memorandum of understanding with Korea’s Phil Energy covers advanced manufacturing tools.
“We’re very well settled for both North American and European volumes,” Huang said, referring to its agreements with SK On and PowerCo.
Battery startups routinely lean on larger companies to help develop and scale their technology. So what Factorial is doing here is nothing unusual. But its a rare acknowledgement that no single company can get all-solid-state batteries over the finish line on its own.
The Mitsui collaboration is critical to making its Solstice all-solid-state battery, Huang told me. “Having access to this material is very important to enhance the performance of this battery,” Huang said. “That’s why we’re able to get really strong performance and high temperature thermal stability, something we couldn’t get without them." Factorial said the company is among the very few companies that holds “foundational IP” for all-solid electrolytes.
Factorial's two main products are the FEST semi-solid-state battery, which uses a gel-like electrolyte, and the Solstice all-solid-state cell. Both are NMC batteries at their core, using anode-free lithium-metal cells paired with solid or semi-solid electrolytes. The semi-solid-state battery is rated for up to 375 watt-hours per kilogram of energy density and is already installed in prototype Mercedes-Benz EQS and Dodge Charger Daytona EVs. The all-solid-state version goes further, targeting up to 450 Wh/kg, roughly double today's lithium-ion cells.
Both products haven't made their way into production vehicles yet, but Huang said the semi-solid-state technology is ready for commercialization, with customer orders already locked in. Karma Automotive is set to be the first to roll out a production EV with its semi-solid battery in 2028. Factorial also landed its first commercial aerospace purchase order for a drone battery this summer. Huang said she expects "large automotive OEMs" to come on board down the line, with timing depending on their requirements for the batteries.
Several other battery startups are racing for the next big EV battery breakthrough. A large number of mostly American startups are among those spearheading that effort, including California-based QuantumScape, Colorado-based Solid Power, and Illinois-based Pure Lithium. Toyota, Taiwan’s ProLogium, as well as several established Chinese battery makers like CATL and BYD are also racing to crack solid-state batteries. Whether a coalition model like Factorial's or a more vertically integrated approach wins out remains an open question.
“Battery innovation can't be done by a single company," Huang said, "[It] is driven by the entire supply chain and, increasingly, by an entire industry coalition."

title: Hyundai CEO's Answer For The EV Slowdown: Building Thousands Of Robotaxis
content:
Hyundai's CEO said it plans to build "tens of thousands" of Ioniq 5 robotaxis for Waymo.
Photo by:
6:30am ET
The market for electric cars in America isn't growing as quickly as Hyundai, or indeed most car companies, anticipated just a few years ago. Thank softer-than-expected consumer demand and the destruction of pro-EV policies for that. But the South Korean automaker's CEO thinks he has found another potentially huge and growing customer base for all of those EVs it can build: robotaxi companies.
As the EV tax credit and fuel-economy regulations fell away over the last year and change, automakers from
scaled back their EV ambitious and took enormous write downs. While rivals "decided to write down their assets, we decided to make the most out of our assets," Hyundai Motor Company CEO José Muñoz told reporters in San Jose on Thursday.
That meant adjusting capacity at the Hyundai Motor Group plant in Savannah, Georgia, to make more hybrids and fewer EVs, he said. "The other thing we've done is to look for new business opportunities within the EV, and the number one biggest opportunity is robotaxis," he said. Hyundai inked a deal to build vehicles for Waymo in 2024, and it also manufactures Ioniq 5s for its own autonomous-vehicle arm, Motional.
An Ioniq 5 EV being assembled at Hyundai's Metaplant in Georgia.
Photo by: Patrick George
Muñoz told reporters on Thursday that the company's robotaxi-manufacturing business is profitable. And, on stage at an recruitment event in San Jose, he said Hyundai will make "tens of thousands" of Ioniq 5 robotaxis for Waymo at its Georgia plant. "So it's becoming a business unit on itself," he added.
Hyundai plans to deliver the first Ioniq 5 robotaxis not destined solely for testing to Waymo in the fourth quarter. The vehicles will use Waymo's sixth-generation autonomous-driving hardware, just like the firm's
Zeekr vans
. The difference is that the Ioniq 5s come equipped with all the bells and whistles from the factory, whereas Waymo outfits Zeekrs with sensors itself at a factory in Arizona.
When the two companies announced their partnership in 2024, they noted that Hyundai would provide a "significant volume" of vehicles but did not specify how many. Today, Waymo's fleet includes some 4,000 vehicles across 14 U.S. cities.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Robotaxis are becoming an increasingly important source of EV volume, especially during a sluggish period for sales. That can be especially crucial to automotive startups still trying to turn a profit.
Rivian recently struck a deal with Uber
to provide up to 50,000 R2 crossovers. Lucid will sell at least 35,000 Gravity SUVs and midsize vehicles through its
tie-up with Uber and Nuro
. This week, Lucid
announced a partnership with European shared mobility platform Bolt
to supply at least 25,000 midsize vehicles for autonomous operation. Stellantis, too, will provide EVs to Uber for a robotaxi program.
Muñoz said he sees "a significant opportunity to scale up" its robotaxi business, and he suggested that the company may not stop with Waymo. There's "a lot of interest" from other customers, he said.

title: ‘The Trend Is Clear’: How EVs Are Closing In On Gas Car Prices
content:
‘The Trend Is Clear’: How EVs Are Closing In On Gas Car Prices
The average new EV costs only 9.4% more than a gas car, with incentives playing a shrinking role in that shift.
One of the biggest barriers keeping car shoppers away from electric cars is steadily shrinking. The average price of a new EV is now getting closer to the average cost of a combustion car, something that could potentially boost EV sales in the U.S. if the trend holds up in the coming months and years.
According to Kelley Blue Book, the average new electric car cost only 9.4% more than the average new car in August. That’s a sharp drop from the 16% gap observed at the same time last year.
While the average transaction price of a new vehicle in the U.S. increased nearly 2% in August to $50,089, electric cars went in the opposite direction, Kelley Blue Book said. The average transaction price (ATP) for a new fully electric car was $54,813 last month, down 2.7% year-over-year. Unsurprisingly, Tesla remained the dominant EV maker in the U.S. and continued to have an outsize influence on EV prices. But it wasn't the only manufacturer pulling prices down.
Stephanie Valdez-Streaty, the director of industry insights at Kelley Blue Book parent Cox Automotive, told InsideEVs via email that the market is moving towards more affordable options from non-Tesla brands.
“Outside of Tesla, the ATP story is largely being driven by Toyota, Chevrolet, Hyundai, and Subaru,” Valdez-Streaty told me.
She added that the some of the country's most popular models, including the Tesla Model Y, Hyundai Ioniq 5, and Cadillac Lyriq, saw barely any price movement in August. The Model Y was down 0.2% year-over-year, the Ioniq 5 fell 0.4%, and the Lyriq dipped 0.1%. Newer and cheaper models like the Toyota bZ, C-HR, Chevy Bolt, and Subaru Trailseeker, on the other hand, have gained market share and are posting strong sales volumes, which is helping pull the average EV price down.
“A greater share of EV sales is coming from affordable models,” she said.
While the average EV transaction price was $54,813 in August, plenty of models cost well below that. The refreshed Chevy Bolt starts at $28,995 with destination. The Toyota bZ starts at $36,575. Hyundai cut Ioniq 5 prices by nearly $10,000 last year, dropping its starting price to $36,900, where it has stayed since. That entry price gets you the small-battery trim with 245 miles of EPA range.
However, there’s a major wrinkle in the KBB data. What the firm calls average transaction price doesn’t factor in incentives. Incentives accounted for 12% of the average transaction price of an EV last month, the firm said, which is nearly double the overall industry average of 6.5%. In other words, there's a lot more cash on the hood on a new EV compared to a new combustion car.
Still, EV incentives accounted for 14.6% of ATP during the same period last year, meaning there are now lower incentives on EVs than before. Valdez-Streaty added that the average EV incentives dropped 20%, from $8,200 a year ago to $6,600 in August. EV incentive support relative to combustion vehicles also dropped. Lower incentives signal a healthier balance between demand and supply.
“The trend is clear: EVs are getting closer to price parity,” Valdez-Streaty said. “The parity story isn't just about EV prices coming down, it's also about EVs becoming less dependent on incentives."
The EV industry is now heading into a major sales season without the federal tax credit for the first time in years. Last year, a rush to claim the credit before it expired drove record EV sales in the third quarter. Many automakers made up for the lost incentive with their own aggressive discounts in the fourth quarter to soften the slowdown.
This time around, Valdez-Streaty said the defining story of the holiday season will be "normalization." That means EV sales will depend on choice, pricing, and inventory availability rather than a looming deadline or incentives, she added.
“We're seeing a market that is increasingly being driven by underlying supply-and-demand fundamentals rather than policy-driven urgency,” she said.

title: “工作垃圾”飞来飞去，曾大力拥抱 AI 的科技大佬开始“踩刹车”了
content:
9 月 19 日消息，当地时间 17 日，据《财富》杂志网站报道，曾经把 AI 吹捧为释放员工全部潜力关键的科技行业领导者，正开始逐渐改变说法。
Shopify 联合创始人兼 CEO 托比亚斯 · 吕特克就是其中之一。去年，他还要求员工把使用 AI 当作基本要求，在申请更多资源之前，先证明现有工作无法通过 AI 完成。
时间来到现在，吕特克开始批评员工
把未经检查的 AI 邮件和代码直接交出去，却不愿为粗糙的结果负责
。“我们把这种东西叫作‘垃圾手榴弹’，人们把它们互相扔来扔去。这绝对是一件坏事。”
吕特克指出，让 AI 彻底放开手脚很容易，但滥用 AI 只会把麻烦转嫁给接收和审核工作的人。比如，AI 本该帮助整理邮件要点，而不是把几句话扩写成浪费别人时间的长篇大论。“你自己根本没认真读，现在却要让同事来审核，他们看完会说，‘这个不太对劲’。
你只是把工作直接丢给 AI 去做
多邻国 CEO 路易斯 · 冯 · 安也开始
收回此前对 AI 的激进表态
。去年，他宣布多邻国转向“AI 优先”，员工考核将参考 AI 使用情况，部分人工承包商会被 AI 取代，只有团队无法把所需工作自动化时才增加人手。
今年 5 月接受《Fast Company》采访时，他坦言自己
曾被 AI 在写作演示中的出色表现冲昏头脑
，但真正扩大使用规模后才发现，
AI 最终仍比不上员工的创造力
。“我们可能需要写 1000 个不同的故事来帮助人们学习语言，到最后你会发现，其中 20% 完全就是垃圾。每当我们用 AI 大规模处理很多工作时，都必须非常小心，不能让这些垃圾混进来。”
图源：Pexels
研究人员把吕特克所说的现象称为“工作垃圾”（workslop），指
表面精致、看似像模像样，实际却缺乏实用内容，还需要别人返工的 AI 产出
BetterUp 实验室和斯坦福大学社交媒体实验室今年调查了 962 名美国全职办公室员工，52.7% 的受访者称曾把 AI 工作垃圾发给同事，而且
所在机构越鼓励使用 AI，这种情况越常见
。另有 38% 的受访者称收到过这类内容，平均每月要花 3.4 小时进行修改。
AI 工作垃圾与人类完成的普通低质量工作不同，前者表面上很像合格成果，
内部却缺少真正有用的内容
。受访者列举的例子包括
格式和结构都很完整、链接却无法打开的邮
本来可以很简单，却被 AI 写得异常复杂的代码
这种问题还会伤害同事关系。调查显示，一旦员工怀疑收到的是 AI 工作垃圾，就会认为发送者能力更差，也更不友善。在收到过这类内容的人中，36% 还称今后希望
避免再与这些同事合作
返工成本也在增加。去年调查中，40% 的受访者称遇到过 AI 工作垃圾，平均需要花 2 小时修改；今年这一数字
升至 3.4 小时
。按 2025 年的估算，单名员工每月修改这类内容造成的成本达到 186 美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,249 元人民币）
，而对于一家拥有 1 万名员工的机构，每年因此损失的生产力成本最高可达 900 万美元
（现汇率约合 6,042.7 万元人民币）

title: 中国空间站稳定运行五年，我国航天健康保障体系总体达到国际先进水平
content:
IT之家 9 月 19 日消息，今天（19 日）晚间的央视《新闻联播》报道，中国空间站稳定运行五年来，我国航天健康保障体系总体达到国际先进水平，空间站长期驻留保障能力持续提升。
今天召开的我国首届航天医学工程大会介绍，我国已构建了“失重防护 — 营养保障 — 医监医保 — 心理保障 — 环境安全”五位一体的航天健康保障体系，总体达到国际先进水平。
在生命保障系统方面，我国正致力于构建更先进、可持续的生命保障体系，逐步实现从“物化再生生保”向“受控生态生保”的技术跨越。用于载人登月任务的“望宇”登月服以轻量化、小型化、高安全可靠为目标，突破数十项关键技术，为月面复杂环境下的出舱活动提供坚实保障。
在空间脑科学领域，已有一批国际首创的弱刺激脑机交互、群脑协同测试与调控设备入驻空间站，通过多批次航天员的在轨实验和试验操作，突破多个国际首次，陆续验证了新技术，获得了新发现。目前，航天医学中对特殊环境适应机制的研究，正在探索向民用医疗领域延伸。
据介绍，“地星三号”卧床实验已于今年 8 月底结束，该实验通过模拟失重环境，研究人体生理变化，同步验证空间站一年期飞行失重生理效应防护与载人月球探测低变重力防护技术，为后续执行更长期飞行任务的航天员健康保障奠定基础。
据IT之家此前报道，此次大会还披露了多项有关航天服的新成就与新进展。目前，我国舱外航天服整体技术居于国际先进水平，“望宇”登月服研制进展顺利，已攻克数十项关键技术。
央视新闻今年 6 月披露的数据显示，中国空间站已在轨部署和实施 267 项科学与应用项目，仅去年一年，就新增 86 项在轨实验，上行科学物资约 1179 公斤，下行实验样品约 105 公斤，获取科学数据超过 150TB。

title: 奕境汽车：奕境 X9 顶压实测 20 吨，车身结构没有任何变形
content:
IT之家 9 月 19 日消息，奕境汽车今日发布视频，提到了在 8 月份举行的预售发布会上，宣传的挑战 16 吨集装箱垂直压顶的测试，ABCD 柱结构完整、无变形，车门可正常开启，当时 16 吨已经是行业最高的数据。
在本月举行的奕境安全技术讲解会上，奕境汽车品牌总经理曾清林则展示了奕境 X9 顶压 20 吨的测试视频。
把重量加到了 20 吨，车身结构没有任何变形。
现场的研发人员又提了一个设想，我们就把集装箱底部的平衡平台拆掉，用吊绳来拽住集装箱两边来保持平衡，然后用车顶顶部的这个弧形，小面积地接触集装箱，直接承压，最后得到的结果就是 20 吨挑战成功。
20 吨是吊车的上限，但不是奕境 X9 的上限。
大部分的车企做压顶测试的时候，都会在车顶做一个随行的一个平衡平台。团队一致决定发布 16 吨的测试视频，因为这个视频是不带平衡平台，用户更容易理解，也更接近真实的工况。而且当时，16 吨已经是行业最高的数据。
所以在这个卷数据的时代，我们有最好的结果，但是我们却宣传，更保守更接近真实工况的数据，这也是我们东风工程师的一贯的风格，营销还是比较老实。但是我敢这么说，同样的测试条件，同样的工况，敢这么做的没有几家。
据IT之家此前报道，奕境 X9 旗舰大六座 SUV 已于 8 月 18 日正式开启预售，号称满配华为乾崑全栈智能，拥有华为乾崑智驾、鸿蒙座舱、乾崑赤兔平台、乾崑车载光、乾崑车云、鲸鳍通信等，预售价 29.98 万-37.98 万元。
- 增程 四驱 Ultra+ 旗舰 长续航版：37.98 万元
- 增程 四驱 Ultra+ 长续航版：33.98 万元
- 增程 Max 长续航版：29.98 万元
奕境 X9 长 5301mm、宽 2015mm、高 1820mm，轴距为 3120mm；搭载鸿蒙座舱 HarmonySpace 6，配备双 17.2 英寸 3.4K 蝶羽双联屏；搭载 896 线双光路图像级激光雷达，最高采用华为乾崑四激光方案。
新车基于 800V 高压平台打造，CLTC 工况纯电续航 465km，在华为 XMC 全域融合架构的加持下，新车综合续航超过 1500km。

title: 市场监管总局肖凌云谈“8 月有一天召回近 800 万辆车”：都是新技术带来的安全缺陷
content:
IT之家 9 月 19 日消息，据每日经济新闻报道，9 月 19 日，国家市场监督管理总局缺陷产品召回技术中心工业品所所长肖凌云在 2026 中国汽车产业发展（泰达）国际论坛上透露，我国 2025 年召回的车辆中，有一半是企业主动召回。
真正能够召回的企业是好的企业、优秀的企业。真正主动去召回的企业，也是质量能够走向优先的企业。
数据显示，截至 2025 年底，我国共实施汽车召回 3265 次，涉及车辆 1.21 亿辆，其中受调查影响召回 662 次，涉及车辆 6408.21 万辆，占召回车辆总数的 53.14%。
肖凌云表示，今年 8 月 21 日，中国市场召回了接近 800 万辆车，都是一些新技术带来的一些安全缺陷。“召回监管制度对推动我国汽车质量安全水平的提升，发挥了很好的作用。”肖凌云称。
据IT之家此前报道，8 月 21 日，因车内应急机械拉手不易识别和操作，特斯拉、零跑、吉利等 9 大厂商宣布召回车辆。
此外，肖凌云指出，我国自动驾驶车辆训练和测试虽然是充分的，但现在很多测试都是基于标准在进行，事实上车辆都是在和非标打交道。“每一个驾驶员每天把车开出去，都是非标的。”肖凌云表示，为此，市场监管总局进一步健全了事故报告的制度，加强安全监测和报告，加强“沙盒”监管制度。
据他透露，目前，大概有 200 多万辆车是通过“沙盒”监管的改进，避免了大规模应用之后出现事故。
肖凌云强调，创新驱动发展，但安全才真正定义汽车。只有更安全的汽车，销量才会更好。大浪淘沙，剩下的一定是质量安全双优的品牌和车型。

title: 批评 3A 游戏“无聊”却误伤《战神：劳菲》，前顽皮狗游戏总监发长文致歉
content:
IT之家 9 月 19 日消息，据外媒 VGC 今天（19 日）晚间报道，曾执导《最后生还者》《神秘海域 2》和《神秘海域 4》的前顽皮狗游戏总监布鲁斯 · 斯特拉利，因近期批评 3A 游戏现状的言论，向索尼圣莫尼卡工作室《战神：劳菲》团队致歉。
斯特拉利曾在顽皮狗工作 18 年，其间担任《最后生还者》及《最后生还者：遗落》DLC 游戏总监、《神秘海域》联合艺术总监，并先后执导《神秘海域 2》和《神秘海域 4》。
斯特拉利最近接受《Edge》杂志采访时谈到 3A 游戏现状，坦言自己很难再对这些游戏提供的体验产生兴趣。“我觉得 3A 游戏提供的玩法和体验…… 说实话，挺无聊的。”
随后，斯特拉利以圣莫尼卡工作室即将推出的《战神：劳菲》为例补充道：“看看这款游戏，每一个像素都令人惊叹。每一帧背后投入的工作和技术…… 我自己也做过这种游戏，依然会觉得震撼。但真正看看玩家在游戏里做些什么，我就兴奋不起来了。这绝不是针对《战神》团队。只是整个 3A 领域似乎都缺少加入新鲜、创新想法的空间。”
这番言论在网上传播后，斯特拉利在 X 发文向圣莫尼卡工作室道歉，称自己的话被断章取义，并强调自己批评的是整个 3A 游戏领域，而不是《战神：劳菲》。IT之家附这篇长文大意如下。
我要向《战神：劳菲》团队道歉，是我无端把你们卷进了这些完全没必要的负面关注。我原本只是想说明一个行业问题，却错误地提到了你们的游戏，结果这段话被断章取义，拿去做吸引点击的内容。你们不该承受这些。对不起。
一名记者问我怎么看游戏行业现状，我谈到了几个担忧，其中之一就是 3A 游戏缺少创新，也越来越不愿承担风险。但这不是开发团队的错！我担心的是，玩家对过去 20 年来反复进行的同一套玩法越来越厌倦。
游戏这种媒介的特殊之处，就在于玩家需要亲自参与和行动，因此产生的生理反应与单纯观看电影完全不同。创作者必须不断突破，创造新的体验，否则就可能削弱玩家的多巴胺反应。
《半条命 2》于 2004 年推出，《战争机器》是 2006 年，《生化奇兵》是 2007 年，《神秘海域 2》是 2009 年，《最后生还者》是 2013 年。我认为这些游戏以及其他作品共同塑造了‘现代 3A 游戏’的基本范式，而且每一款都像是在尝试于 3A 框架内创造新的体验。但创新不足只是我担忧的一部分。
遗憾的是，本应为行业提供稳定支持的平台方，反而削弱了创新能力。不断追逐服务型游戏，企图复制下一个《守望先锋》《堡垒之夜》或《Roblox》，并不是可行的策略。
坦率说，这也说明这些‘行业领导者’根本不了解自己的品牌。说个可能有争议的看法：那些身居高位、掌握资金决策权的人缺少优秀的领导力、明确的方向和坚定的信念。（资金 = 稳定性。）如果他们真正理解自己的品牌，就应该能够与创作者进行坦诚而富有启发性的交流，引导游戏媒介继续创新。
总之…… 我对行业究竟出了什么问题、可能遭受哪些严重伤害，以及应该怎样解决，都有自己的想法。但我原本想认真讨论这些问题，却说错了话，提到了《战神：劳菲》，这是我的错。

9 月 19 日消息，2024 年的故障滞留事件两年后，据《华尔街日报》当地时间 18 日报道，NASA 正与波音洽谈，希望让星际客机继续承担新的载人飞行任务。
知情人士透露，双方讨论的方案包括
未来数年安排星际客机执行至少 10 次新任务
波音发言人告诉路透社：“我们将
继续支持 NASA 的商业载人航天计划
，并期待按照该机构的任务要求执行下一次星际客机任务。”
NASA 没有回应路透社的置评请求。
尽管星际客机两年前的载人测试任务麻烦不断，这次谈判仍说明，NASA 希望继续保留波音，使其与 SpaceX 共同承担美国载人航天运输任务。
2014 年，NASA 选中波音和 SpaceX 开发载人飞船，把宇航员送往空间站。航天飞机退役后，美国一度长期依赖俄罗斯联盟号飞船，两家公司承担的新项目旨在恢复稳定的美国本土载人发射能力。
NASA 发言人告诉《华尔街日报》：“我们正制定计划，以实现美国在近地轨道保持长期存在的国家目标。”具体方案预计很快公布。
当天早些时候，NASA 还向 SpaceX 授予一份价值 9.46 亿美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 63.52 亿元人民币）
的合同，追加 3 次国际空间站载人任务，使 SpaceX 承担的载人飞行任务延续至 2030 年。
2024 年，波音星际客机在载人测试飞行中接连出现问题，NASA 最终决定
，宇航员布奇 · 威尔莫尔和苏尼 · 威廉姆斯则改乘 SpaceX 龙飞船返回地球，
原定 10 天的任务因此演变为超过 9 个月的国际空间站驻留

title: 消息称大众加大保时捷裁员力度，拟再裁逾 4000 人填补约 7 亿欧元成本缺口
content:
感谢IT之家网友 华南吴彦祖 的线索投递！
IT之家 9 月 19 日消息，当地时间 19 日，德国《商报》发布消息称，大众汽车集团准备进一步扩大保时捷裁员规模，计划再削减超过 4000 个岗位。此前，保时捷业务困境拖累集团业绩，并引发盈利预警。
《商报》获得的文件显示，大众集团监事会近期通过了一项重组协议，准备启动集团迄今规模最大的改革，其中拟在保时捷再裁减约 4100 人，以填补约 7 亿欧元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 53.9 亿元人民币）的成本缺口。据悉，这批裁员将在现有协议之外另行实施。
今年 7 月，保时捷管理层与劳工代表同意额外裁员 5000 人，再加上此前确定的 4000 人，目前双方商定的裁员总数约为 9000 人。到 2035 年，这一裁员规模相当于保时捷员工总数的约五分之一。
作为母公司，大众集团只能向保时捷提出裁员建议，无权强制执行。
当地时间 18 日，大众集团下调全年利润率预期，从原先的 4.0%-5.5% 降至最高 1%。
利润率目标下调很大程度上与保时捷资产减记有关。中国市场销量暴跌，加上调整纯电战略付出高昂代价，保时捷 CEO 骆明楷正承受制定复苏方案的压力。

title: 消息称新能源车险定价区间对标燃油车，保费将走向“一车一价”
content:
9 月 19 日消息，据中新经纬从业内了解到，
新能源商业车险自主定价系数区间预计调整为 0.5-1.5，与燃油车保持一致
IT之家此前曾报道，2025 年 1 月，国家金融监督管理总局等四部门发布《
关于深化改革加强监管促进新能源车险高质量发展的指导意见
》，明确提出对新能源商业车险自主定价系数浮动范围进行合理优化。
2025 年 9 月，新能源车险自主定价系数由 0.65-1.35 调整为 0.6-1.4；2026 年 3 月再次调整至 0.55-1.45。
据悉，燃油车现行商业车险自主定价系数区间为 0.5-1.5。这意味着险企在基准保费基础上，
自主定价系数最低可至 0.5、最高可至 1.5
，但最终保费还要叠加 NCD 等系数，并非最终保费相对基准保费只有 5 折到 1.5 倍这一个浮动空间。
其中，NCD 系数是指无赔款优待系数，是保险行业根据车主过往理赔记录统一计算的一个保费浮动系数，主要看车主过去几年有没有出险、出险几次。
自主定价系数是保险公司在基准保费和 NCD 系数之外，根据投保人年龄、驾驶习惯、车辆风险等因素综合评估后给出的一个浮动倍数。它直接决定保费在基准价基础上的上浮或下浮幅度。车险保费的计算关系可以简化为：保费 = 基准保费 × NCD 系数 × 自主定价系数。
对外经济贸易大学保险学院教授王国军对该媒体表示，定价系数调整至 0.5-1.5 后，
将真正走向“一车一价”
，并非所有车主都能享受降价。
从测算情况看，低出险、维修便宜的车型，保费有望下降 10%-20%；高零整比、出险较多的车型保费将上浮，部分车辆涨幅甚至超过 20%

将持续到 2027 年初
PlayFront 获得的一份内部备忘录显示，面对暂时性的市场供应限制和旺盛需求，索尼将继续对 PS5 Pro 采取
更谨慎的供货策略
高需求与有限产能

报道指出，《GTA 6》定于 11 月 19 日发售，很可能成为进一步推高 PS5 Pro 需求的最大因素。近期的实机演示公布后，市场需求明显升温，德国零售商的机器库存几乎随即开始见底，转售市场的报价甚至比官方零售价
《GTA 6》首发阶段仅登陆主机平台，亦有望进一步刺激需求。由于 PC 版不随主机版同步推出，希望第一时间玩到《GTA 6》的 PC 玩家必须准备一台兼容主机，索尼此前更是重点把 PS5 Pro 宣传为“标杆平台”。
海外零售商已透露，未来几周预计会有新一批 PS5 Pro 到货，然而零星补货并不等于大面积恢复供应。索尼究竟能在这段时间向零售渠道提供多少主机，也没有明确答案。
因此，消费者仍要面对
相当不稳定的供货局面
。几轮补货很难让市场真正恢复稳定，打算等到《GTA 6》发售时再临时入手 PS5 Pro 的玩家也可能会扑空。早在今年夏季，零售商就已警告第四季度恐将出现缺货现象。
硬件供应收紧恰好撞上全年最重要游戏之一发售，也暴露出供应链的脆弱性。IT之家获悉，索尼明确称当前状态下“

title: 滨口直树：《最终幻想 7：启示录》游戏容量或达 200GB，需“一定程度”突破硬件限制
content:
感谢IT之家网友
9 月 19 日消息，《最终幻想 7：启示录》游戏总监滨口直树在 2026 东京电玩展接受外媒 VGC 采访时透露，本作容量可能达到约 200GB。
在被问到游戏下载容量是否会超过前两作使用的两张蓝光光盘时，滨口直树回应称：“简单来说，是的。目前还有一些细节没有最终确定，但游戏容量
大概会达到 200GB
。我知道大家对此有很多不同看法，不过归根结底，我们确实需要
在一定程度上突破硬件限制
。还有一点我想说，虽然完整游戏内容
不会全部装在光盘里
，但考虑到光盘可能逐渐退出市场，也可能继续存在，因此对于《最终幻想 7：启示录》，
我们无论如何都希望提供某种实体产品
。这对我们来说真的非常重要。相信我！”
作为对比，《最终幻想 7：重生》2025 年 1 月登陆 PC 时
占用 155GB 存储空间
。《最终幻想 7：重制版》和《最终幻想 7：重生》的实体版均采用两张光盘，《最终幻想 7：启示录》则只会使用一张光盘，因此所有平台的实体版都
需要额外下载游戏数据

据IT之家了解，《最终幻想 7：启示录》定于 2027 年 4 月 8 日登陆 PC、PS5、Xbox Series X|S 以及任天堂 Switch 2 平台。

title: 美联邦航空管理局斥资 8.75 亿美元打造 AI 空管系统，治理空中交通问题
content:
感谢IT之家网友
9 月 19 日消息，据《华尔街日报》当地时间 17 日报道，美国联邦航空官员将在全美最繁忙的航空走廊之一启用一套 AI 空中交通管理工具，最快当地时间 21 日上线。
据美国政府和航空业官员透露，这套名为 Smart 的软件将率先在华盛顿特区一带投入使用，随后逐步推广至全美。Smart 旨在帮助美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）和航空公司
减少航班延误与取消
，并在天气或其他突发状况扰乱空中交通时，
为航班重新寻找合适航路
Smart 全称为“空域、航路和轨迹战略管理（IT之家注：取 Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories 的首字母）”。系统可以
综合分析航空公司时刻表、天气、机场跑道容量和运行限制等信息
，预测空中交通流量，并提前发现潜在冲突。
待 Smart 全面覆盖美国空域后，系统将扮演类似全美空中交通管制体系“大脑”的角色。长期以来，空管设施人员不足也是造成航班运行中断的常见原因。今年早些时候，Air Space Intelligence 拿下一份
价值 8.75 亿美元
（现汇率约合 58.75 亿元人民币）
、为期 12 年的美国政府合同，负责开发 Smart 及一套配套系统。
在 Smart 准备扩大应用范围之际，FAA 也在与航空公司讨论如何协调航班时刻。航空业人士仍对系统的具体运行方式存在疑问，尤其是各家航空公司为了抢占一天中特定时段的航班资源，彼此竞争十分激烈。
经过数月筹备后，Smart 首轮上线规模仍小于部分航空业人士此前的预期。政府官员称，Smart 原本就计划先以有限规模投入使用，待软件得到验证后再逐步增加功能。拟议功能包括
拉开航班抵达时间间隔，以及提前数天规划航路
。现阶段，Smart 主要会在出现运行问题时充当决策辅助工具。
据政府和航空业官员透露，美国联邦官员还计划于 21 日在美国交通部总部设立 Smart 中央办公室。美国航空协会称，Smart 有望提升航空安全、增加空域容量并改善运行效率，让旅客和货运客户受益，并大赞这是“FAA 数十年来采取的最令人振奋、最大胆的举措之一”。

title: 联想 CEO 杨元庆个人捐建，中国科大“周光召楼”正式开工
content:
9 月 19 日消息，据联想集团，9 月 19 日，由杨元庆个人捐资建设并命名的中国科学技术大学少年班学院“周光召楼”正式培土奠基。
联想集团董事长兼 CEO、中国科大校董、计算机科学系 89 届校友杨元庆重返母校，与中国科大党委书记舒歌群、校长常进等共同挥锹，为“周光召楼”培下第一锹土。

title: 20 MW molten salt nuclear battery moves toward first-fission test
content: MicroNuclear is moving its 20 MW thermal Molten Salt Nuclear Battery toward detailed engineering, safety reviews, prototype manufacturing, and first-fission testing under a new collaboration with the Idaho National Laboratory Foundation.The agreement brings together MicroNuclear, the INL Foundation, engineering firm EXP, nuclear manufacturer Premier Technology and Porter House. The group will work on engineering, manufacturing, nuclear quality assurance, operations, training, licensing and commercialization activities.The MsNB is designed as a compact molten salt microreactor using natural circulation instead of relying on pumps to move its coolant. MicroNuclear says the system is intended to provide resilient power and process heat for critical infrastructure, military and government facilities, remote grids and industrial users.The company envisions the unit as a 20 MW thermal system capable of operating at full power for an anticipated 10-year battery interval before being returned to a centralized facility for fuel and salt recovery and recycling.Compact reactors target resilienceThe collaboration is intended to take the concept through a more structured development phase, including detailed design work, safety documentation, applicable government reviews and regulatory pathways.MicroNuclear describes the MsNB as cyber-protected, with physical and electromagnetic pulse protection also incorporated into its broader microreactor approach. The company is targeting applications where reliable power or high-temperature process heat may be difficult to provide through conventional energy infrastructure.The system could also support potential hydrogen production, according to the company. However, the announcement does not provide details on the hydrogen-production process, operating temperatures, or expected efficiency.“We are well positioned to move the Molten Salt Nuclear Battery from a promising technology to a disciplined path toward engineering, testing, licensing, and eventual development,” CEO of MicroNuclear Paul Marotta said.The development team will also work toward establishing a repeatable model for future deployments. That could help translate the reactor concept from prototype development into potential commercial projects if testing, licensing, and other regulatory requirements are met.Testing moves toward laboratoriesThe INL Foundation will support early fundraising and help facilitate access to Idaho National Laboratory. It also plans to present information about the MsNB through investor events. Contributions supporting testing may qualify for tax-deductible treatment, subject to applicable requirements.EXP will contribute engineering capabilities, while Premier Technology brings advanced manufacturing and nuclear quality-assurance experience. Porter House will contribute expertise related to deployment and commercialization.The companies say the combined effort is intended to accelerate technology maturation and establish the documentation and manufacturing capabilities needed for future demonstration.Testing is expected to take place at Idaho National Laboratory or other U.S. Department of Energy national laboratories. Those activities would be conducted through separate agreements rather than being automatically authorized by the collaboration announced this week.The agreement therefore marks a development step rather than confirmation that the MsNB has entered operational deployment. Before commercial use, the concept will need to progress through engineering, prototype testing, safety evaluation, licensing and other regulatory processes.

title: 50-year-old accelerator at Los Alamos lab slated for $1B upgrade
content: For more than five decades, the Los Alamos Neutron Science Center (LANSCE) in New Mexico has supported research that depends on specialized accelerator technology. It has allowed scientists to conduct materials research and highly advanced experiments involving neutron scattering and dynamic proton radiography.However, much of the infrastructure powering these experiments dates back to the facility’s initial startup. As a result, some systems are approaching the end of their operational lives, creating a challenge for scientists who rely on the facility’s capabilities.The LANSCE Accelerator Modernization Project (LAMP) has now received approval to begin designing a major upgrade, aiming to preserve these capabilities and keep the facility operational until 2050.The National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) granted LAMP Critical Decision-1 (CD-1) approval on June 1, with authorization from the US Deputy Secretary of Energy.“CD-1 gives us a clear path forward, ensuring LANSCE will continue delivering the world-class accelerator capabilities our national security mission requires,” Charlie Nakhleh, deputy Laboratory director for Weapons at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL), said.This milestone will allow the project to enter its design phase, where engineers will develop plans to replace and modernize multiple systems in LANSCE’s front end.Replacing obsolete systems and componentsLANSCE’s aging infrastructure has become increasingly difficult to maintain. In recent years, its systems have shown signs of wear, including end-of-life failure indications and increased downtime affecting the availability and quality of particle beams.The facility is also the last US accelerator using certain high-voltage generator technology. Critical components, including the drift tube linac, have required extensive repairs. A significant failure in 2019 even led to emergency intervention.LAMP will address these problems by replacing the accelerator’s front end with modern ion sources and other components. The project is designed to improve reliability, reduce maintenance requirements, enhance worker safety, and extend the facility’s operational life.“Moving into the design phase is a crucial step toward addressing aging infrastructure challenges so that the facility can consistently exercise the experimental capabilities that address national security needs and important scientific challenges,” Pat Fitch, deputy Laboratory director for Science, Technology and Engineering at LANL, said.A mix of capabilities found nowhere else in the nationThe challenge extends beyond maintaining an aging accelerator. LANSCE brings together an integrated suite of experimental capabilities that the laboratory describes as unique within the US.These include dynamic proton radiography, materials science, neutron scattering, and nuclear physics, all operating at a facility authorized to use hazardous materials and handle classified data.This combination supports weapons component qualification for stockpile sustainment, advanced manufacturing initiatives involving modern and aging components, nuclear data generation for simulation and modeling, and radiochemistry research related to nuclear weapon science and threat assessment.LAMP is intended to maintain these experimental capabilities while improving the infrastructure that supports them. The modernization project has an estimated cost of $687 million to $1 billion and will serve both NNSA and non-NNSA customers.“The LANSCE modernization helps ensure we can continue delivering on mission-relevant science for decades to come,” Fitch said.

title: 7 legendary missiles that reshaped aerospace engineering during Cold War
content: The Cold War was a contest not only of military power but also of engineering ability. Each side needed missiles that could travel farther, react faster, and operate more accurately under unforgiving conditions. Meeting those demands produced advances in propulsion, navigation, computing, materials, and structural design. Some missiles even became launch vehicles for satellites and astronauts, carrying their military engineering into the emerging Space Age. 1. R-7 Semyorka The Soviet R-7 became the world’s first intercontinental ballistic missile to complete a successful flight in 1957. Designed under Sergei Korolev, it used a central core surrounded by four strap-on boosters to generate the thrust needed for intercontinental travel. All its major engines ignited before liftoff, reducing the uncertainty involved in starting engines during flight. A modified R-7 launched Sputnik 1 in October 1957, and descendants of the same basic design later carried Vostok, Voskhod, and Soyuz spacecraft. 2. SM-65 Atlas America’s SM-65 Atlas pursued extreme weight reduction through pressure-stabilized propellant tanks made from thin stainless steel. Internal pressure gave the missile its structural rigidity, meaning the vehicle could buckle if insufficiently pressurized. Atlas also employed an unusual “stage-and-a-half” propulsion arrangement in which all three primary engines ignited before launch. Its two outer booster engines were discarded during flight, while the central sustainer continued operating and later helped the converted Atlas launch John Glenn into orbit. 3. Polaris A-1 Wikimedia Commons The Polaris A-1 turned the nuclear-powered submarine into a mobile ballistic-missile launch platform. In July 1960, USS George Washington successfully fired Polaris missiles while submerged off the coast of Florida. Engineers developed a weapon that could survive extended underwater deployment, exit a sealed launch tube, and travel through water before beginning powered flight. Its two solid-propellant stages eliminated complex pre-launch fueling and established an engineering foundation later developed through the Poseidon and Trident missile families. 4. LGM-30 Minuteman Minuteman changed ballistic-missile operations by combining solid propulsion with highly automated launch control. Its three solid-fuel stages allowed the missile to remain stored inside a silo in a launch-ready condition, avoiding the lengthy fueling procedures associated with earlier liquid-powered systems. The missile also carried a compact digital computer connected to an inertial guidance system. Its development pushed advances in solid-state electronics, miniaturized computing, automated diagnostics, and reliable rocket motors capable of remaining dormant for years before operating. 5. AIM-9 Sidewinder The AIM-9 Sidewinder demonstrated that guided weapons could achieve remarkable effectiveness through mechanical simplicity. Developed at the US Navy’s China Lake facility, it used a passive infrared seeker to follow the heat emitted by an aircraft without requiring continuous guidance from the pilot. One of its most inventive features was the rolleron, a small toothed wheel mounted on each rear fin. Airflow spun the wheels so they acted like gyroscopes, controlling unwanted rolling without complicated powered equipment, while the missile’s modular construction made later upgrades comparatively straightforward. 6. Titan II Titan II was a two-stage American ICBM powered by storable hypergolic propellants that ignited automatically upon contact. Although highly toxic and dangerous to handle, the propellants allowed the missile to remain fueled and launch faster than systems dependent on cryogenic liquids. NASA subsequently converted Titan II into the Gemini Launch Vehicle by reducing vibration and adding equipment designed to protect its astronauts. Between 1964 and 1966, Titan II launched Gemini missions that demonstrated orbital rendezvous, docking, spacewalking, and other procedures required for the Apollo lunar program. 7. BGM-109 Tomahawk Wikimedia Commons The BGM-109 Tomahawk combined the aerodynamic characteristics of an aircraft with the compact packaging of a ship- or submarine-launched missile. After launch, its booster separated, its wings unfolded, and a small turbofan powered it through sustained low-altitude flight. Its Terrain Contour Matching system compared radar measurements of the ground with stored elevation maps, allowing the missile to determine its position without continuous external commands. Later versions added image-matching guidance near the target, helping establish the modern architecture of an autonomous precision cruise missile. Engineering beyond the battlefield These seven missiles represent different answers to the demanding engineering problems created by the Cold War. Together, they advanced lightweight structures, solid and liquid propulsion, digital computers, inertial guidance, infrared seekers and autonomous navigation. Their influence also extended beyond their original military missions and into satellite launches, human spaceflight and unmanned aviation. Built as weapons, they ultimately became important stepping stones in the wider development of modern aerospace engineering.

title: China shows 838-pound laser system for its advanced J-36 fighter
content: China may be developing a high-energy laser weapon for its J-36 fighter, adding a potential new layer of missile defense.An AVIC research institute revealed a fighter laser tracking and aiming system at a Beijing defense expo. The display showed the system beside an image of the large tailless aircraft linked to China’s sixth-generation fighter program.The system weighs less than 838 pounds, according to information shown at the China International Defence Electronics Exhibition. The event ran from September 15 to 17.Several technical figures on the display remained hidden. One power figure appeared as “*00kW,” which could indicate output of at least 100 kilowatts.The poster also obscured the system’s dynamic tracking accuracy. That measurement matters for an airborne laser because even tiny aiming errors can move a beam away from its target.J-36 gets laserChinese military aviation researcher Andreas Rupprecht identified the aircraft shown with the system as the J-36. The three-engine aircraft first appeared over Chengdu in December 2024.Defense analyst Mark Cazalet reached a similar conclusion after examining the display. He said the J-36 likely has enough space, weight capacity and power for a high-energy laser.Large aircraft can provide more room for equipment, cooling hardware and power systems. That could make directed-energy weapons practical on platforms beyond fighters.Bombers, transports and airborne early-warning aircraft could also potentially use similar technology. Such aircraft could use lasers for self-defense against incoming threats.The 838-pound figure still leaves a major question unanswered. It is unclear which components AVIC included within that weight.Cazalet said the figure could encompass the laser source, beam director, and cooling system. The display did not provide a detailed equipment breakdown or electrical power requirement.838-pound systemAn airborne laser faces demanding engineering conditions. Aircraft vibration, turbulence, and rapid maneuvers can constantly disturb the beam.The tracking system must compensate for those movements and maintain an extremely precise aim. That becomes harder as the aircraft and target move at high speed.Cazalet said physical damage would generally require relatively short engagement distances. Lasers could potentially reach farther when attacking or dazzling optical sensors.That makes missile defense one possible mission. A laser could attack an incoming missile or interfere with its seeker before impact.The concept has particular relevance to US airpower. The United States is developing long-range air-to-air weapons including the AIM-174B, AIM-260 and AIM-424.China has investigated airborne laser weapons for years. PLA procurement notices in 2020 sought an airborne laser attack pod and related control software.Chinese researchers have also examined laser tracking from moving aircraft. A 2021 study used transport-aircraft flight data to model the effects of movement and vibration.The US Air Force encountered similar problems with its SHiELD program. The effort explored pod-mounted lasers designed to protect fighters from incoming missiles.SHiELD ended in 2024 without mounting a laser pod on a fighter test aircraft. Program officials had previously identified turbulence, wind and aircraft maneuvers as major challenges.AVIC has also reported testing other directed-energy tracking systems. An AVIC publication described a 2024 trial that maintained a drone lock through clouds, birds and increasing distance.Those tests do not establish that the J-36 carries a laser weapon. No public evidence currently shows the fighter flying with such a system.The Beijing display does, however, offer a rare look at China’s progress toward airborne directed-energy weapons.

title: China turns to older chipmaking technology to make 3nm chips
content: Chinese researchers have developed an early process for building gate-all-around (GAA) transistors at the sub-3nm level using deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography, potentially offering China another route toward advanced chip manufacturing without access to the most advanced EUV machines. The work, reported by Digitimes based on comments from veteran Chinese semiconductor researcher Ye Tianchun, comes as US and Dutch export restrictions continue to limit China’s access to ASML’s most advanced lithography systems. The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) says its researchers have completed early integration of stacked nanosheet-channel GAA CMOS transistors using DUV tools. However, the technology remains at an early development stage and has not demonstrated that it can support commercial-scale production.GAA architecture could help overcome lithography limitsThe research is focused on GAA transistors, an architecture that is replacing FinFET designs as semiconductor manufacturers move toward smaller process nodes. Unlike FinFETs, where the gate surrounds the transistor channel on three sides, GAA designs wrap the gate around the channel, providing greater control over the flow of current, the South China Morning Post reported.The CAS team has reportedly integrated stacked nanosheet-channel GAA CMOS transistors using DUV lithography. Ye Tianchun, a veteran researcher from the Chinese Academy of Sciences’ Institute of Microelectronics, described the work as an early process route for developing sub-3nm devices.However, that does not mean China has demonstrated a production-ready sub-3nm chip. The Chinese researcher emphasized that the work remains at an early stage and that further wafer-level validation will be needed to determine whether the process can eventually be transferred to a manufacturing line.Still, the approach is significant because GAA technology is already being used by leading semiconductor manufacturers. Samsung began mass-producing 3nm chips using GAA, while TSMC moved to the architecture for its 2nm process in 2025.Looking for ways around EUV restrictionsThe research comes against the backdrop of China’s limited access to extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, the technology used by leading chipmakers to manufacture the most advanced semiconductor nodes. ASML’s EUV machines use 13.5nm light to pattern extremely small features on silicon wafers. The systems are among the most sophisticated industrial machines ever built and are critical to modern leading-edge chip production.Export restrictions prevent ASML from selling EUV systems to Chinese customers and as a result, Chinese semiconductor researchers have increasingly explored ways to extract more performance from older DUV equipment, including through new transistor structures, process techniques and materials.CAS has been working on several pieces of this puzzle. In 2025, researchers at the institute developed an all-solid-state DUV laser capable of producing 193nm coherent light, the wavelength used by advanced DUV lithography systems. Furthermore, researchers are also investigating whether different device architectures and process techniques can compensate for limitations in lithography.China’s semiconductor industry is nevertheless pursuing several parallel approaches. Huawei unveiled what it calls the Tau Scaling Law in 2026, a chip-design approach based on “time scaling” that the company says could eventually produce transistor densities comparable to a 1.4nm process by 2031.

title: EV-maker produces battery cells using recycled cathode active material
content: A German company has successfully produced battery cells using recycled cathode active material for the first time. For this, Porsche partnered with companies such as the German recycling company cylib.The company exclusively used battery raw materials recovered from its own high-voltage batteries. The battery cells manufactured within the pilot project are currently undergoing extensive operational testing.Battery cells made entirely from recycled raw materials“With battery cells made entirely from recycled raw materials such as lithium and cobalt, we have achieved an important technological milestone,” said Joachim Scharnagl, Member of the Executive Board for Procurement at Porsche.  “This innovation is a key step in advancing both circular economy principles and raw material resilience, always with the ambition of optimizing progress, quality and resource efficiency.”This achievement continues the pilot project on high-voltage battery recycling launched last year. Within the project, Porsche and its partners recover valuable raw materials from end-of-life high-voltage batteries, process them into new materials, and subsequently use them in new battery cells for Porsche test-vehicles, according to a press release.Battery recycling loopFollowing the recovery and processing stages, the project has now entered its next phase: for the first time, recycled active materials fully replace conventionally used primary raw materials. The recycled cathode active materials include lithium, nickel, cobalt and manganese. “cylib closes the battery recycling loop, from end-of-life batteries to recovered raw materials,” says Dr. Lilian Schwich, Co-CEO and Co-Founder of cylib. “The pilot project with Porsche demonstrates that our approach is feasible in practice: valuable raw materials from Porsche batteries at the end of their first life can potentially flow back into new high-performance batteries for Porsche vehicles.”The company revealed that beyond the recovery of raw materials, Porsche is placing a strong emphasis on the quality of the recycled materials. The next step is to ensure that the recycled raw materials meet Porsche’s high standards for value, quality and performance when used in batteries. Initial tests have already indicated the technical feasibility of the approach. Further results are expected in the second half of 2026. Insights gained from the pilot project will form the basis for a potential future application of these materials in series-production battery cells.The findings from the pilot project are already being incorporated into Porsche’s regular battery disposal process. The partnership between Porsche and cylib enables the recycling of end-of-life high-voltage batteries collected from Porsche Centers across Germany. Since May 2026, the batteries have been recycled using an innovative water-based process. The recovered battery raw materials are tracked through a dedicated material account and will be available to Porsche and selected partner companies for battery cell production beginning in 2028. This approach aims to reduce dependence on global raw material sources. In the future, battery raw materials recycled in Europe could be used in high-voltage batteries for Porsche vehicles.

title: First-ever fully autonomous flight across US covers 3,199 miles
content: Joby Aviation has completed a 3,199-mile autonomous flight across the United States, marking a major test of its aircraft control technology. The company used a modified Cessna Caravan for the journey, which ended near North Carolina’s Outer Banks.An onboard safety pilot remained present throughout the flight but never operated the aircraft’s controls. Joby instead managed the aircraft remotely, with supervision coming from facilities in California and South Carolina.The aircraft handled critical portions of the mission autonomously, including taxiing, takeoff, navigation and landing. Remote operators supervised the flight from distances reaching 2,323 miles.The eastbound trip formed part of Joby’s 2026 Electric Skies tour. The route also gave engineers opportunities to test the system across different airspace and operating conditions.Autonomy faces real airspaceOne of the more significant tests came at Phoenix Deer Valley Airport in Arizona. The busy general aviation airport provided a tougher environment than a controlled demonstration area.Joby also said its aircraft encountered severe weather and thunderstorms during the journey. Its autonomous system rerouted the aircraft without needing previous familiarity with the destination airport.That capability matters because autonomous aircraft must handle changing conditions beyond carefully scripted test flights. Airports, weather patterns, and surrounding traffic can all change during a mission.The aircraft also stopped at Fort Worth Alliance Airport in Texas. There, Joby demonstrated how autonomous aircraft could eventually support freight operations at a major logistics hub.At Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina, the aircraft took part in a demonstration focused on military operations. The company sees potential applications across commercial cargo, emergency response, and defense logistics.Autonomy reaches aviation’s birthplaceAfter reaching North Carolina, the aircraft flew a low pass near Kitty Hawk’s First Flight Monument. The location carries particular significance for aviation history.Orville and Wilbur Wright conducted their first powered flight there in 1903. Joby’s aircraft then landed at Dare County Regional Airport.The North Carolina operation also connected autonomy with regional healthcare logistics. Flights supported NCDOT’s eLIFT-NC initiative, which examines statewide transportation of medical supplies.Joby said autonomous aircraft could eventually serve communities that lack efficient access to larger transportation networks. Smaller airports could provide useful launch points for point-to-point cargo missions.800 hours behind systemJoby’s autonomy program has accumulated more than 400 flights and 800 automated flight hours. Those tests have covered both controlled and uncontrolled airspace.The company acquired its current autonomy division from Xwing in 2024. Joby has since tested the technology during several U.S. military exercises.During an Air Force Agile Flag exercise, the system delivered replacement parts 24 hours faster than conventional logistics, according to Joby. Another exercise demonstrated remote operation between Hawaii and Guam, nearly 4,000 miles apart.JoeBen Bevirt, Joby’s founder and CEO, said autonomy could expand aviation access while reducing risks to pilots. The aircraft now faces another test of the westbound return trip. Joby plans stops in Raleigh, the Washington area, Louisville, Wichita, Oklahoma City, Salt Lake City, and Portland.

title: Historic 1960s US nuclear coolant arrives for Natura's Texas reactor
content: A specialized molten salt coolant has arrived for a new experimental nuclear reactor in Texas. Advanced nuclear company Natura Resources received the shipment from the US Department of Energy on September 18.The material will serve as the coolant for Natura’s MSR-1 demonstration reactor. Workers are currently building the test facility at Abilene Christian University. By taking possession of the compound, the company has resolved a major supply-chain challenge and obtained an essential material needed to operate the facility.Natura’s small modular reactors are designed to deliver clean, reliable baseload power using liquid fuel and low-pressure operating conditions, according to the company.The newly delivered substance is known as FLiBE salt. It originated at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory and traveled through the Idaho National Laboratory before reaching Texas.Historic legacy and operational baselineThis specific salt directly links today’s commercial efforts to the birth of molten salt technology sixty years ago. The Molten Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE) operated from 1965 to 1969, logging more than 13,000 hours demonstrating passive safety, high‑temperature performance, and fuel flexibility, noted the company.The very same FLiBE salt formulation cooled that 1960s experiment. Today, Natura is using that early success as the technical baseline for its modern small modular reactors.“Receiving this salt from the DOE is a handoff between generations of American innovation,” said Jordan Robison, CEO of Natura Resources. “The MSRE showed what molten salt technology could achieve. We’re carrying that legacy forward and turning it into a commercial reality that will deliver reliable energy, clean water, and medical isotopes to the world.”Natura won the rights to the coolant through a competitive Department of Energy solicitation. The bidding process was launched in August 2025 and managed by the Idaho National Laboratory.Commercial proving ground with regulatory progressThe material has precise chemical qualities that are critical for nuclear operations. The FLiBE salt contains 99.99% enriched lithium-7 which minimizes tritium generation in the salt, explained the company.Natura intends to run the MSR-1 reactor as a proving ground. Engineers will gather operational data from the test run to design and license future commercial systems. The company plans to deploy these small, liquid-fueled modular units to supply electricity to industrial sites, remote communities, and critical infrastructure. Beyond reliable energy, the technology is designed to produce medical isotopes and support clean water production.The salt arrival represents the second major milestone for the Abilene project in recent months. In July, the Department of Energy approved a Nuclear Safety Design Agreement for the research facility.That formal agreement laid out the safety rules and design standards for the reactor. It defined the technical framework needed to evaluate the primary safety features, the structural materials, and the operating limits of the liquid-fueled core. Establishing those baseline boundaries was an essential regulatory step, giving federal authorities the legal groundwork to approve construction and authorize system testing.

title: Lockheed Martin rolls out first F-35A stealth fighter jet for Germany
content: Germany has unveiled its first F-35A Lightning II as it prepares to field 35 fifth-generation fighter jets and replace its aging Tornado aircraft in the nuclear weapons mission.Lockheed Martin presented Germany’s first F-35A to the German government at a ceremony at the company’s production facility in Fort Worth, Texas, on September 18. According to a Lockheed Martin news release, the company plans to deliver the first aircraft this year, with full operational capability planned for 2029.Ebbing Air National Guard Base in Arkansas will receive the first eight German aircraft for pilot training beginning this fall. Lockheed Martin plans to send the first F-35s to Germany in late 2027.“This is the beginning of a new era for the German Air Force: the new F-35A fighter jet is the world’s most advanced combat aircraft,” said German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius in the release.“It is characterized by its stealth capabilities, close integration with other platforms, and exceptionally powerful sensor technology,” Pistorius added. “The F-35A can gather vast amounts of data and rapidly synthesize them into a comprehensive operational picture.”Germany plans to acquire 35 F-35As. The program stems from an $8.8 billion deal Berlin signed in 2022 following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, according to Breaking Defense.Germany’s $8.8 billion F-35 programThe agreement followed U.S. approval of a potential F-35 sale to Germany in 2022. The U.S. State Department approved the potential sale of up to 35 F-35As, along with munitions and related equipment, at an estimated cost of $8.4 billion, according to a July 2022 Defense News report published on the F-35 website. The F-35 purchase reversed Germany’s earlier plans to acquire Boeing-built F-18 aircraft.The aircraft are set to take over the nuclear weapons mission from the German Air Force’s aging PA-200 Tornado fleet by 2030, as per Defense News. The Tornados carrying out that mission are based at Tactical Air Wing 33 in Büchel, Germany.“With the F-35, the German Air and Space Force is receiving a modern, proven and highly capable 5th Generation fighter jet,” noted Lt. Gen. Holger Neumann, chief of the German Air and Space Force, in Lockheed Martin’s release.“It will not only bring significant changes in our Air and Space Force but will also influence how we think, command and fight,” stated Neumann. “The F-35 will allow us to become part of the larger international F-35 community.”Germany prepares for F-35 deliveriesLockheed Martin said twenty nations have selected the F-35, including 13 in Europe. More than 1,355 F-35s are currently operational worldwide, and the fleet has surpassed 1 million flight hours while operating from 42 bases.German industry has participated in the F-35 program since 2001. Lockheed Martin said it continues to explore additional opportunities for German companies in manufacturing, sustainment, training, and research and development.With Germany’s first aircraft now unveiled, the next eight F-35As are scheduled to head to Arkansas for pilot training beginning this fall. The first aircraft are due to arrive in Germany in late 2027, ahead of planned full operational capability in 2029.
